News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Sports.title: Inside growing tensions at BBC ‘behind’ Mark Chapman’s deadpan delivery on Match Of The Day
Sports.content:
Next

MATCH of the Day host Mark Chapman’s dull presentation on Saturday night was blamed on growing tensions within BBC Sport.

Fans blasted the deadpan delivery of usually-upbeat Chappers, 53.



One wrote online: “Is Mark Chapman having a massive sulk or did he have a row with someone just before going on air?”

Another added: “Pretty sure the host is usually a lot more cheerful.”



Chapman, said to be dating co-star Kelly Cates, is believed to be unhappy about cuts being introduced by department chief Alex Kay-Jelski.

A TV insider said: “All the whispers are that whether this was deliberate or not his demeanour was all down to being enraged by the changes.

“It is a deeply unhappy ship at the moment.

“Fingers are inevitably pointed at the captain, Jelski.”



The show has seen a dip in viewing figures since long-time host Gary Lineker left last year.

Just over 1.86millon watched on Saturday.

That figure compares to 2.24million the same time in 2025 and 2.44million in 2024.

The BBC and Mark were asked for comment.

Sports.title: Ben White desperate for England recall after impressing Thomas Tuchel during Arsenal win over Everton
Sports.content:
Next

BEN WHITE once looked like he may never play for England again — now he is desperate to get back in the squad.

And the defender boosted his chances on Saturday by setting up Arsenal’s second goal in their 2-0 win over Everton, with Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel watching on at the Emirates Stadium.



White, 29, returned to the England fold in the spring after a four-year absence that began when he left the 2022 World Cup finals in Qatar for personal reasons.

The right-back missed this summer’s tournament and the most recent squad due to injury but is eager to play for his country again.



Asked if he hoped to be in the England squad for next month’s Nations League games with Croatia and Spain, the Gunners star said: “Yeah, definitely.

“It is an amazing feeling playing for England. It’s like nothing else.



“If that does happen, I’ll be absolutely over the moon.” White was booed by some England supporters at Wembley as he made a rollercoaster return to the international stage in March.

The defender scored — but then gave away a penalty which enabled opponents Uruguay to snatch a last-minute 1-1 friendly draw.

It was claimed White’s 2022 exit followed a bust-up with Steve Holland, who was the long-term assistant of then England manager Gareth Southgate.

And White only made himself available for selection again after holding talks with German chief Tuchel when he took charge at the start of 2025.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The road back to an England international recall has not been easy, with White struggling for form and fitness.

And the worst of a series of injuries came in May, just two months after Tuchel had decided to pick White for the first time.

He damaged a knee during a 1-0 win at West Ham, which forced him to miss the Champions League final with Paris Saint—Germain and the World Cup finals.

White said: “It was tough. As soon as I did it, I knew. I have had little things like that before and I kind of digested it walking around the pitch.

“It was that quick, really. I knew that was going to be me for the season — and I had a little cry on the way round.



“That was it, once I got in the dressing room, I was focused on trying to recover and get back.

“I literally trained every day over the summer. I didn’t really have a break — that was my aim.”

The work over the break has paid off for White.

And he continued his good start to the season on Saturday — by helping Arsenal move level on 21 points with Premier League leaders Manchester City with this victory over David Moyes’ Merseysiders.

Summer signing Ezri Konsa put the Gunners ahead after seven minutes, when the former Aston Villa centre-back bundled the ball home from a corner.



The scruffy strike was in contrast to the slick move that White helped create for Arsenal’s second goal on 68 minutes.

The right-back’s dinked cross found Gabriel unmarked at the back post. White now has three assists this season, starting in seven of the Gunners’ eight Prem games.

Only Greek winger Christos Tzolis and Declan Rice can better that tally for Arsenal — and it was the ideal way for White to mark his 200th appearance for the club.



White said: “It’s really creeped up, creeped up slowly. It’s amazing to play 200 games for this club.

“I wouldn’t want to be anywhere else. I had four years on the bounce at different teams.

“So to come here and be here this long, and play that many games, is a really nice feeling.”

White may be on the bench tomorrow when Arsenal head to Fleetwood in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta also has Jurrien Timber as back-up at right-back.



White believes he and the Dutchman are benefiting from being fit at the same time.

He said: “It’s always been — you have to play, you have to play. Now, it’s a different moment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We can actually get some rest. I am sure you will see the best versions of each of us.

“It’s really nice to share the load with me and JT.”

Sports.title: Man Utd need to sack Michael Carrick after Bournemouth but buck can’t stop with him – Jason Wilcox must go as well
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED supporters know the manager has to go but the buck cannot stop with Michael Carrick.

United matchgoers have booed the manager before. On Sunday, they turned on the players as soon as Carrick disappeared down the tunnel.



Diogo Dalot had dozily lingered longer on the pitch than teammates, so was the last player left on it. The boos grew louder for a United player who has outstayed his welcome.

United have lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth three times within three years under three different managers. That is ample evidence that Carrick cannot be the only one who goes.



There was gallows humour on the Stretford End as they told Sir Jim Ratcliffe to shove his new stadium up his backside.

There were sinister songs about kissing Ratcliffe and the Glazers on a bonfire. Ousting the Glazers is wishful thinking but jettisoning director of football Jason Wilcox is not just doable but advisable.

Ratcliffe said last year he would not have “tolerated” Ed Woodward. Wilcox has mimicked Woodward by promoting a former player from interim to permanent head coach only for United to spiral.

It has been sooner and more spectacular than under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Carrick is cut from the same cloth as his colleague and friend, who was also in the running to replace Ruben Amorim in January.



That Wilcox considered Solskjaer was a red flag. Wilcox’s treatment of Amorim in their infamous Wolves debrief last season convinced the Portuguese to engineer his own sacking.

Wilcox does not control the purse strings but he has made dire decisions, dodges questions and was underqualified for the DoF role he was promoted to in June 2025.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Man Utd ratings vs Bournemouth MANCHESTER United hit a new low for the season, if that's possible, with the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Michael Carrick stuck Bruno Fernandes on the bench – supposedly for ‘football reasons only’ – and kept him there for the whole game. So how did those who did play get on – and were there any shining lights on another stormy afternoon in Manchester? Find out how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated United’s flops right here.

His past with Leeds United and Manchester City makes him an easy target. An image of Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada was captioned “Agent Leeds and Agent Sham,” the latter a reference to Berrada’s 14 years at City.

In this era where managers or coaches answer to sporting directors, it can’t be just Carrick’s head who rolls. Wilcox is at United on the strength of his time as Berrada’s colleague at City. Jobs for the boys.

Carrick went past the point of no return last month. United did not have the courage to dismiss him during the elongated international break.



The heat was turned up on City amid their guilty verdict, so those upstairs at United crossed their fingers and covered their own backsides.

They have since had them spanked by Atletico Madrid, Como and Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Barcelona 1 Real Madrid 2: Mbappe rains on Lamine Yamal’s parade to claim El Clasico win after Bellingham brilliance
Sports.content:
Next

KYLIAN MBAPPE will not win the Ballon d’Or – but he heads to London having firmly wiped the smile from Lamine Yamal’s face.

Mbappe’s double, a comical opener and a shock late winner, ended Barcelona’s perfect LaLiga start.



This is why Jose Mourinho was brought back.

Ahead of the Ballon d’Or showdown between Yamal and Harry Kane tonight, Barca’s teenage terror was, in prime Mourinho fashion, booted to the Clasico fringes by Real.



Mbappe has touted himself for football’s top individual prize, but surely cannot top either Kane or his LaLiga rival tomorrow night.

But in cutting the gap to the top a from six to three points, he and Real remain in the title hunt, Raphinha’s goal irrelevant and Barca hearts broken.

Mourinho had said there was to be no specific plan to stop Barcelona’s young phenom.

He may not have altered his tactics, but Marc Cucurella had certainly been given clear guidance: make his life hell.

Whether he was walloping his Spain teammate into the air, trying to relieve him of his shirt or just snapping at his heels the frizzy-haired full-back was sticking to his task with gusto and causing clear frustration.

LaLiga’s two grandest clubs have been freescoring this season but both were struggling to create clear openings.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Raphinha fired high and then, after a fine back-heel layoff from Anthony Gordon, sent another wide.

Mbappe attempted some acrobatics but was closer to the building site of a top-tier than Joan Garcia’s goal.

Perhaps then it was inevitable that, with the eyes of the world on the Nou Camp, the opener would be more by accident than design.

Taking a break from shamelessly kicking lumps out of Yamal, Cucurella fed Yan Diomande down the left.



The winger drove forward and guided a low cross with the outside of his boot, which is where the quality ended and the slapstick took over.

Gerard Martin arrived on the scene to clear, but thumped the ball straight into Mbappe, who was flinching instead of finishing but still ended up celebrating as it cannoned in off of his knee.

Yamal had the chance to hit back almost immediately, fed on the edge of the six-yard box by Fermin Lopez but duffed his finish entirely.



A superb Bellingham run five minutes after the restart opened the door for Real to double their lead.

Two-on-one with Mbappe all the Englishman had to do was square the ball, but he opted to go alone and made a mess of it.

There was much better to come, however.



After Raphinha’s leveller looked to have this Clasico on course for a point-a-piece, Bellingham, belatedly, rose to the moment.

Some stunning skill, sidestepping one Barca shirt and rolling another, sent Eduardo Camavinga haring down the right.

The French sub squared for his compatriot to prod home and seal a first Real Madrid win here in three years.

Mourinho dropped to his knees and pumped his fist as bottles rained down on his players who celebrated in front of the Barca fans.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A bit more of that and this time next year, the Ballon d’Or and a bit more may be in the hands of Mbappe.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker and Harry Kane’s old bosses on why striker should be England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE is the bookies’ favourite to win the Ballon d’Or tonight — as it comes to London for the first time.

The 70th anniversary ceremony is being held at the London Palladium Theatre, in tribute to its first winner, England great Stanley Matthews.



Three Lions captain Kane bagged an astonishing 73 GOALS for club and country last season — only ­bettered by Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2011-12.

Kane, a league winner with Bayern Munich, faces fierce competition from the likes of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.



Gary Lineker and Kane’s former bosses Harry Redknapp and Tim Sherwood told SunSport’s Jack Rosser and Isabelle Barker why Kane should be the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

GARY LINEKER

I’ve got a feeling it will be Harry. What he’s done has been amazing.



There are a lot of really, really good players in the world at the moment.

The Ballon d’Or is the Ballon d’Or. It’s way more important than it was in my day. I should have won it. I was robbed in 1986!

It’s between Harry and Lamine Yamal, if you look at the bookmakers — and you could make a case for both, obviously.

Kylian Mbappe and Yamal have made cases for themselves, as has Harry in a way — he’s done all the interviews.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

I’ve never seen him appear so much all over the place. And that’s great.

That’s how it is nowadays.

So you put yourself out there without quite saying it to everybody, classically British in his modesty, I suppose.

But he’s absolutely deserving if he wins it. And I hope he does, it would be great to see an English player win it.



He’s also a really good bloke, as well as a magnificent all-round centre-forward.

And to score that many goals this season, he totally merits it.

If you’re talking about the best footballer, it’s hard to look past Yamal. But I’d actually say this year’s Lionel Messi is still the world’s best player.

He was easily the best player at the World Cup. He really was. Spain won it, so therefore, Rodri won it. And he deserved it, too.



But Messi was unbelievable. He’s won enough. I think it’ll come down to Harry, I’ve got a feeling it’ll be him.

There are certain things that those voting have to weigh up about the success of your season.

But Harry won a double for Bayern Munich and hit a multitude of goals.

He won the European Golden Boot. He scored six goals at the World Cup.



Didn’t quite manage it at the end.

Will not winning a World Cup or Champions League count against him in some people’s eyes?

Because Spain won the World Cup and the World Cup is generally the big thing of the year.

Someone like Mbappe would have been running him close.



But Real Madrid didn’t win anything either — and France didn’t quite make it.

Kane was also brilliant at the World Cup. So you’re in among the game’s absolute elite.

I think it’s 50-50 between Harry and Yamal, ultimately — and it’s in London!

HARRY REDKNAPP

I have a funny story about Harry Kane, who I worked with when I was Tottenham manager.



I loaned him out when he was 17 to Barry Hearn, who was the chairman of Leyton Orient.

Hearn rang me and said ‘We’re going to get relegated. Have you got any players at Tottenham you could loan me?’

So I said, ‘Yeah, I’ve got three kids here you can have, take them, it will do them the world of good to go and play’.

So I loaned him three players, and I was at a function the other week where he spoke.



He said, ‘Harry loaned me three players — and at the end of the season we stayed up’.

Hearn recalled saying at the time ‘Andros Townsend, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, which he did, he played for England.

‘Stephen Caulker, he could go back and play for Tottenham’, he did — and he played for England, too.

He said, ‘Kane, no, he’ll never be good enough to play for Tottenham’, but he said at the function, ‘Shows you what I knew about football!’



To be fair, I don’t think any of us saw him going on to become the best centre-forward in the world, which he is.

And he should now win the Ballon d’Or.

He was a boy, like Frank Lampard, who would practise after training for an hour, every day, with Jermain Defoe, shooting, finishing, practising, wanting to be a success.

“I gave him his senior debut at Spurs in a Europa League qualifier in 2011 against Hearts.



Last 10 Ballon d'Or winners 2025 – Ousmane Dembele

2024 – Rodri

2023 – Lionel Messi

2022 – Karim Benzema

2021 – Lionel Messi

“Our progression to the group stage was all but secure following a 5-0 victory in the first leg in Edinburgh.

“We got a penalty, and he’s only a kid, and he grabbed the ball and he wanted to take it, but he actually missed it!

“That shows what he was like — you had all those fantastic players in that team — but he didn’t care.

“He has remained humble, and he’s got time for everybody. He’s a fantastic human being. Really genuine.”

TIM SHERWOOD

Didn’t hesitate to give Harry Kane his first ­Premier League start.



Emmanuel Adebayor was a big player on big money — who we had signed from Manchester City.

Roberto Soldado, the top goalscorer in Spain, had come to Tottenham for a record fee.

He had a lot of traffic in his way. We know how many goals Jermain Defoe scored in the Prem.



But I judged everyone on a level playing field.

I watched Harry every day in training and decided the time was right to give him the opportunity.

I knew he wouldn’t be fazed by it.

He almost looked at me when I told him he was going to play against ­Sunderland on a Monday as if to say, ‘about time!’

I knew there wasn’t any danger of him going home and not ­sleeping properly.



He backed his ability and needed someone to back him too. I gave him that little bit of love he needed.

He took his opportunity with both hands.

A lot of people talk to me about Harry Kane’s failed loans. I don’t see any of them as failures.

They were better development pathways than playing with the Under-21s.



I always felt we needed him to go out and play competitive football.

It was the environment of meaning something.

The boys he played with at Orient needed to pay their mortgages.

He’s about the team before himself. That’s why everyone loves him.

If I asked him, he would pick winning the Champions League this season with Bayern Munich over the Ballon d’Or.



He’s just a model ­professional and that is why Alan Shearer is ­quaking in his boots.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

I think he will eventually look for a team that might win trophies in England.

He wants to come back to beat that Shearer’s Prem goalscoring record.

Because of his professionalism and durability, I think he would be able to.

Sports.title: Sean Dyche ‘lined up for Premier League return’ after eight months out as manager on brink of being sacked
Sports.content:
Next

SEAN DYCHE could be handed a surprise Premier League lifeline as Crystal Palace consider making a change in the dugout.

The 55-year-old has been without a club since being axed by Nottingham Forest in February but is now being tipped to make a comeback in South London.



According to The Telegraph, Dyche is high on Palace’s list of potential replacements for Pierre Sage, who is facing an uncertain future following another miserable result.

The Eagles were booed off by their own fans after Newcastle cruised to a 2-0 victory at Selhurst Park.



Will Osula broke the deadlock just two minutes after the restart before Harvey Barnes doubled the visitors’ lead.

It was another afternoon to forget for Sage, whose side were battered 5-0 by bitter rivals Brighton the previous weekend.



And the Frenchman’s troubles are mounting, with Palace sitting just one point above the drop zone after winning only two of their opening eight league games.

The Eagles have also shipped a staggering 19 goals in those matches, giving them the worst defensive record in the division.

Sage, 47, only arrived in the summer to replace Oliver Glasner, who had guided Palace to FA Cup and Europa Conference League glory.

Dyche also faces competition from former Tottenham and Brentford boss Thomas Frank, while ex-Ipswich boss Kieran McKenna could also contend for the Eagles job.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Dyche, meanwhile, could offer some much-needed experience after spending almost a decade at Burnley, where he earned two promotions and even secured European football on a shoestring budget.

He also helped Everton beat the drop before his brief spell at Forest ended after just 114 days.

But Sage remains in charge for now and faces a huge test against Tottenham next weekend, with Liverpool also on the horizon before the international break.

Sports.title: Incredible moment goalkeeper steps up and scores late free-kick as subs pour onto pitch to celebrate
Sports.content:
Next

A RUSSIAN goalkeeper scored a worldie free-kick in the dying minutes of normal time to give his team an incredible lead.

Ural’s Aleksandr Selikhov stepped up to the mark in his yellow jersey with a whole 23.3 metres in the way between him and the Chelyabinsk goalposts.



In the 87th minute, the 32-year-old plucked up the courage to boot it like a dart to the bullseye with an almighty kick.

The Chelyabinsk goalkeeper never had a chance, needing to stretch all the way to the near post and still missing it.



He tumbled to the ground as one of Selikhov’s team-mates booted the ball into the back of the Chelyabinsk net for good measure.

Celebrations erupted from the visiting fans with a flurry of orange players sprinting towards the electric party.

While some of Ural’s stars tried their best to collect the shotstopper for a hug, he was unstoppable in making it to the fans.

Selikhov jumped one barrier and then another, before lifting two arms in the air in a roar of elation.



The team’s classic orange and green colours were all over the place as fans swung their scarfs and waved their flags.

Even the stewards looked to be clapping the stunning moment – along with the substitutes.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But the game did not end there.

Four minutes into injury time, Brazilian centre-back Italo netted again leaving the blockbuster clash at 3-1.

The three points sent Ural into the top four of the Russian First League but they still trail leaders Nizhny Novgorod by a huge 12 points.



Meanwhile, Chelyabinsk sink firmly into the middle of the table in 12th.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League ace Jermaine Pennant left needing 50 stitches after dog mauls him – before own pet fights off attacker
Sports.content:
Next

EX-Premier League star Jermaine Pennant needed more than 50 stitches after a dog repeatedly sank its teeth into his leg.

The talkSport pundit, 43, was saved by his own dog who leapt to his defence.



He had been walking American Akita King when it was confronted by a German Shepherd.

Ex-Arsenal and Liverpool star Jermaine told The Sun: “It was really scary. The other dog had a go at King, so I stepped in to protect him.



“The next thing I know, it was attacking me.

“I was on the floor and it was on my leg for at least five seconds.

“I felt this huge pressure. Imagine the force of a dog bite.

“King jumped in to protect me.



“The two dogs were really going at it, and then King stood by my side until help arrived.

“He saved my life. If King had been a smaller dog, there would have been no chance.”

Jermaine said both dogs were off the lead in North London.

His girlfriend of two years, Mimmi Montgomery, got him an Uber to A&E where he was treated for four bite wounds on his right leg.

He spent Friday night in hospital and has been told he might need plastic surgery on one large wound.



Ex-winger Jermaine, who retired in 2018, declined to report the matter to police.

He added: “It’s just one of those things.

“I’m fine, the dog’s fine. It’s all good.”



Police-recorded offences of out-of-control dog attacks causing injury have risen from 16,040 in 2020 to 29,400 last year, up 83 per cent.

The true figure will be higher as they exclude unreported incidents.

Sports.title: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit
Sports.content:
Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.

The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen.

Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw.

Schindler was broken in the next but offered a four-leg burst - including finishes of 116 and 127 - to cut the deficit to 9-7 and threaten a famous comeback, but the next three legs went with throw as Smith closed out victory and the £150,000 first prize.

Victory sees Smith join Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as the only players to win multiple European Championship titles, with his latest success following his World Series of Darts title in September and lifting him to world No 6.

Machineseeker European Championship results Quarter-Finals: Ross Smith 10-6 Luke Woodhouse, Gerwyn Price 10-3 Stephen Bunting, Martin Schindler 10-1 Jonny Clayton, Krzysztof Ratajski 10-6 Luke Littler Semi-Finals: Ross Smith 11-7 Gerwyn Price, Martin Schindler 11-6 Krzysztof Ratajski Final: Ross Smith 11-8 Martin Schindler

"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there going to that end with Martin - he wouldn't let up, would he!" Smith said. "Full credit to him. To have this trophy in my hands, to win another major - I'm absolutely over the moon and drained, but I'm buzzing!"

Luke Littler was the pre-tournament favourite to claim the only missing ranked major from his glittering CV, only for the world No 1 to suffer a shock quarter-final exit to Krzysztof Ratajaski.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler failed to win a maiden European Championship as he suffered a surprise defeat at the hands of Krzysztof Ratajski (Credit: ITV)

How Smith secured Dortmund title

Schindler thrashed Jonny Clayton 10-1 and despatched Ratajaski - who eliminated Littler 11-6 in the previous round - to reach his maiden ranked TV final, with the German missing chances to grab the early lead against Smith.

He wasted multiple opportunities to break in the third leg but responded with a 14-dart hold in the next, levelling the match, before Smith quickly pulled away.

Image: Smith came into the event as No 1 seed after a strong season on the PDC European Tour

Smith took out an 86 finish to break and kept the German crowd quiet by sweeping all five legs in the next mini session, with Schindler only allowed back in when his opponent squandered five darts at double to open a seven-leg lead.

The pair traded breaks of throw before Schindler followed a 15-dart hold by firing successive ton-plus checkouts, with Smith stuttering over the closing legs before wrapping up victory with his fifth match dart.

Sports.title: 'The pace was rubbish' - Russell in blunt admission after Austin struggle
Sports.content:
George Russell admitted his pace in the United States Grand Prix was "rubbish", with the Mercedes driver at a loss to why he trailed race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli by such a large margin,

Russell finished 54 seconds behind the sister Mercedes in the 56-lap race in an eighth place that only just kept him in mathematical championship contention heading to next week's race in Mexico, where Antonelli is set to clinch the crown.

Russell had held his grid position of sixth through the race's first stint but dropped to eighth after serving a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop for an incident with Oscar Piastri in the opening lap, when he was judged to have gained an advantage by running off track in battle with the McLaren.

Russell subsequently spent the final 26 laps on the similarly one-stopping Piastri's tail but was unable to find a way back past the Australian driver.

Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The pace was rubbish. That's the long and short of it.

"The five-second [penalty] didn't help things and probably cost me two or three positions but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty.

Russell made no excuse for his lack of competitiveness and said he had no immediate answer for why his Austin weekend was such a struggle.

"Just not been quick enough," he added.

"I need to try and understand why that is. It's strange when you're so far off. Hopefully there are some answers somewhere but at the moment I don't have them."

What went wrong for Russell?

Antonelli's win was his ninth of the year and represented what Toto Wolff, Mercedes' team principal, believes was "the best race that he's delivered so far".

It was the first win for Mercedes upgraded car, which has taken time for the world championship leaders to get the best out out of since the aerodynamic revisions debut at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix.

The team have said, however, that the changes have narrowed the car's optimum set-up window.

On Russell's weekend, Wolff said: "George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult.

"In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3, it didn't work. He said, 'that goes on me'.

"And today in the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair why he didn't get past. It's the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment. But I'm going to see him now."

'He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance'

Analysis from Sky Sports F1's Jenson Button:

"George has had a lot of tough races but also some great races and that's the thing that's really difficult to understand - how he's able to get the maximum out of that car on some tracks but not at others.

"Austin was difficult as he started so far down. He was in the pack and when you're in the pack, sometimes it's difficult to move forward. You're in the dirty air. You try to do something different with strategy but then you get a five-second penalty which puts you back further.

"I don't believe his pace is that far off. He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance."

Sports.title: Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for world title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli moved to the brink of becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion with a superb drive to victory in the United States Grand Prix.

Antonelli had an outside chance of clinching the 2026 title as early as Sunday's Austin race provided he won, Lewis Hamilton finished outside the top four and George Russell was ninth or lower.

And while he held up his side of the bargain by brilliantly claiming a ninth win of the season on a one-stop strategy to his nearest rivals' two, Hamilton took fourth and Russell eighth to stay in mathematical contention.

But Antonelli has moved 123 points clear of Russell, and 124 points clear of Hamilton, with just a maximum of 125 left to play for this season to make a coronation at next Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix all but inevitable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Antonelli, who only turned 20 in August and is in his second season of F1, will definitely clinch the title with four rounds to spare in Mexico if he finishes anywhere in the top nine.

"We are very close," said the Italian, who will also be assured of the title at the next round if neither Russell nor Hamilton win the race.

"We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Antonelli won at the Circuit of The Americas by 13 seconds with Charles Leclerc finishing a fine second for Ferrari after winning out against Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the battle of the two-stop strategies. Leclerc overtook Verstappen at Turn 12 after an entertaining battle with seven laps to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Hamilton was fourth, crossing the line just one second behind Verstappen after also fast-catching the Red Bull late on, with Lando Norris fifth on a one-stop strategy ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

While Antonelli was peerless up front, team-mate Russell's difficult Austin weekend, and indeed season, was summed up by his disappointing eighth-place finish.

Russell, who had started sixth, dropped behind the McLarens after having to serve a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop after being judged to have gained an advantage by going off track in battle with Oscar Piastri on the first lap.

United States GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Lando Norris, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) George Russell, Mercedes



9) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



10) Pierre Gasly, Alpine

The elongated pit stop dropped Russell behind Piastri, whom he was then unable to pass despite following closely for almost half the race. He described his race pace as "rubbish".

Liam Lawson continued his relentless points-scoring form with ninth for Racing Bulls, while Pierre Gasly was 10th for Alpine.

Faultless Antonelli returns to winning ways - and verge of history - in style

Despite his inexperience in just his second year of F1 and the fast-looming spectre of achieving his lifelong dream of becoming world champion, Antonelli had already barely put a foot wrong across the title run-in during a period when Mercedes have rarely had the fastest car.

The Italian had not won a race since his fortuitous triumph at the Spanish Grand Prix in mid-September and Mercedes' most recent upgrade, first brought to the car two races ago in Malaysia, had initially not delivered the results the team had expected.

But any suggestion that the season's world championship-leading team and driver might have to take a defensive approach to the final rounds of this season to get over the title-winning line was firmly put to bed in Austin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win

Antonelli's pole position - his first in eight races since the Belgian Grand Prix since July - had been perhaps his most unexpected of the season and had led Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to play down the Italian's prospects of victory.

On Sunday, the Italian was alone among the top five on the grid to opt for the medium tyres for the race start and yet, despite his rivals behind having the grippier softs for the crucial uphill run to COTA's wide first corner, Antonelli had a dream getaway and easily converted his starting advantage into a lap-one lead.

It was instead second-placed Verstappen who came under pressure from behind, the Dutchman initially overtaken by Leclerc through the Esses before getting back ahead of the Ferrari into Turn 13 later round the opening lap.

But Antonelli had soon opened an early lead of four seconds and, struggling to keep up, Red Bull pitted Verstappen surprisingly early on lap 13. He took on a second set of soft tyres, locking him into a two-stop race given the requirement to run two different tyre compounds.

Ferrari soon followed suit with their drivers but Mercedes stuck to their guns on a projected one-stopper and did not pit Antonelli until the end of lap 24. When they did they switched him onto the more durable hard compound, ensuring he could go to the end of the race without stopping again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff says that Kimi Antonelli's performance at the United States Grand Prix was 'exceptional'

Antonelli rejoined in fourth place but was back in the lead by lap 32 by passing the long-running Leclerc.

Verstappen had by then pitted for a second time having run into a more problematic second stint on softs. And while the fresher tyres of the Red Bull and Ferrari into the closing laps meant Antonelli's lead over both came down, neither had sufficient speed to truly cause Mercedes alarm.

"It was the result we needed," said Antonelli. "The whole team deserve it so much.

"All this time putting so much work into bringing this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant.

"It was also perfect execution from strategy to call the one-stop. Really happy we made it stick. Today was a great team effort."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen reflects on the United States GP, in which he finished third

Verstappen had looked the most likely to challenge Antonelli on his two-stopper but, in the end, it was Leclerc who got closest.

Ferrari's soft-medium-medium tyre strategy allowed the Monegasque to display impressive turn of speed from his first stop onwards, eventually fighting back from his final stop to pass the long-running Norris and then Verstappen during his final stint.

"It was quite a good race," said Leclerc. "Unfortunately we came short of the victory which was our target.

"At the end of the day, a positive race. We had good pace. The first stint was more difficult."

Sports.title: Mbappe's late strike earns Mourinho and Real Clasico glory at Barca
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe's double took Real Madrid to a famous 2-1 Clasico win, which had Jose Mourinho sliding on his knees in celebration in Barcelona.

It was the 87th minute when Mbappe tucked in from Eduardo Camavinga's cutback following some sublime skill from Jude Bellingham. The celebrations from Real Madrid were wild, with their head coach unable to contain himself, his staff on the pitch, and his players clashing with Barcelona fans.

Real had been on the defensive after Raphinha's snapshot had levelled a pulsating clash, with Lamine Yamal narrowly clipping wide as LaLiga's defending champions pushed for a winner. Instead Real have closed to within three points of their great rivals. Atletico are second just two off Barca now.

Image: Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe celebrates after scoring against Barcelona

It's been a bad week for Hansi Flick's side, whose 11-game winning streak at the start of this season was halted with defeat in the Champions League at Paris St-Germain. This loss will sting far more - it's Real's first win in Barcelona in three years.

Mbappe's opener had been fortuitous, Gerard Martin slamming a clearance in off him. But Real's move to get to that point had been excellent and throughout the contest they showed they were willing to go toe-to-toe with their more favoured hosts.

There was controversy before Raphinha's equaliser, with Joao Cancelo not punished for putting his studs into Yan Diomande's calf. But Mourinho and Real Madrid will leave Spotify Camp Nou celebrating.

Key moments at Spotify Camp Nou...

Sports.title: City's perfect start ended in derby draw with Man Utd
Sports.content:
A late equaliser from Elisabeth Terland earned Manchester United a well-earned 1-1 draw that ended Manchester City's perfect start to the WSL campaign.

City looked set for victory as Khadija Shaw finally broke the deadlock with a little over 20 minutes to go. However, it was Shaw who inadvertently set up Terland for the equaliser in the last minute of normal time.

Both teams came into the contest in good spirits. City had made a perfect start in their opening six WSL games, while United had been starting to click under Eva Olid.

It was the hosts who appeared more likely to find the opener following a tense first half. They were on top after the break, with Jess Park ratting the crossbar on the hour mark as they looked to make their dominance count.

Shaw had been having an uncharacteristically quiet evening, being heckled by home fans and marked out of the game by Maya Le Tissier in the first 45. She targeted Dominique Janssen when the game resumed and the switch paid off.

The PFA Player of the Year backed into the Dutch defender before turning and firing through her legs to find the bottom corner and give City the lead against the run of play on her 100th WSL appearance.

It was a bitter blow for the Red Devils, whose hard work looked set to be unrewarded. That was until Shaw's tame clearance from a deep Le Tissier cross fell to the feet of Terland, who dispatched perfectly to snatch a share of the spoils.

The result means that City only go level on points with Chelsea at the top, but fall behind Sonia Bompastor's side on goal difference following their come-from-behind win against Crystal Palace.

Jeglertz: Disappointed to concede so late

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz speaking with Sky Sports:

"You remember the last five minutes where you concede a goal and you feel disappointed.

"Overall, it's a fantastic football game. An intense game, a lot of emotions during the whole game. United is giving us a big fight. You can't say anything about the result but of course you are disappointing when you concede late and had a big chance before that.

"I'm so happy for her [Bunny Shaw]. A tough game for her. A lot of hits and knocks and then she's the one scoring for us. She has done it so many times. At the same time, we always want to win games."

Terland: We had the chances to win

Manchester United striker Elisabeth Terland speaking with Sky Sports:

"I think with the way the game evolves we should be happy with a point. I'm really happy with the performance today. We could've come away with a win. We will take the point at the end of the day.

"We had the chances today to get the goals. Even in the first half, we should be up. There's a lot to take from this game and this is the standard going forward.

"It's a fun way to play football. If we can play like this every week, it is enjoyable. We are competing against a top team and should probably win. That just speaks for itself."

Sports.title: Rodgers backs 16-game 'NFL International week' after Paris history
Sports.content:
Aaron Rodgers endorsed the introduction of an international week to the NFL season as he led the Pittsburgh Steelers to victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris on Sunday.

Rodgers and the Steelers made history last year when they beat the Minnesota Vikings in the NFL's Dublin debut at Croke Park, before travelling overseas again this week to deliver another milestone moment for the league in the French capital.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell revealed on Friday that the league has plans to play a game in Tokyo, Japan in either 2027 or 2028, with wider ambitions of reaching 16 international games per season.

"I really look forward to that. We know that soccer worldwide probably has the most amount of fans. If you watch the World Cup at all, you know how fanatical the people for their country teams are. But the NFL is still shown in a number of countries, the Super Bowl is shown in over 100 countries; the reach of the league is fantastic," said Rodgers.

"I think I always wanted to be a part of it. I remember the 2011 CBA, there was talk about expanding the amount of international games, didn't really a whole lot until the second CBA.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player NFL commissioner Roger Goodell explains how the league is following Formula 1's model with international games, but adds that they may explore creating an international franchise or division.

"And there was talk about doing an international week, where you had games in 16 different places and you just added an extra bye week. I think it would have been phenomenal for the game.

"Now that the owners want to push for 17 games for the extra revenue and because they care so much about player safety. But it would have been nice."

Sunday's game in Paris featured as part of a record nine international games being played during the 2026 campaign, joining Melbourne and Rio de Janeiro as the league's newest host territories.

The NFL will now head to Madrid, Munich and Mexico City over the next month amid what has taken shape as a Formula 1-style format.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron Rodgers passed Peyton Manning for the third-most touchdown passes in NFL history

"You could do obviously Canada, you could do Mexico," Rodgers continued. "There's been games in Brazil. You could probably open up another country in South America. Obviously there's a lot of opportunities in Europe, Ireland is fantastic, France, Spain, Germany, multiple games in England. And then who knows?

"There's Dubai, those areas really got into the sporting world in a number of ways, you got boxing and UFC, so I think there's great opportunities for expansion in those.

"It'd be awesome to see them have an international week because I think it's great for the game and the expansion of the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodgers gives his reaction after his side beat the New Orleans Saints

The Steelers arrived late into Paris this week as they landed on Friday morning before heading straight into media availability at their hotel. Rodgers said at the time he wished the team had flown in at the beginning of the week as the Saints had.

Arrival time has become a prominent talking point surrounding the NFL's international games, the Rams landing in Melbourne just a day before their defeat to the San Francisco 49ers. It came a year after Sean McVay's side dominated the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium having flown in on the eve of the game, a strategy that did not work in Australia.

"I wish there was a mandate from the league and they would have to open up their pocketbooks, too, which, you know, maybe a little tight on money and stuff," said Rodgers.

"But I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday to really enjoy the culture and the place you're going. And you can do events in those cities and outreach stuff and community work. But they won't because they're a little tight."
