Sports.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as head coach after he oversaw another torrid defeat, against Bournemouth at Old ­Trafford on Sunday, that left his job in the balance.

Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post. “I totally understand the situation,” Carrick said of his job prospects. “I’m not expecting anything in ­particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal and I love this place.”

But the United executive are actively ­considering his dismissal, the ­Guardian understands, with the expectation at the club being that Carrick will be sacked.

Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential ­targets.

Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given that Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher ­Vivell, United’s head of ­recruitment, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim ­Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick, who left Bruno Fernandes out of his starting lineup – insisting before kick-off that he did so for football reasons and not because of the captain’s criticism of his ­tactics after the midweek ­Champions League defeat at Como – said: “I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, ­whatever decision is made on anything really. So that’s kind of it. I’m not expecting anything either way.

“It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won’t change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see.”

United endured a sixth defeat in 12 games in all competitions after Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and ­Evanilson scored for Marco Rose’s side. They have won only once in the league this season and sit in 16th. Their last win was on 10 September, against Sabah in the Champions League.

The club cannot announce a sacking until they inform the New York Stock Exchange, which is closed at weekends. When Ruben Amorim was sacked in January, the decision was taken on the Sunday night after the coach’s explosive press conference following a draw at Leeds, but was not announced until the next day.

Carrick made a point of ­applauding the home supporters at the end of the match, pumping his hand to his chest as he walked past a supportive Stretford End. As soon as he disappeared down the tunnel, boos met Fernandes, who was following the manager, alongside other United players.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It wasn’t a farewell from me,” ­Carrick said. “I’m feeling it for my players, they’re going through a tough spell. Some of it we can help, some of it the situation unravels and the boys are feeling it at the moment. Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way.

“To have that connection with the supporters, it’s mixed emotions, it’ll take a bit of time to digest but I certainly appreciate their support. The situation is where we are and we haven’t had results or performances that have been good enough.”

On his decision to omit Fernandes, who was an unused substitute, ­Carrick said: “There’s always times when you’re trying to make decisions that are to change the course of play and made a difference, but those are the decisions we made today.”

Harry Maguire, United’s captain in Fernandes’ absence, insisted that the squad were “fully behind” ­Carrick. He said: “Coming into the team last season he turned things around and got Champions League football this season.

As individuals, we’re not ­playing well enough. We have to look at ­ourselves and find something within ourselves to bring more to the team. That’s every player that I’m talking about. When things aren’t going your way you have to do the basics well.”

Sports.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
Sports.content:
Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile.

There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.

Fabian Hürzeler praised the Brighton performance and the self-belief necessary to take the game to Liverpool when trailing to two quickfire goals. But he exaggerated the threat they displayed. Yasin Ayari missed a glorious chance to open the scoring and also struck a post, but Alisson was troubled more by his own distribution after Liverpool’s second goal than by anything the visitors engineered.

“I think everyone in the stadium saw there was one team who really tried to create and tried to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players,” claimed the Brighton head coach, prompting a mass raising of eyebrows in the post-match press conference. “The difference was that they scored and we didn’t. They blocked a lot of shots and defended the box well. We didn’t have that efficiency. We couldn’t keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes and lost some important personal duels but overall I saw a team with a lot of good things. It is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. Liverpool’s attacking force devastated the visitors’ hopes of a fifth straight win and clean sheet in succession in the Premier League. The hosts were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat the Brighton captain and Olivier Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross rebounded off two Brighton players before going to Wirtz, whose first-time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low-key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz’s shot was credited as an own goal by his fellow German, Pascal Gross. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool soon doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously extended. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.

Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second-half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Iraola said: “It is a very valuable win. The key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions, and we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones when we’ve conceded first.”

Sports.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
Sports.content:
At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.

Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.

However, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.

Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.

United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team being humbled by Bournemouth earlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.

This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Show Chelsea came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute. London City Lionesses stayed third after drawing 2-2 at Liverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty. Aston Villa moved level on points with Everton after winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals. Birmingham won for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw off Charlton 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.

United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.

Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

Park’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Not long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.

Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.

Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”

As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.

“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”

Sports.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.”

Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said.

“My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball.” The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage said.

Palace conceded two goals against Besiktas on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”

Sage is sure he can improve ­Palace’s fortunes – they are 17th having lost back-to-back Premier League games, the other being a 5-0 thrashing by their rivals Brighton – and said that although he remains in regular contact with the Palace chair, Steve Parish, the issue of his future has never been raised. “Inside, we are just really focused on solutions,” Sage said. “How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work. There’s no noise inside, if you want.”

There was relief for Matthias Jaissle as he oversaw a first ­Newcastle win in three games. “It was a tough game especially in first half,” the ­German said. “We couldn’t get ourselves the reward for the intensity of our possession.

“The first half out of possession was not that bad but we didn’t have our attacking mindset. The second half was much better. Even if you don’t play a fantastic game in possession, keeping a clean sheet is the fundamental of football.”

Sports.title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record
Sports.content:
Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after this draw with Brentford.

The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam while trying to hook the ball away.

Although Brentford’s Caoimhín Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his first Premier League goal for more than 900 days.

After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.

Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.

An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last opportunity to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off‑target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point.

Hull’s manager, Sergej Jakirovic, was pleased with the improved efforts of his side after the defeat by Fulham the previous weekend. “I think we played a good game, especially in the first half,” he said. “We were much more aggressive in duels, we won a lot of first and second balls. Maybe there were some cheap mistakes, bad passing, bad receiving, but you see how fast they are – in five seconds they were in our box. We should have scored one or maybe two more with better decisions.”

Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.

The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Ten minutes later Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike Mathias Jensen rushed in to foil the attempt.

After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Brentford had to wait until the 63rd minute to equalise, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.

Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with Cho – on as a substitute – in pursuit as backup, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.

The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away. Jakirovic said: “I can regret the chance we had through Mohamed-Ali Cho and Gelhardt, maybe it should have been 2-1, but in the end I think it’s a fair result.”

Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, who had a spell at Hull as a player, was happy to see the response from the players who were brought off the bench during the second half in the leadup to their equaliser. “It was a tough game and it was always going to be a tough game, “ he said.

“I’ve got a lot of respect for Sergej and the journey he’s taken this team on – I think it’s been remarkable. We reacted well at half-time, the impact from the bench was pretty good but it was a tough game.”

Sports.title: Roefs and Trafford stand firm as Sunderland and Leeds battle for point
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris can usually do impassive to perfection but, by the final whistle, even Sunderland’s ultra-balanced manager was looking more than a little fed up and frustrated.

His bottom-placed team had arguably just about deserved a second Premier League win of the season but, instead, had to settle for a draw on an afternoon when the hugely disruptive Storm Boelo proved the enemy of good football.

While Daniel Farke will doubtless regard his resilient side’s fifth league draw of the season as a fair return on the windblown road, much now hinges on Sunderland’s visit to Coventry on Saturday.

At least Le Bris’s side ended a run of four straight league defeats on a day when they could have done without meeting James Trafford’s goalkeeping excellence. “It’s so hard to win games,” said Sunderland’s manager. “But it’s a positive point; we played with intensity and togetherness. We were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey but I think we’ve shown we’re embracing the challenge. We probably deserved more today. But there’s no drama, no panic.”

The wind was strong, and capricious enough, to bend the corner flags out of shape, send pieces of rubbish swirling around the pitch and turn passing calibration horribly awry but it would take a hurricane to throw Brian Brobbey off balance.

The good news for Sunderland was that their formidable centre-forward had recovered from a hamstring injury and seemed to be relishing the physicality of his duel with Jaka Bijol.

Along the way Brobbey had a ­couple of first-half chances. First came the connection with an Enzo Le Fée cross and the slightly deflected shot that prompted a decent save from Trafford.

Then there was the moment when Brobbey bullied Bijol into attempting a short back-pass before charging after it and ­getting there before Trafford. Hats off to Farke’s England goalkeeper for keeping his cool, bravely ­standing his ground and eventually saving cleverly with a leg.

Leeds possess a not-too shabby centre-forward of their own in ­Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He passed a late fitness test on a bruised foot and, although initially less involved than Brobbey, seemed on a mission to engage Luke O’Nien in a personal subplot.

View image in fullscreen James Trafford denies Brian Brobbey from close range. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA

It soon became clear that Calvert-Lewin had little enthusiasm for being marked by O’Nien’s central defensive partner, Nordi Mukiele, and duly manoeuvred himself into cameos against the former at every ­opportunity. Yet although O’Nien endured a couple of wobbles he also made a vital, quite possibly goal-preventing tackle on Calvert-Lewin as half-time beckoned.

The second half had barely begun before fortune frowned on Sunderland. An attempted clearance ­concluded with O’Nien throwing out an elbow and accidentally catching Mukiele in the throat. T he former Paris Saint-Germain defender requiring lengthy treatment as Le Bris looked on anxiously.

Eventually it became apparent a distressed Mukiele – who, Le Bris reported, fully recovered – could not continue and the recently erratic Omar Alderete stepped off the bench.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

By now, a generally ­second-best Leeds were renascent and it took important interceptions from Alderete and Le Fée to break the ­dangerous stride of Jayden Bogle and Ao Tanaka respectively. Undeterred, Sunderland rallied. Nilson Angulo was in encouraging form and two shots from the Ecuadorian forced Trafford into a couple of smart saves.

Shortly after the hour mark the fading Brobbey was replaced by the inexperienced Ukrainian striker Timur Tutyerov as, simultaneously, Farke introduced fresh attacking legs of his own.

They belonged to Noah Okafor and Anton Stach who filled the spaces behind Calvert-Lewin from where Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson had struggled to ­destabilise Sunderland’s backline.

The game remained in the balance. Trafford did well to somehow scramble the ball to safety as Granit Xhaka’s corner very nearly curved beyond him but Robin Roefs was required to dive at Calvert-Lewin’s feet after spilling Tanaka’s shot. Calvert-Lewin wanted a penalty but Stuart Attwell disagreed and a video assistant referee check endorsed that viewpoint.

When the former Newcastle midfeilder Sean Longstaff, on as a Leeds substitute, unleashed a dangerous low, 20-yard shot, Stadium of Light regulars feared the worst but Roefs proved equal to it, making a superb one-handed save to turn the ball around a post.

There was still time for Longstaff to have another shot cleared off the line but Farke remained sanguine. “I’m not complaining about the draw,” said the Leeds manager. “It’s always good to have a clean sheet. It’s fair to say that, in weather like this, it wasn’t the nicest game.”

Inevitably, Farke was invited to praise Trafford and his concession of a mere six league goals in eight games. “He chose a good team,” he said smiling before turning serious. “He delivers, he has the potential to be England’s No 1.”

Sports.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
Sports.content:
Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written.

“The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again.

In the corner, Madrid’s players piled on. This was the Frenchman’s 10th goal against Barcelona but none felt quite like this. Not only was this the first time Barcelona failed to win in the league this season, their record-equalling run halted at nine; it was the first time they had failed to win any game since returning here a year ago.

“I’m not going to let them have their heads on the moon,” Mourinho said, but he knew what this meant. So much for a struggling side heading to an inevitable fall; so much for Barcelona going nine points clear, the title race run before November. There is life in Madrid and in this league. Life in their manager too: this was expertly planned and executed, the rivals who were running at 4.3 goals per game reduced to just one. Those certainties, misplaced, seemed a long way away now; a season starts here instead.

In the beginning, the ball was all Barcelona’s but no sooner had they lost it than the first shot was Madrid’s, Pedri’s startlingly loose pass allowing Arda Guler to break and fire over on four minutes. That felt like a pattern set, a portrait of the way both teams would likely approach this. So too did the way that Marc Cucurella went for Lamine Yamal, the Madrid full-back seeking a way under the winger’s skin – a task in which, it had to be ­concluded, he was successful.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha is congratulated by his teammates after scoring Barcelona’s equaliser. Photograph: Jose Breton/AP

The impression though was deceptive, Madrid willing to step on to the front foot and apply a pressure with which Barcelona were not comfortable, Pedri and Rodri unable to fully settle. Where they could they played too, Bernardo Silva included alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni.

They were also, naturally enough, ready to run. In those early phases, Fede Valverde was opening the pitch with long diagonals. From one, Mbappé went dashing up the left, leading to Joan García scooping away ­Guler’s shot. This was frantic and Madrid were finding it to their liking, Mbappé and Yan Diomandé a threat.

Quick Guide European football roundup Show Ballon d’Or contender Harry Kane failed to find the net on Sunday, but Bayern Munich won 3-1 away at Freiburg to regain top spot in the Bundesliga. The visitors took a 2-0 lead through Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry — his 100th goal in the Bundesliga — before an 82nd-minute Tom Bischof own goal brought Freiburg back into the contest, but Michael Olise secured victory for Bayern in the fifth minute of added time. Bayern remain without their head coach, Vincent Kompany, who collapsed during training on Friday, but lead the Bundesliga on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, who beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 on Saturday. Marcus Thuram scored and then earned the penalty that decided Inter’s late, come-from-behind 2-1 victory over visiting Fiorentina. Álex Jiménez had put Fiorentina ahead midway through the second half at San Siro. Thuram equalised in the first minute of added time with a low shot through traffic and was tugged down minutes later to set up a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the seventh minute of stoppage time. That late comeback moved Inter back to the top of the table, level on 22 points with Lazio but ahead on goal difference. Juventus eased past Lecce in Serie A, with first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz enough to secure a 2-0 victory. It was only Juve's second win in six league outings, an inconsistent run of early season form that sees Luciano Spalletti's just outside the European places in Italy. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The hosts tried to impose control but could not. That said, they too enjoy flying into space, and from a Pedri run Raphinha shot over. Then Anthony Gordon bombed through and produced a neat back-heel for Raphinha to curl wide. The Brazilian would have another shot wide soon after, although the openings were often lost to an insistence on playing (and ­wasting) one last pass or, conversely, to snatch at shots. The half’s best opportunity came when Guler’s gorgeous ball was volleyed over by Mbappé. Back and forth it went, Gordon drawing a sharp save from Andriy Lunin.

In the midst of it all the Camp Nou roared in indignation with each, increasingly intense Cucurella challenge on Lamine Yamal, before silence fell on 41 minutes. Cucurella released Diomandé, so often the destination, who pulled across low and hard. Gerard Martín got there first but could only hit it against Mbappé and in. There was fortune there, but it had been worked for, not simply found. And when Lamine Yamal had a wonderful chance to level he wasted the opportunity, scuffing wide at the near post, a picture of a night that wasn’t his.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona came back at Madrid in the second half. The tackles around the box were racking up: Tchouaméni and Bellingham, Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté. The threat never went away, Martín ended one ­Bellingham break, but the match had tilted. On the hour Barcelona were level. Lamine Yamal took a corner short to Pedri who slipped a clever angled, reversed ball into Raphinha to strike low into the net.

The noise rose. Raphinha was denied at one end. García saved from Guler at the other. And, Barcelona back again, Lunin made an astonishing stop from Martín’s header. Barcelona had taken a grip but not entirely, leaving them exposed to every break and leaving the game, the players and the entire place on edge. Mbappé ran at Barcelona, Pedri ran back again, leading a move that concluded with some neat footwork and a shot just wide. Huijsen then dived in to stop Frenkie de Jong and stopped a Lamine Yamal shot with his face, laying him out. The chance had been laid on by Gordon.

Barcelona insisted. Madrid, tired now, resisted. But there was still some fight in them, and still some finish too.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.

It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. After dropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

View image in fullscreen Rangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller scored to help Hearts secure a 2-0 win over Motherwell at Fir Park on Sunday. A return to winning ways after last weekend’s humbling 7-1 defeat by Celtic leaves Hearts four points behind second-placed Rangers and eight off the leaders. Motherwell sit 10th after this sixth straight defeat, equalling a record from 2003. They were booed off the pitch at the interval and at full time.

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice on Saturday. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton says he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's kids as he gives rare insight into their romance
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's kids as he gives rare insight into their romance

Lewis Hamilton has offered a rare glimpse into his relationship with Kim Kardashian and admitted he 'loves' spending time with her four children.

The pair have been romantically linked since February, and have since gone Instagram official.

But the Formula One legend spoke about his relationship with the reality TV star in a rare moment at this week's US Grand Prix in Austin.

During a panel event at Circuit of the Americas, the Ferrari driver said: 'My niece and nephew always gave me a lot of happiness.

'My girlfriend's kids, I love spending time with them,' he added, referring to North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7.

'She's got four, so I'm getting to play with these kids. I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family.'

Lewis Hamilton has revealed he 'loves' spending time with Kim Kardashian's four children

Hamilton offered a rare glimpse into their romance during an event in Austin this weekend

Kardashian exuded glamour as she strutted out of the Bulgari Hotel in Rome on Friday night

Kardashian, who shares her four children with ex-husband Kanye West, has been to support Hamilton at some races this season but skipped Sunday's race in Austin because she's in Rome celebrating her 46th birthday with mom Kris Jenner.

It comes just days after Kardashian admitted she is 'really, really happy' with how their romance is going during an episode over her reality show.

Kim made the coy admission on The Kardashians and revealed the iconic driver meets every requirement on her famously demanding relationship checklist.

The star discussed a list of more than 50 qualities she wanted in her ideal partner, before suggesting she had finally found someone who fulfilled them all, while speaking to comedian Nikki Glaser, 42, on the set of their film The Fifth Wheel.

When producers pressed her to reveal more about the mystery man, Kim said: 'Oh, you guys are really trying to get this out of me.'

She added: 'Let me just say this – I am just really, really happy. That's all I'll say for now.'

Since going public with their romance, Kim has been seen supporting Lewis at his Formula One races across the globe.

The couple also took a trip to Japan earlier this year, and they are said to have spent a weekend at luxury hotel Estelle Manor in the Cotswolds, and visited Paris – the 'city of love' – in February too.

In the same month, they appeared publicly together at the Super Bowl, when they were shown on the stadium's big screen during the game between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks.

Lewis – who has previously been linked romantically with singer Nicole Scherzinger, 48, and actress Sofía Vergara, 54 – and Kim had known each other for several years prior to their relationship.

Sports.title: Mourinho knee slide
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho hit out at the VAR officials despite Real Madrid's late victory in Barcelona's back yard.

The Portuguese rolled back the years with an epic knee slide as Kylian Mbappe struck a late winner to cut the gap to three points behind Barcelona in La Liga.

His most iconic knee slide came 14 years ago when Cristiano Ronaldo sealed a 90th-minute comeback win against Manchester City in the Champions League.

And Mourinho - now 63 and sporting a grey beard - was on good form as Madrid won 2-1 thanks to Mbappe's double.

But his press conference was dominated with his frustrations and he said: 'The referee was great but the VAR was sleeping.

'There was a clear red card for Cancelo on Diomande that would have changed the game.'

Jose Mourinho won his first El Clasico back at Real Madrid - but still ranted about VAR

He was outraged at Jose Cancelo's apparent stamp on Yan Diomande - not long before Raphinha's equaliser for Barcelona

But Mourinho celebrated Kylian Mbappe's late winner with a knee slide, rolling back the years

Referee Juan Martínez Munuera had allowed play to continue but replays showed that Cancelo had effectively stamped on the forward. Minutes later, Raphinha equalised - and Barcelona had several chances to snatch a winner via him and Lamine Yamal.

Mourinho added: 'In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou. Real Madrid play to win La Liga.

'This must be the mentality. We need to continue like this and don’t go over the moon after this win.'

He is fast gaining momentum in his second spell in charge at the Santiago Bernabeu, with eight wins in their last nine games in all competitions.

Mbappe had put Madrid ahead going into half-time before Raphinha equalised, but the Ballon d'Or contender finished what he started in the 87th minute.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi was at fault twice, accidentally knocking the ball to Mbappe for the first before being skinned by Yan Diomande for the second.

Mourinho was a tempestuous presence on the touchline all night, and had to be calmed down at one point by the referee.

But at full time he was a happy man and crossed the pitch to embrace deputy goalkeeper Andriy Lunin, standing in for Thibaut Courtois, who was ruled out with the flu.

Mbappe struck twice, capitalising on defensive errors from the La Liga leaders

Anthony Gordon and Jude Bellingham faced off against each other and played well

Despite his ferocious activity throughout the game, and his wild celebrations for Mbappe's winner, he was a calm presence at the final whistle, sauntering around with his hands in his pockets.

Madrid have shattered Barcelona's flawless start to the league season and edged ahead in the all-time El Clasico ledger.

They have won 107 derby games to Barcelona's 106, having drawn 52.

Mourinho now has six wins, six draws, and six defeats in the fixture, which has been going since 1888.

England stars Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon both starred in Sunday night's edition and put in strong displays, with the latter teeing up Raphinha for a great chance with a beautiful backheel in the first half.

Former Manchester City stars Rodri and Bernardo Silva played for the first time in Spanish football's marquee fixture, while Ibrahima Konate, Marc Cucurella, and Dean Huijsen joined the ex-Premier League contingent.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was introduced as a substitute deep into added time.

Barcelona manager Hansi Flick felt his side were simply too jaded after four matches in 12 days and did not appear overly troubled by the defeat.

'We were not playing at the highest level because of the (lack of) freshness,' he said.

'It's not top for us but we have to accept it and defeats is part of the game. It's the first defeat in 10 games.

'We have a whole week before the next game to prepare and disconnect.'

Sports.title: Betting SUSPENDED on Man United to sack Michael Carrick after humiliating 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth - with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann favourites to replace him
Sports.content:
Bookmakers have suspended betting on Michael Carrick being sacked by Manchester United. The 45-year-old manager presided over yet another humiliating defeat on Sunday, watching his side go down 3-0 at home against Bournemouth. His United future is hanging by a thread and almost all major betting companies are no longer offering a market on Carrick being dismissed. Attention inevitably then turns to who might replace Carrick if indeed the axe does fall, with United languishing in 16th in the Premier League table. Currently, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe (4/5) is the bookies' favourite, while Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are also in the running. Nagelsmann (5/2) has been out of work since leaving his post as Germany boss after their disappointing World Cup campaign. And ex-Premier League winner Conte (5/1) left Napoli by mutual consent at the conclusion of last season. Other runners and riders, albeit with longer odds, include Unai Emery (17/2), though there is no indication he would want to abandon his post at Aston Villa and Thomas Tuchel (22/1), who remains under contract with England ahead of a home Euros in 2028. Gareth Southgate, Diego Simeone, Kieran McKenna and Cesc Fabregas are all given the same outside shot of taking the helm as Tuchel. There are a few more comedic offerings, with Gary Neville listed at 100/1 to take charge – as is sacked former manager Erik ten Hag. For now, Carrick remains in his position at the crisis club and insisted his gestures to the United fans cheering him after the defeat on Sunday were not a goodbye. ‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them. ‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. Sports.title: Kimi Antonelli WINS the US Grand Prix but is forced to wait for F1 title - as triumph in Texas puts Mercedes star on the brink of history
Sports.content:
It was a day of high stakes and Kimi Antonelli’s father Marco kissed him on the forehead on the grid at the Circuit of the Americas.

Antonelli, 20, was a little red in the face, nothing to do with any embarrassment at his dad’s tenderness, but perhaps a sign he was feeling the weight of history on this warm afternoon that yielded a huge win for him at the US Grand Prix, if not the total fulfilment of his world championship ambitions. Not yet. That will inevitably come.

‘Another small step,’ purred his Mercedes boss Toto Wolff in acclamation over the team radio.

Antonelli, trying to be as cool as possible, had indicated to his team-mates that he had enjoyed the ear-splitting flypast that had drowned out the last strains of the Star-Spangled Banner belted out in the pre-race rituals. The words, ‘Home of the brave,’ were not audible above the engine roar that rent the skies a second or two sooner than perfect choreography’s best-laid plans had dictated.

And then Antonelli spoke to his engineer Peter ‘Bono’ Bonnington, a couple of manly hugs between them, and he stepped into the car, aiming to become the youngest title-holder ever in just a couple of hours.

It was always going to be a tough task in Austin, where he was to go on to triumph by more than 13 seconds from Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, but at least he had started where he would have chosen to. On pole and best placed to set about steeple jacking the wonderful first turn up the hill, with a new hospitality confection overlooking it and punters on the deep grass bank beside it.

Kimi Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix to take another huge step towards the F1 title

After qualifying on pole, the Italian kept his nerve to storm to a convincing win in Austin, Texas

Charles Leclerc (left) and Max Verstappen (right) joined F1's runaway leader on the podium

That first left-hander, a tight one, was his principal challenge. He ruled danger out of the equation there, even with Verstappen, who came home third, sharing the front row of the grid. Antonelli was too fast away, and could take any line he chose, almost bang through the middle of the track as it turned out.

What a relief for Antonelli, for Max Verstappen has been a master here, a four-time winner at COTA, and now the Italian had an element of control over the race.

By then end of lap one, he was more than two seconds ahead of the Dutchman, who was passed by Ferrari’s Leclerc before repassing the Monegasque.

Briefly on the mathematics of the title contest, which are complicated.

This is owing to uncertainty over whether the scheduled final two races will go ahead in Qatar and Abu Dhabi at the end of November and beginning of December. Will they fall victim to war? Nobody can tell. How will Iran act over the next few months? Or the Houthis by proxy? Or The Donald after midterm elections on November 3 (a contest incidentally fighting with Big Pharma for advert airtime on TV networks here)?

So if the schedule were to play out as Formula One bosses hope it will, with the Middle Eastern rounds still on, he needed to leave here 125 points in front.

If they are yet to be called off, and Imola offered as the lone replacement, which is the stand-in option, reducing the existing schedule to just four rounds after Austin, he only needed to leave 100 points clear.

His lead at the start over his demoralised team-mate George Russell stood at 102. Over Lewis Hamilton 111. Over Verstappen 119. Russell was starting sixth, his mental tyres proverbially punctured. Hamilton started fifth, not the best scenario for him behind his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc on a track where he has won five times in a country where he has won six times, the first occasion being in Indianapolis in his debut year at McLaren, 19 years and 20 seasons ago.

To remain in the fight (based on the original roster of races) Russell had to finish eighth or better; Hamilton fourth. But, really, this was a case of them merely prolonging their agony. Their hopes were already destined for the morgue.

So this was the scene. And in brief flickers it looked as if Antonelli might pull off his dream. Hamilton, though, was largely running fourth, which is where he ended up. He had made a decent start and is now 124 points back.

It is inevitable that the Mercedes star will become F1's youngest ever champion very soon

His Mercedes team-mate George Russell endured a frustrating weekend, finishing in ninth

That means – and apologies for all these figures – to be certain of the title Antonelli now needs to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City next weekend, and only that is required if Russell or Hamilton were to win.

As for Russell, he finished eighth and, like Hamilton, only theoretically in the fight – 123 adrift, and even that yawning margin seemed in doubt after an eventful opening lap.

He ran off and then banged wheels with McLaren’s Oscar Piastri. He was punished with a five-second penalty for the latter. And when he had served it, he came out 10th, albeit behind two cars, the Alpine of Pierre Gasly and the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson, neither of which had stopped. He clambered his way to finish where he needed to stay in the contest, arithmetically. But it was a poor afternoon for him, one that summed up his miserable season, one that has seen him demoralised by Antonelli’s run to glory.

‘It was the result we needed,’ said the winner, celebrating his ninth victory in 18 races.

Despite his title glory being delayed, Antonelli’s father Marco could sip the champagne in the Mercedes hospitality area as dusk closed in here, well assured that his boy will be crowned champion in Mexico.

If it’s not there, it will be in Brazil seven days later. Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi/Imola are just spares, laps of honour for Kimi, the kid blowing everyone away.

Sports.title: Man United's players 'aren't professional, don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things and have CONNED Michael Carrick' - he will look at them 'in disgust', rages Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Man United's players 'aren't professional, don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things and have CONNED Michael Carrick' - he will look at them 'in disgust', rages Gary Neville

Gary Neville has accused Man United's players of 'conning' Michael Carrick and branded them 'unprofessional' in an eviscerating attack.

Sunday's abject 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford followed the dire 4-1 embarrassment in Como and looks likely to spell the end of the manager's tenure.

Carrick, 45, received a warm reaction from the Stretford End despite the latest miserable loss and the home faithful then turned on the squad, booing them off the pitch.

Neville appears to agree with the sentiment shown by fans, saying he has 'no time for the players', some of whom he claims 'don't eat the right things' or 'go to bed at the right time'.

'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned him for a few months. They have they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast.

'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though. He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players

'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.'

Carrick chose to leave Bruno Fernandes on the substitutes bench on Sunday after the club captain's scathing remarks about team tactics in midweek and did not turn to him, even with the team losing.

It represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021. Jamie Carragher believes Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Fernandes by snubbing him on Sunday.

For Neville, the simple fact that Fernandes was willing to break rank as he did and publicly take a swipe at Carrick shows that the players have turned on the manager.

He went on: 'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

United were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth and the manager is hanging on by a thread

United are 16th in the Premier League and some bookmakers have suspended betting on Carrick being axed.

Eddie Howe remains the current betting favourite to take the helm if indeed United choose to pull the trigger just months after making Carrick permanent boss following his interim spell.

Carrick put his hand to his chest and showed his appreciation for the support fans offered him after the Bournemouth defeat but insisted his gestures should not be interpreted as a farewell.

Asked if he expects to be sacked, Carrick said: ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way.

‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made.

‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see.

‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?

‘I've tried to do everything I can to not be in this position, of course I have. For a number of reasons, we've not been able to stop that happening to the position we're in right now.

‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough.’

‘It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them.

‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion.

‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair.

‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’

Sports.title: Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Gary Neville labels 'whingeing' Man United captain 'an excuse merchant'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick 'deliberately tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by dropping him against Bournemouth, claims Jamie Carragher - as Gary Neville labels 'whingeing' Man United captain 'an excuse merchant'

Jamie Carragher has claimed Michael Carrick left Bruno Fernandes on the bench during Man United's defeat by Bournemouth to 'embarrass him in front of the supporters'.

Fernandes, 32, was dropped from the starting XI by the under pressure Carrick after his explosive outburst following United's shambolic 4-1 defeat away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That represented the first time Fernandes has been pulled from the line-up for non-fitness reasons since Carrick, again, took him out against Villarreal in November 2021.

The move didn't have the desired impact though as United were dominated by Bournemouth, yet Carrick refused to turn to his club captain.

Lisandro Martinez and Matheus Cunha were initially summoned from the bench, and even when United went 3-0 down after 71 minutes, Carrick brought on Joshua Zirkzee and youngster Shea Lacey instead as he only used four of his permitted five substitutes.

Fernandes looked subdued on the bench throughout the game, and Carragher felt Carrick never had any intention of using him.

Jamie Carragher claimed Michael Carrick 'tried to embarrass' Bruno Fernandes by leaving him on the bench against Bournemouth

Carrick dropped Fernandes after his midweek outburst in the media and refused to turn to him

'I don't think he was ever going to bring him on,' Carragher said on Sky Sports. 'It was a decision to just leave him on the bench and almost try and embarrass him a little bit in front of the supporters, I don't know.

'He brought him off in midweek and that's where the... what Bruno did after the game was on the back of him getting brought off.

'And I think Michael Carrick never had any intention of bringing him on at all today - that sub was never going to happen.'

Speaking after the defeat, which left Carrick on the brink of losing his job, the former midfielder refused to be drawn too much on the issue.

'He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team we did,' he said. 'Unfortunately for everyone, we didn't manage to get the right result.

'There's always times when you're trying to make decisions that make a difference.'

When the team news was announced earlier on Sunday, Carragher had claimed Fernandes' absence could be a positive for the side and also benefit several individual players.

Carragher explained: 'He's Man United's best player, PFA Player of the Year, but Michael Carrick had to make the stand. But, once you've put him there (on the bench) you need a result.

'You're hoping, could this (the benching) bring us together as a group because there's no doubt about it, even though he's the best player there will be a lot of people who don't like playing with him at Man United because he's permanently throwing his arms up at people.

'He's basically saying "you lot aren't good enough to play with me". That's what we see from Fernandes a lot when things aren't going right for Man United, so hopefully the players in the dressing room will stick together and that's what they'll need today.'

Gary Neville told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast after Sunday's defeat.

Gary Neville called Fernandes an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast after the defeat

Carragher claimed that Carrick never had any intention of using Fernandes in Sunday's defeat

'Eric Cantona was very unorthodox as a captain. Roy Keane could sometimes be explosive in his interviews after matches, but they weren't whingers about the tactics, about pressing, or excuse merchants.

'Bruno can't press. To come out and whinge after the game about the manager's tactics, when you've just lost 4-1, and a few thousand fans have paid thousands of pounds to travel over in that far corner and get wet through. I'm sorry, read the room, Bruno.

'This is not a time for whingeing, throwing your arms up in the air. This is a time for you to stand up and say, that's not good enough. Be positive. Do something with a positive influence as a captain. But he's not.

'He's gone and basically thrown his manager under the bus the week after [Lisandro] Martinez did the same.'

Nevilled added: 'They weren't singing for Bruno Fernandez to come on today. They're backing Michael Carrick.

'So get in your box. You know where you stand. Michael Carrick's won things for the football club on a constant basis, and proven that he can have the humility, the resilience. And Bruno has got that. Bruno has delivered for Manchester United in more ways than any other player in the last 13 years.

'He's massively talented but he let himself down this week. He didn't need to do that because he's basically stuck the knife into his manager.'

Pre-match, Carrick had said: 'When you're picking the starting XI and you've got options to choose from, it's always a difficult decision. We've got to make what we feel is the right one for today and the team to get the performance that we want.'

On whether Fernandes was dropped after his explosive outburst, he replied: '(The decision was for) pure footballing reasons.'

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

Sports.title: Sunderland stop the rot in atrocious Storm Boelo conditions - but Leeds boss Daniel Farke is left grateful to £45m James Trafford
Sports.content:
Sunderland stop the rot in atrocious Storm Boelo conditions - but Leeds boss Daniel Farke is left grateful to £45m James Trafford

Well at least Sunderland stopped the rot, even if they remain rock-bottom. And Leeds United departed with a point, not something to be sniffed at in the Premier League.

But this was a tough watch on a bleak day when neither side could beat each other – or the elements – and find the quality required for a breakthrough.

In atrocious conditions caused by Storm Boelo which saw winds of 50mph batter Wearside earlier in the day, that was perhaps understandable.

Half-chances proliferated at both ends but really it needed a touch of class from somewhere to break the deadlock and warm the cockles of over 46,000 frozen spectators.

Or a mistake perhaps. Neither came.

Two of the division's leading marksmen – fit-again Brian Brobbey of Sunderland and Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin – were left to feed off scraps.

Leeds were left grateful to goalkeeper James Trafford as they claimed a point at Sunderland

Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin was left to feed off scraps before he was withdrawn

Leeds might have pilfered the points late on through former Newcastle man Sean Longstaff

Both were withdrawn during the second half, which in many ways summed things up, although Leeds might have pilfered the points late on through former Newcastle man Sean Longstaff.

That would have been harsh on Sunderland, who showed undeniable spirit in ending a run of four straight Premier League defeats.

For all Leeds' progress this season – they have lost just once – wins are proving hard to come by and this stalemate marked their fifth draw of the campaign and left them in seventh.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke said: 'First of all, I think it's fair to say that this was not the nicest piece of football.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 6, Mukiele 6 (Alderete 52, 6), O'Nien 6, Reinildo 6; Xhaka 6, Sadiki 6; Rigg 6, Le Fee 6 (Diarra 79), Angulo 7 (Talbi 79); Brobbey 6.5 (Tutierov 65, 6) Booked: Mandava Manager: Regis Le Bris 6 LEEDS UNITED: (3-4-2-1): TRAFFORD 7.5; Bijol 6, Muharemovic 6, Justin 6; Bogle 6, Ampadu 6, Tanaka 6 (Longstaff 89), Gudmundsson 6; Aaronson 5.5 (Okafor 65, 6), Wilson 5.5 (Stach 66, 6); Calvert-Lewin 6 (Nmecha 85) Booked: Ampadu, Bogle Manager: Daniel Farke 6 Referee: Stuart Attwell 6 Attendance: 46,182

'But these games also belong to the Premier League and we came here to a difficult ground where not many teams have won.

'With the weather conditions, you could hardly predict the curve of the ball, so you have to dig in and show steel.

'This is what we did and to get a clean sheet away from home is always pleasing. Overall a draw was a fair outcome.'

Farke pointed to the disruption which saw defender Nico Elvedi miss out through illness and Calvert-Lewin, Noah Okafor and Anton Stach struggle with knocks during the week.

The Leeds boss was also left grateful to his £45million club-record signing James Trafford who made a number of saves to keep the Black Cats at bay.

Farke added: 'I wouldn't say there was one world-class save but several good saves and James showed why we were desperate to sign him. To be honest, I expect this from him.'

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris was happy to take the positives after his side's abject 2-0 surrender at Bournemouth last weekend.

The manner of that loss prompted defender Nordi Mukiele to brand his team 'arrogant' and 'not good enough'.

After fighting tooth and nail against Leeds, this was another step in the right direction following the 1-1 draw at Lech Poznan in the Europa League.

Le Bris reflected: 'It was a tight game against a good team.

'We are struggling a bit, so the most important thing was to be Sunderland.

'We showed togetherness, intensity, consistency and avoided the unforced errors that we've committed in recent games.

'The weather wasn't easy to manage, but we created some small chances, although not enough to win it.'

Farke flatly rejected suggestions last week that Leeds could mount a serious challenge for European qualification this season.

He claimed such talk is 'unrealistic' and his side certainly struggled to impose themselves on Sunderland during the first half.

Brobbey went closest with a 20-yard strike that Trafford kept out and the England goalkeeper cut an assured presence all afternoon.

Sunderland's commitment was clear to see and typified by Trai Hume's crunching challenge on Leeds left-back Gabriel Gudmundsson as half-time approached.

Leeds began to turn the screw after the break and Tarik Muharemovic headed straight at Robin Roefs from a corner.

But as the hour mark approached, Trafford proved his worth again when turning Nilson Angulo's low curling shot away for a corner.

Calvert-Lewin saw appeals for a penalty ignored before Leeds substitute Longstaff hit a low, left-foot shot in the 90th minute which Roefs turned round a post.

Longstaff went close again moments later but could not find the net as both sides settled for a point from a game they will be happy to move on from quickly.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace feel numbered as clinical Newcastle triumph 2-0 to ease pressure on Matthias Jaissle, writes BOBBY MANZI
Sports.content:
Two managers were desperate to alleviate the pressure on their jobs at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

For 45 minutes, it looked as though both Matthias Jaissle and Pierre Sage would achieve that - with defences on top in a tame affair.

But an 11-minute Magpies masterclass saw Palace implode, leaving the Newcastle boss in a much more secure job than the man in the opposite dugout.

Newcastle sliced through Palace as William Osula roamed free of Chris Richards to poke Jacob Murphy’s cross home from close range. Harvey Barnes added the second, capping off a slick passing move with a neat finish inside the box.

Daily Mail Sport’s Bobby Manzi unpacks a consequential afternoon in south London.

Harvey Barnes and William Osula scored within 11 minutes of each other as Newcastle climbed to seventh in the Premier League

Defensive improvement

This was a monumental defensive performance from Jaissle’s side, who kept only their second clean sheet of the season.

Confidence in the Newcastle backline was low after conceding eight goals in their previous two away matches.

But a change in personnel at centre-back, bringing experienced heads Dan Burn and Fabian Schar in from the start, gave Newcastle much more stability.

Schar made 15 defensive contributions, 10 clearances and was not dribbled past once. Similar can be said of Burn alongside him.

Besides a good chance inside the six-yard box for Jean-Philippe Mateta inside the first five minutes, Palace did not create much of note.

There were some scruffy penalty area scrambles in the first half but Burn and Schar consistently found ways to deal with it.

Newcastle had greater defensive organisation, giving a stable platform to win for the first time since mid-September.

‘It’s important to mention Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw have done a good job in the last weeks,’ Jaissle said. ‘But we went for more experience and leadership to give stability to a young group who have been shaking a bit with the defeats. We’re really glad it worked out.’

The midfield pair were pivotal, too. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton grafted defensively.

Every player knew their role in a dogged showing, and that will encourage Jaissle moving forward.

Matthias Jaissle's side were better at both ends of the pitch against struggling Crystal Palace

MATCH FACTS Crystal Palace (3-4-3): Benitez 5; Richards 4, Disasi 6, Canvot 6; Khalaili 6, Wharton 4, Kamada 6, Mitchell 6; McNeil 6 (Osorio 62min 6), Mateta 5 (Nketiah 62min 6), Pino 6 Booked: Canvot, Khalaili, Pino Manager: Pierre Sage 5 Newcastle United (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 8; Dedic 7 (Thiaw 90min), Schar 8, Burn 7, Hall 7; Gonzalez 8, Joelinton 7 (Steur 85min); Murphy 7, Willock 6 (Ramsey 77min 6), Barnes 7 (Elanga 77min 6); Osula 7 (Wissa 77min 6) Booked: Gonzalez, Schar Manager: Matthias Jaissle 8 Referee: Paul Tierney 7

Clinical Magpies

At the opposite end of the pitch, it was a clinical Newcastle performance. They did not have many chances, amassing less than one expected goal but lethally punished Palace’s mistakes to climb to seventh in the league.

Osula's goal came from nowhere after the break. Newcastle had created very little in the first half but Jaissle's team talk seemingly sparked them into life - moving the ball quicker and with more purpose.

It was a simple goal, a neat cross in and some clever movement. A perfect response to their dull first half where they did not manage a shot on target.

Again, their second goal was another rapid move. Adam Wharton’s sloppiness in midfield was punished as Newcastle quickly shifted the ball to the right, crossed low into the box before laying off to Barnes.

Moving forward, Newcastle must create more chances because, aside from the goals, they crafted very little.

But the clinical display – alongside the defensive strength – marked a step in the right direction.

Sage’s time to go

The season’s first managerial sacking is imminent. Will it be Palace manager Sage or Michael Carrick at Manchester United?

At this rate, both clubs could release their statements at the same time. If at least one hasn’t posted the traditional corner flag picture alongside an official statement by Monday afternoon, something has gone seriously wrong.

Palace have the worst defence in the Premier League, conceding 19 goals in eight games, with only Oliver Glasner’s Nottingham Forest keeping them outside of the relegation zone.

There were signs of improvement in the first half against Newcastle. Palace defended as a solid unit and did not offer Newcastle a shot on target.

However, they imploded straight after half time, shipping two cheap goals. Soft goals have been a hallmark of Sage’s side, as have lapses of concentration and inconsistent performances within games.

An 11-minute spell straight after the break killed all the positive work Palace had done.

It feels like Pierre Sage's days at Crystal Palace are numbered after another disapponting loss

Meanwhile, this was the second game in a row they conceded less than one xG but shipped two goals.

It can be argued that they have been unlucky with every mistake punished. But that is a product of the defensive structure, where they are asked to be aggressive and come unstuck when they don’t have the ball.

Sage believes possession is the best form of defence, which is slightly worrying considering only three teams have had less possession than Palace this season.

Palace have won just one of their last six, and Sage’s defensive record is alarming decision-makers. It is difficult to see him fighting on much longer. Palace play again on Wednesday, and the quick succession of games may be Sage’s saving grace.

But supporters are growing restless, booing the team and manager off the pitch on Sunday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Board hold crisis talks as Man Utd boss on verge of sack
Sports.content:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick could be facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford

Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is hanging by a thread after the Reds suffered a humiliating 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

Carrick, 45, had come into the game against the Cherries under huge pressure following a dismal start to the season, with the Reds winning just TWO in 11 fixtures across all competitions.

But United were humiliated on home soil with Bournemouth running out comfortable winners. Rayan put the Cherries ahead in the 38th minute before Marcus Tavernier capitalised on a defensive error from Leny Yoro to double the visitors' lead.

Despite an improved start to the second half, Bournemouth made it three in the 71st minute with Evanilson rounding Senne Lammens before curling the ball home from a tight angle.

That is how it remained with Carrick now facing the sack after United extended their winless run to seven matches. They have dropped to 16th in the Premier League table on just seven points from a possible 24.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz sends clear message Jamie Carragher after helping Liverpool to another win
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz sends clear message Jamie Carragher after helping Liverpool to another win

Florian Wirtz has been on the receiving end of some harsh criticism from Jamie Carragher and other pundits this season, but the Liverpool playmaker isn't worried

View 2 Images Florian Wirtz has been criticised for his performances this season (Image: Paul Currie / AFP via Getty Images)

Florian Wirtz has brushed off the harsh words of his critics, insisting he is not interested in their opinions.

‌



‌



Wirtz has proven to be a hugely divisive player since Liverpool splashed out £116.5million to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. The Germany international arrived with an exciting reputation to go alongside his sky-high price tag and is yet to fully convince.

‌



He flattered to deceive in his debut campaign under the management of Arne Slot, but appears to be finding his feet under Andoni Iraola. Liverpool picked up their fourth straight win on Sunday by beating Brighton and Wirtz made a telling contribution.

‌



It was his shot which cannoned off Pascal Gross to make it 1-0 before Bradley Barcola set up Alexander Isak to double the lead minutes later. He was forced off in the second half with a knock but still spoke to reporters post-match.
