Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Could Abandon WBO Title Over Raymond Muratalla
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson could soon face a tough business call if the WBO installs Raymond Muratalla as his mandatory challenger at 140 pounds. Taking that fight means accepting real physical risk without the massive financial windfall tied to bouts against Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, or Gervonta Davis.

Top Rank took the first step by petitioning the sanctioning body to elevate their top-ranked contender. A petition doesn’t make the fight a done deal, yet it instantly forces the question of whether Shakur actually wants the matchup if it gets ordered.

Nobody can say Shakur is running just yet. At the same time, wanting to wear a world title strap and wanting the specific challenger standing behind it are completely separate things.

Muratalla brings zero box office power compared to the superstars Shakur keeps calling out. The challenger hits hard enough to turn lights out, but that kind of heavy-handed grit rarely guarantees a huge network budget or career-best purse. Without any clear financial guarantees on the table, Stevenson would effectively be asked to accept a discounted payday for a fight that could destroy his road to far bigger money.

That threat doesn’t mean Muratalla has to outbox the champion for twelve rounds. Stevenson could easily control long stretches with his southpaw jab, footwork, and outside defense. Still, he would need to stay locked in every second Muratalla steps inside to plant his feet. One slip against a true puncher wipes out entire rounds of clean boxing.

Defending the belt carries obvious perks for Shakur. He retains his hardware, adds a legitimate scalp to his resume, and silences critics who would otherwise claim he ducked the division’s toughest boogeyman. Chasing mega-fights with Haney, Garcia, or Tank always involves tricky promotional hurdles and clashing timelines. A hypothetical super-fight puts no cash in the bank until ink hits paper.

If a genuine blockbuster offer surfaces right as the WBO issues a firm order, dropping the title becomes a very real temptation. Shakur would take heat from fans for walking away from an elite challenger, but boxing remains a business first.

Holding that WBO belt helps Stevenson sell himself as the top dog at light welterweight. If Muratalla gets named mandatory, holding onto the hardware means taking a fight where the physical risk completely outweighs the financial reward. Until Shakur puts his signature on a bout agreement, nobody should be shocked if that belt suddenly loses its shine.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Runs His Own Fighter Of The Year Campaign
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is out here campaigning for Fighter of the Year like an actor chasing an Oscar. He put together the kind of year that lands him in the conversation, yet he talks like the engraver already finished carving his name onto the plaque.

The WBC welterweight champion took to X to laugh off his detractors, already picturing their meltdown if he takes the hardware.

“I wish I can screenshot peoples faces when I am picked as fighter of the year.

They think comments and their opinion matter

HILLARIOUS”

Ryan builds his case around a February decision over Mario Barrios and a wild second-round blitz of Conor Benn in September. Grabbing a belt and immediately defending it with a highlight-reel knockout gives him a loud pitch to make to the public.

Still, do those two names really justify that kind of swagger?

Barrios and Benn ring bells with casual fans. That definitely juices his campaign, because everyone remembers the violent finish. But star power alone cannot carry the day when stack-ranking his resume against elite runs across the sport.

Voters have to dig into the actual depth of the competition, what each challenger brought to the ring, and how those nights stack up against the best wins in boxing this year.

That brings us right back to the Hollywood analogy. Ryan stays in everyone’s face, feeding his base fresh talking points and using every single critique as fuel to dominate the timeline. Every debate over whether he deserves the trophy simply keeps him front and center.

There is nothing wrong with wanting recognition. Fighters have short careers, and an award can help sell their next appearance. Ryan also understands how to get a reaction without throwing a punch.

Still, he is getting ahead of the voting. His post treats disagreement as something he will eventually laugh at, when the reasonable question is whether beating Barrios and Benn amounts to the best year in the sport.

If Ryan gets his wish and steps into the ring with a 49-year-old Floyd Mayweather Jr. before December wraps up, what does that actually show the ballot casters? Mayweather’s brand still sells pay-per-views by the truckload, but Ryan would be sharing a ring with a man staring down his fiftieth birthday, nearly a decade removed from actual world-class prize fighting.

Beating up a retired legend does not tell voters a single thing about how Ryan handles the elite, prime talent ruling today’s welterweight division.

A third outing would certainly give Ryan an active calendar year. Still, the quality of the man in the opposite corner has to justify the accolades Ryan demands. Mayweather earned his legendary status decades ago; Ryan cannot simply inherit those accolades by beating on a senior citizen.

That kind of booking makes the Oscar campaign comparison dead accurate. Ryan would have a massive box office spectacle to push during voting season, leaving the panel to figure out whether there is any genuine substance behind the marquee name.

Sports.title: Nearly Three Years Out, Vasily Lomachenko Bypasses Tuneup For O’Shaquie Foster Clash
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko wants to make his comeback at super featherweight in 2027, eyeing an immediate collision with O’Shaquie Foster for three world titles. Stepping directly into a fight of that magnitude following a layoff of over two years represents a massive gamble.

In an interview with DAZN, Lomachenko revealed plans to end his retirement and target the victor of the unification clash. Foster then took care of business, outpointing Emanuel Navarrete to collect the WBC, IBF, and WBO belts at 130 pounds.

Lomachenko (18-3, 12 KOs) long maintained that 135 pounds was north of his natural fighting weight. Returning to super featherweight pits him against men his own physical dimensions. Yet, the calendar tells a harsh story: Lomachenko has not made 130 pounds since forcing Guillermo Rigondeaux to retire on his stool in December 2017. He was 29 years old on that night. He turns 39 this coming February.

“During the preparation, it looks very good, but nobody knows what will happen after another month or two of preparation,” Lomachenko admitted.

That physical reality demands scrutiny before any title clash gets finalized. Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, laser reflexes, and suffocating punch volume. Dropping five pounds will not magically restore those physical gifts after such an extensive absence from competition.

Foster presents a nightmare stylistic exam for an aging ring master. His victory over Navarrete showcased frustrating defensive elusiveness, slick counterpunching, and lateral movement. Lomachenko cannot afford his trademark reconnaissance rounds against a mobile champion who racks up points from distance.

The championship math matters as well. Foster currently holds three titles rather than the full undisputed collection, with the WBA strap still elsewhere. How the division shakes out over the coming months will dictate exactly what sits on the table when Lomachenko officially makes his move.

Lomachenko has not boxed since May 2024, when he broke down George Kambosos Jr. in Australia to capture the IBF lightweight crown. The desire to compete remains potent. Taking an interim tune-up bout before stepping directly into Foster’s sights would tell boxing, and Lomachenko, whether his reflexes can still match his ambitions.

When an elite fighter sits out from May 2024 until 2027, the biological clock does not pause. Lomachenko dropping back down to 130 pounds after a decade away from the division introduces extreme physical stress on an aging body.

Bypassing a tune-up saves wear in the gym, but walking straight into a unification against a rangy, prime champion after years of inactivity leaves zero margin for error.

Sports.title: Arthur Biyarslanov Lands In Saudi Arabia While Lindolfo Delgado Remains Stranded Stateside
Sports.content:
Lindolfo Delgado’s chance at a world title could vanish from the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli card before either junior welterweight laces up the gloves. Arthur Biyarslanov is already on the ground in Riyadh, yet Delgado’s trip remains entirely up in the air ahead of their scheduled October 31 vacant IBF title bout.

According to BoxingScene, Biyarslanov touched down alongside promotional teammate Mbilli after the pair took an alternate route into the Saudi capital. Meanwhile, Delgado’s trainer, Robert Garcia, chose not to address his fighter’s travel status while heading back from Albert Gonzalez’s win in San Antonio. That report stopped short of an official pullout, but the clock is ticking fast.

Right now, Biyarslanov is getting acclimated in the host city while nobody knows if his challenger will ever show up. With less than a week remaining, the delay wipes out the essential window Delgado needs to shake off jet lag, adjust to the local clock, and put the finishing touches on his camp.

Dan Rafael added more fuel to the fire, reporting that Delgado, Garcia, and the rest of the crew are still stateside without flight itineraries in hand. When pressed on whether the matchup actually takes place, Rafael noted that an insider gave it a flat “probably not.” While not a formal scrap just yet, that level of skepticism speaks volumes.

A vacant world championship is usually all the motivation a boxer needs to cross an ocean. At the same time, elite fighters require reliable logistics, smooth transit, and a clear setup they can trust. Dealing with travel chaos during peak fight week is the last thing any contender needs before stepping inside the ropes.

Having Biyarslanov in town gives organizers half the equation. It does nothing to solve the other side, and neither man gains anything from sitting through fight week wondering if the opening bell will ever ring.

The marquee event will march on behind the headliners, but undercard contenders are putting their health, records, and livelihoods on the line. Even the brightest championship belt loses its shine when the simple act of getting to the arena turns into a nightmare.

Unless Delgado’s team solidifies an itinerary immediately, this clash stays trapped in limbo, leaving one fighter waiting in the desert and the other stuck thousands of miles away.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Admits The Blueprint: Why Playing Smart Means Surviving Christian Mbilli
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez talking about “playing it smart” against Christian Mbilli sounds like code for fighting less. Pick a few sharp counters, cover up between them, and avoid getting dragged into a pace his 36-year-old legs and lungs cannot sustain.

Alvarez practically laid out the entire blueprint. At this point in his career, he fights like a 40-year-old because he turned pro at fifteen. The biological mileage is massive. Against a tireless machine like Mbilli, trying to match output is impossible, and Canelo knows it.

“We’re always looking for the knockout. Every single fighter is looking for a knockout. A spectacular win for the fans, too. But if not, I’m going to play it smart,” said Canelo to DAZN.

He could spend long stretches absorbing shots on the arms while waiting for a single clean opening, trusting his occasional flashy punches to outweigh Mbilli’s sustained work.

On Saturday night, we’ll likely see Canelo shell up in that high clamshell guard, parked against the ropes, letting Mbilli unload 20 punches on his gloves and arms, then waiting for one opening to throw a clean left hook or uppercut. Then he resets, catches his breath, and hopes the dramatic sound of his one punch convinces three judges to ignore the two minutes of sustained body snatching Mbilli just put in.

It is pure veteran survival mode dressed up as ring craft. If Mbilli has the chin to walk through those occasional counter shots without blinking, Canelo is going to spend twelve rounds trapped in a meat grinder, praying his reputation and the house scorecards bail him out at the final bell.

Mbilli is crude, but he is stubborn and possesses endless stamina. Canelo can definitely steal rounds from the high guard if he stays sharp enough to land the flashiest punch in each frame. If Mbilli swallows those shots and refuses to break off his attacks, Canelo will find out that playing smart turns into a very painful night.

Sports.title: Arum Claims Emanuel Navarrete Was Leading O’Shaquie Foster Before Final Round Beatdown
Sports.content:
Bob Arum claims he had Emanuel Navarrete ahead going into the 12th round against O’Shaquie Foster on Saturday night. That is a baffling read on a fight where Foster boxed circles around him before dropping Navarrete twice in the final three minutes.

Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) outclassed Navarrete (40-3-1, 33 KOs) by unanimous decision in San Antonio to collect the IBF and WBO super featherweight titles alongside his WBC belt. The judges turned in cards of 118-108, 115-111, and 118-108.

The Top Rank boss somehow watched a completely different fight through the first 11 rounds.

“Navarrete is not the easiest guy to fight because he comes from so many different angles, and I had him slightly ahead going into the last round,” Arum said to Fight Hub TV.

Sure, Navarrete is awkward. He throws punches from weird trajectories that you cannot mimic in training camp. Trying to argue that he was actually winning the fight going into the 12th is another story entirely.

Throwing unorthodox shots from strange angles does not win rounds if you are hitting air or gloves. Plodding forward without landing clean punches does not score points either. You have to look at who is actually landing effective blows. Foster picked Navarrete apart all night, yet Arum’s unofficial tally completely ignored his ring generalship.

The official scorecards shred Arum’s narrative. Foster’s two knockdowns in the 12th padded the final gap, though he already had the fight locked up on the cards. Two judges had Foster winning by ten points at the final bell. Even the tightest card had him up by four. Do the math without the 10-7 final round, and Foster was still cruising to a comfortable victory.

Arum conveniently skipped giving a round-by-round breakdown to back up his claim. Knowing which six rounds he somehow handed to Navarrete would be fascinating. What exactly was Arum scoring?

Boxing fans debate close rounds all the time. Claiming Navarrete led after 11 rounds is just pure promoter spin.

Foster should not have to rely on two late knockdowns just to get full credit for a masterclass. Dropping Navarrete twice was simply the exclamation point on a dominant night. Arum is trying to paint a picture where Foster needed a last-minute miracle to pull out the win, which is an insult to the clinic everyone else just watched.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Questions WBO Over Voluntary Defense Reversal
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is challenging Gustavo Olivieri to explain what changed after claiming the WBO president publicly agreed to let him make a voluntary defense before facing mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez next year.

Bentley’s response follows Olivieri’s explanation that the organization never received a formal petition to approve the proposed fight against Shane Mosley Jr. The dispute leaves two different accounts of how Bentley’s planned voluntary defense reached this point.

“Whether I had an opponent or not this guy agreed and tweeted I get a voluntary defence before the end of the year then fight yo-yo next year which I was happy to do so the question everyone needs to ask is what changed,” Bentley wrote on X.

That is the question Bentley wants answered. His argument is that Olivieri had already accepted the sequence: a voluntary before the end of 2026, followed by Hernandez in 2027.

Olivieri, speaking to Tru School Sports, described a process that still required formal approval.

“We never received a formal petition. From Zuffa, from team Bentley, or from team Mosley for this particular fight.”

The WBO president added that every championship defense requires the approval of its championship committee, whether the opponent is a mandatory challenger or a voluntary selection.

According to Olivieri, Bentley had no date, opponent, or venue when the mandatory obligation needed to be addressed. Hernandez had been the designated challenger since July, and his team submitted a petition seeking enforcement.

Bentley is scheduled to face Mosley on November 7 in London, but the WBO rejected his appeal to take a voluntary defense and instructed him to commit to Hernandez.

The wording of Olivieri’s earlier post is therefore crucial. An explicit agreement allowing Bentley to fight a voluntary before Hernandez would give the British fighter a reasonable basis to question the subsequent ruling. Permission dependent on committee approval would leave Bentley’s team responsible for completing that process.

A public conversation with the president and formal authorization from the championship committee may be separate steps. Bentley’s latest response does not explain whether his team submitted the details needed to secure that authorization.

Hernandez has his own interests to protect. He pursued his mandatory opportunity and asked the WBO to enforce it. Accepting Bentley’s preferred timetable would require him to wait while the champion takes another fight.

Bentley says he was willing to face Hernandez next year. The disagreement is over whether he had permission to take another opponent first—and whether Olivieri’s earlier words support the permission Bentley believes he received.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Falls Short Against Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton “Thunder” Smith (20-0, 14 KOs) retained his WBC light welterweight title with a split decision over former champion Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-2, 11 KOs) on Saturday at a sold-out Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England.

Two judges scored the fight 115-113 for Smith, while the third had Puello ahead 115-112. Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Boxing promoted the event, which aired on DAZN.

The opening six rounds were closely contested, with this writer’s unofficial card even after Puello took the fifth and sixth.

Smith responded well in the seventh and eighth, edging the action as swelling appeared beneath Puello’s left eye. Puello answered with stronger work in the ninth and tenth before Smith took the 11th.

In the final round, a left hand from Puello opened a small cut on Smith’s right cheek. Smith began celebrating during the final 30 seconds, although the divided scorecards showed how close the contest had been.

Lee Every refereed.

Giorgio Visioli Edges Maxi Hughes

Unbeaten southpaw Giorgio “The Italian Job” Visioli (12-0, 6 KOs) defeated veteran Maxi “Maximus” Hughes (29-10-2, 6 KOs) by majority decision over ten rounds to win the vacant WBC International Silver lightweight title.

Two judges scored it 96-94 for Visioli, with the third returning a 95-95 draw.

Visioli’s effective jab helped him through much of the first seven rounds. Hughes opened a cut over Visioli’s left eyebrow with a right jab in the eighth, but Visioli responded and finished strongly enough to secure the decision. Kieran McCann refereed.

Shannon Ryan Stops Emma Dolan In Rematch

Shannon “Kaos” Ryan (12-1, 3 KOs) avenged her previous defeat to Emma Dolan (9-2, 1 KO) with a first-round stoppage in their scheduled ten-round super flyweight rematch.

Around 20 seconds into the fight, Ryan dropped Dolan with a right hand to the side of the face. Dolan rose, but another right followed by a left sent her down again.

Referee Howard Foster stopped the contest at 40 seconds after Dolan regained her feet.

Edward Hardy Outpoints Diego Ruiz

Edward Hardy (9-0, 3 KOs) remained unbeaten with an eight-round points victory over Diego “El Profeta” Ruiz (28-16-1, 14 KOs).

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-73 for Hardy, who controlled most of the action from the second round onward.

Both fighters maintained a high work rate during an active final round, but Hardy finished with a clear points win.

Joe Hayden Defeats Will Harrison

Joe Hayden (25-0, 4 KOs) handed Will “The Thrill” Harrison (8-1-2, 0 KOs) his first professional defeat in their eight-round welterweight bout.

Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick scored it 79-72 for Hayden.

Leo Atang Scores Three Knockdowns In First-Round Stoppage

Nineteen-year-old heavyweight Leo Atang (9-0, 8 KOs) dropped Jonathan “Chicito” Vergara (9-5, 5 KOs) three times before stopping him in the opening round of their scheduled six-round contest.

A right hand dropped Vergara within the first minute. Atang scored another knockdown with a right to the side of the head with approximately 30 seconds remaining.

A third right hand sent Vergara down again in the closing seconds. Referee Jamie Kirkpatrick waved off the fight after Vergara rose, just before the bell.

Chris Mulunda Shuts Out Harley Collison

Chris “Mulla” Mulunda (5-0, 0 KOs) defeated Harley Collison (3-9-2, 0 KOs) by points over six rounds.

Referee Michael Alexander scored every round for Mulunda, returning a 60-54 verdict.

Divine Omojor Wins Professional Debut

Cruiserweight Divine Omojor (1-0, 1 KO) began his professional career with a second-round stoppage of Goran Kozul (8-13, 2 KOs).

Referee Michael Alexander stopped the scheduled four-round bout at 1:52 of the second.

David Diamante served as ring announcer.

Ghana News.title: T-bills auction: Government exceeds target; 91-day and 182-day yield decline
Ghana News.content:
Demand for treasury bills increased as the government exceeded its target by about 12%.

This is coming after the government announced it would raise GHȼ15.3 billion in the final quarter of 2026.

The government received total bids of GH¢4.26 billion from the investors, but accepted GH¢3.9 billion.

A little over GH¢2.8 billion of the bids were tendered for the 91-day bill, representing 67% of the total bids. The uptake was, however, GH¢2.5 billion.

The 182-day bill received bids of about GH¢533.28 million. About GH¢ 420 million was accepted.

For the 364-day bill, about GH¢873 million of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢420 million of the bids were accepted.

Meanwhile, interest rates went down on the shorter end of the yield curve, but rose on the longer end of the yield curve.

The yield on the 91-day bill declined by a basis point to 4.61%.

Again, the 182-day bill also fell to 6.27% from the previous week’s 6.31%.

However, the yield on the 364-day bill increased by 4.0 basis points to 9.75%.

Ghana News.title: Testing new Goldbod CEO’s ‘new law’ on small-scale mining against the law
Ghana News.content:
“Once it’s not a water body; it’s not a forest reserve or… place like a roadside, whether the person has a licence or not; the government says we should allow the person to mine and register and regularise them” – CEO, GoldBod

1. Section 9 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703) provides that a person shall not conduct mining, prospecting or exploration on land in Ghana unless granted a mineral right under the Act — and this applies even where the person owns or holds rights in the land. Section 82 separately provides that a person shall not engage in asmall-scale mining operation without a licence granted by the Minister or an authorised officer, and it does so "notwithstanding any law to the contrary."

2. Mining without that licence is not merely irregular; it is a crime. Under section 99 as originally enacted, small-scale mining without the Minister's licence attracted a minimum fine of 1,000 penalty units and up to three years' imprisonment. The Minerals and Mining (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 995) dramatically increased this. According to the Minerals Commission, a Ghanaian engaged in unlicensed mining or mining support services faces a fine of 10,000 to 15,000 penalty units and 15 to 25 years' imprisonment; a non-Ghanaian faces 100,000 to 350,000 penalty units and 20 to 25 years, with deportation after sentence. Equipment and product are seized on arrest and must be forfeited to the State on conviction.

3. So the instruction described is an instruction to permit the commission of a crime carrying, for a Ghanaian, a mandatory minimum of fifteen years.

4. A ministerial or administrative direction that unlicensed persons "should be allowed to mine" is therefore ultra vires. The Minister's statutory power under section 82 is a power to grant licences. It is not a power to authorise mining without one. A public officer who purports to exercise a power he does not have acts outside the law, and Article 296 — which requires that discretionary power be exercised fairly, candidly and not arbitrarily or capriciously — bites on top of that.

5. Section 18 of Act 703 (Minerals and Mining Act) requires environmental and forestry clearance from every mineral right holder — not only from those operating in forests or rivers. A site that is neither a water body nor a forest reserve nor a roadside is still unlawful to mine without an environmental permit.

6. The statement's implicit test — anywhere that is not expressly prohibited is permitted — reverses the statutory scheme, which is a permission-based regime: nothing is permitted unless affirmatively licensed.

7. Formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining is not contrary to Ghanaian law. It is lawful policy, and it is arguably obligatory. As a party to the Minamata Convention on Mercury, Ghana must, under Article 7 and Annex C, develop a national action plan for artisanal and small-scale gold mining, and formalisation is an express element of that plan. The Minister has express power under section 89 to designate areas, and under section 82 to grant licences. A properly structured fast-track registration drive, the Community Mining Scheme model, and district-level licensing support are all lawful vehicles.

8. The illegality lies entirely in the sequence. The law permits: register first, then mine. The statement describes mining first, then registering. Regularisation cannot retroactively cure a completed offence. Once unlicensed mining has occurred, the offence under section 99 is complete. Subsequent registration does not expunge it. Only a nolle prosequi by the Attorney-General under Article 88(3)–(4) or a presidential pardon under Article 72 can affect criminal liability, and neither is available as a general administrative policy.

9. The Goldbod CEO's assurance is no defence to the miner. Mistake of law does not excuse, and no estoppel can arise against a statute — a citizen cannot acquire by official representation a right that Parliament has withheld. The miner who relies on this assurance is exposed to fifteen years' imprisonment; the official who gave it faces no exposure at all. That asymmetry is itself an argument that the practice is indefensible.

10. An official who directs that unlicensed mining be permitted may be:

• liable as an abettor under the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), s.20, to the

section 99 offence;

• liable under the Act 995 offences relating to facilitating participation in small-scale mining and providing equipment contrary to law;

• in breach of the following provisions of the 1992 Constitution: Article 284 (conflict of interest) and Article 296;

• in breach of the State's Article 36(9) duty to protect and safeguard the national environment, with the citizen's reciprocal duty under Article 41(k).

The CEO cannot claim ignorance of the law. This is not a slip of the tongue. This is a deliberate strategy to test Ghanaians' resolve to fight the galamsey menace, which poses an existential threat to the State. It confirms a bold attempt by the NDC to take us a step deeper into galamsey and to confirm that Ghana is a galam-state. This statement undermines all the so-called efforts that the government has been touting as a success story in its fight against galamsey. It also affirms, in no uncertain terms, the allegation that at least some of the gold Goldbod buys is linked to galamsey.

Indeed, this is not the first time the current government has made pronouncements on galamsey, which suggests an unwillingness to help fight the galamsey menace. Yet, overall, society's reaction to them has been largely weak. So they are emboldened to stretch it further.

We should not lie down and let this happen. We voted the NDC into power. We did not give them the power to trample over us. The power is still with us. We must take all legal action to resist galamsey.

Ghana News.title: Mourinho keeps Clasico midas touch 13 years on as La Liga heats up
Ghana News.content:
Jose Mourinho has done it again.

The Real Madrid manager celebrated Kylian Mbappe's late winner at Barcelona on Sunday with a trademark knee slide, maintaining his Midas touch over their bitter rivals.

Mourinho has become just the third Real boss to go six El Clásicos in a row without defeat - 13 years after he last led Los Blancos in this fixture.

Four wins and two draws in his past six matches in charge of Real Madrid against Barcelona put him up there with Miguel Munoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003) as Real managers who have gone six in a row without defeat against the old enemy.

It was also just a second victory in eight games against Barcelona for Real, with the return of Mourinho to the fixture haunting the reigning champions

And more importantly for Mourinho, Mbappe's double in Real's 2-1 win ended Barcelona's nine-game unbeaten domestic run with a crucial Clasico victory at the Camp Nou.

A Real defeat would have allowed Barcelona to establish a commanding nine-point advantage but the result has transformed the top of La Liga, bringing Mourinho's side to within three points of their rivals.

"In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou, Real Madrid play to win La Liga," he said.

"We could win with luck, but we won with calmness and with all merit," he said. "It's a very strong group. Everyone works very hard. Everyone was ready to win.

"The credit goes to the players. When you win, the credit goes to the players. But when you lose, the blame falls on you. And that's why we see coaches being sacked from their positions every week."

The Portuguese, who returned to Real 13 years after his first stint in charge this summer, has now won six and lost six El Clasicos.

He said: "I've learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mindset to play.

"In midfield, having a mix of talents gives us more than just having two players with similar characteristics. This mix of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when we go on the attack.

"We've beaten several teams by four or more goals, but this is Barca, and the players put on a great performance. We need to continue like this and don't go over the moon after this win."

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said he didn't want to give excuses for the defeat but admitted his team lacked fresh legs after a demanding few weeks.

"We missed the freshness," he said. "It's not easy for our players. We have to recover well, train well and we have to respond from this defeat.

"In big games, small things are important and they decide the games and today, it wasn't on our side.

"I can see that today we were not fresh and this is what we have to change."

Ghana News.title: Courage Babanawo Kwabla elected Ketu South constituency Deputy Youth Organiser
Ghana News.content:
A nurse, Courage Babanawo, has been elected as the Ketu South Constituency Deputy Youth Organiser for the National Democratic Congress.

He recorded a convincing victory as his contender, Allah Thomas Kwame, polled 80 votes, representing 28% of the total votes.

Mr Babanawo’s message to build a stronger youth base for the party resonated well with the delegates, who gave him 205 votes, representing about 72% of the total votes in the constituency executives' election.

In an interview with Joy News, he assured of his readiness to serve, mobilise, and empower the youth at the grassroots level, stressing that the youth are the “backbone and driving force of the NDC”.

He believes that committing to building a stronger and more vibrant youth base would increase the party’s performance in the 2028 general election.

Mr Babanawo added that he would not relent in working with the other executives to strengthen party structures and ensure unity at every level of the party.

“I pledge to serve with loyalty, discipline, humility, and dedication. I will work closely with party leadership, executives, comrades, and all stakeholders to advance the fortunes of the NDC and deepen youth participation in party activities”, he added.

Mr Babanawo has served as Deputy Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) Organiser, Tamale Nursing and Midwifery Training College; TEIN President, Tamale Nursing and Midwifery Training College; Branch Communications Officer, Wuduoba LA Primary; Member, Communications Committee, Ketu South Constituency; Member, Special Operations Committee (Youth Wing), Ketu South NDC; and Communications Team Member, Volta Region.

Ghana News.title: MTN Yellow Ladies Network screens 500 market women for breast cancer
Ghana News.content:
The Yellow Ladies Network, a non-profit organisation made up of female staff of MTN, has organised a free breast cancer screening for 500 women in Accra as part of activities to mark this year's Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

The programme was used to educate women on maintaining healthy breasts.

Speaking during the programme, MTN Ghana's Chief Finance Officer and Chairperson of the MTN Yellow Ladies Network, Antoinette Kwofie, said the network is extending its activities beyond staff welfare to impact communities through health interventions.

Madam Kwofie said the Yellow Ladies Network was established in 2025 to empower, inspire, and coach women within MTN, but it was not limited to staff; it also reaches out to customers and communities.

She said last year the network organized a fundraising walk and donated the proceeds to the Breast Cancer Unit of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and to Breast Care International.

She said this year's theme focuses on better outcomes through action, hence the decision to take screening to the community, particularly market women who hardly get time to visit hospitals." We thought we would come to the marketplace because as women, we always put ourselves last when it comes to healthcare," she said.

She said the outreach was designed to bring healthcare providers to the women, educate them, share survivors' experiences, teach self-examination and offer free screening.

She said early detection saves lives and the exercise sought to help women know their status and identify lumps that need further checks. No specific target was set, as the aim was to screen as many women as possible.

She said envoys were sent to market queens and beauticians' associations to mobilize participants, with doctors from various hospitals conducting the screening and referring cases that need further attention.

She expressed satisfaction with the turnout, noting that screening started at 8:00 a.m. and women had already formed long queues to be screened, indicating that many had overcome fear.

The President of Breast Care International and CEO of Peace and Love Hospitals, Dr Beatrice Wiafe Addae, who partnered MTN for the exercise, called for increased awareness to reduce fear, stigma and mortality.

She said many people still attribute breast cancer to witchcraft, leading women to prayer camps and delaying treatment.

She disclosed that over 5,000 Ghanaian women are diagnosed with breast cancer annually and over 2,300 die, but early reporting can reduce mortality.

Dr Wiafe Addae said breast cancer is not painful at the early stage, hence the need for monthly self-examination and education.

She said about 60 to 70 per cent of patients are diagnosed at stage three or four cancers, but detection at stages one and two allows for breast-conserving surgery.

She said risk factors include being a woman, family history, late childbirth, excessive alcohol intake, smoking including shisha, skin-lightening products, hair relaxers, lack of exercise and fatty diets.

She cautioned against cosmetic products without English labelling, noting some contain carcinogens, and called for financial support for patients, since screening and biopsy are not covered by health insurance. She proposed enrolling vulnerable breast and prostate cancer patients on the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty programme.

Ghana News.title: Businessman in court over alleged World Cup visa fraud
Ghana News.content:
A businessman has appeared before an Adenta Circuit Court for allegedly defrauding a colleague of US$3,000 and GH¢20,600.

Kwaku Duah allegedly collected the money and other items from the complainant under the pretext of securing United States and Canadian visas for him to attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Charged with defrauding by false pretences, Duah pleaded not guilty.

The court, presided over by Mrs Angela Attachie, admitted him to bail in the sum of GH¢60,000 with two sureties, one to be justified with landed property.

It also ordered him to deposit his passport with the court registry. The court adjourned the case to February 17, 2027.

Chief Inspector Maxwell Lanyo led the prosecution.

The facts presented to the court were that the complainant, whose name was withheld, was a businessman residing at Adenta, while Duah lived at East Legon Hills.

In March 2026, one John Teiko introduced Duah to the complainant as a friend who needed spare parts for his tipper truck.

The complainant supplied the parts, and the complainant made payment.

The prosecution said that after the transaction, Duah told the complainant that a top official of the National Sports Authority (NSA) had introduced his personal assistant, identified as Gyamfi, to help his clients secure US and Canadian visas to attend the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Duah allegedly told the complainant that each participant had to pay US$4,500, which he described as the NSA's official fee.

The complainant said he could raise only US$3,000, but Duah insisted that US$4,500 was required.

Prosecution said Duah later proposed an alternative arrangement: the complainant would supply four brake drums and four 22.5R tyres for his tipper truck, valued at GH¢18,300, in addition to paying a visa fee of GH¢2,300.

The complainant allegedly supplied the items and paid GH¢2,300 and US$3,000.

The prosecution said the complainant became concerned when the visa interview was delayed and questioned Duah, who allegedly took offence and stopped answering his calls.

The complainant subsequently reported the matter to the Adenta Police.

Investigations allegedly established that Duah had made a false representation, as he did not know anyone at the NSA and no visa interview had been scheduled for the complainant.

The court heard that Duah retrieved the complainant’s passport upon his arrest.

Ghana News.title: Northern Ashanti Mines seeks injunction to block government takeover of $110m mine investment
Ghana News.content:
Northern Ashanti Mines Limited Company has filed an injunction application seeking to stop a government takeover of its Konongo concession, warning that about $110 million in committed expenditure is at risk.

The application, filed at the Commercial Division of the High Court in Accra, seeks to restrain the Minerals Commission and the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources from taking possession of the mine or reallocating it to third parties.

The company wants the restrictions to remain in place until the court determines its challenge to the termination of its mining lease. The Attorney-General is also named as a respondent.

In a supporting affidavit, Administrative Manager Jonathan Adongo alleges that Minerals Commission officials, accompanied by military personnel, visited the mine on October 22, 2026.

He says they ordered the company, its staff and workers to vacate the mine, offices and residential accommodation by midday that day.

The company argues that any takeover before the court determines the legality of the lease termination would threaten its investment, equipment and operations.

“The threatened military takeover is imminent, and I humbly pray this Honourable Court to hear this application with urgency,” Mr Adongo states.

According to the affidavit, Northern Ashanti Mines is wholly Ghanaian-owned and was formerly known as Owere Mines Limited. It is redeveloping the historic Konongo Gold Mine in the Ashanti Region.

The company says it renewed its lease on February 2, 2023, for 13 years, covering about 125 square kilometres. It maintains that Parliament ratified the renewed lease, which runs until February 1, 2036.

It says it has committed capital and incurred expenditure exceeding US$83.34 million on the concession. It also recently secured a facility of more than US$30 million to develop a gold processing plant, which it describes as more than 50% complete.

The affidavit puts its committed expenditure at about US$110 million and says the company employs approximately 422 people directly and indirectly.

The dispute follows a termination notice dated April 30, 2026, issued by the Minerals Commission on behalf of the minister.

The notice, attached to the application, states: “Your company failed to remedy and/or refused to remedy the breaches which were served within the statutory and regulatory timeframe.”

Northern Ashanti Mines disputes that position. It says no notice of any breach was served and that it was given no opportunity to remedy alleged breaches or explain why its mineral rights should not be cancelled.

The company says it received no response to a letter from its lawyers dated May 4 and a petition dated May 20 seeking a review and reversal of the decision.

Its injunction application also seeks to prevent security deployments intended to enforce the termination and to stop the granting or transfer of mineral rights over the concession.

The company argues that a forcible takeover could endanger staff and surrounding communities, damage equipment and destroy exploration records and geological data.

It is asking the court to preserve its possession of the concession pending the final determination of its judicial review application.

Ghana News.title: Are California voters about to impose ‘world’s first’ tax on billionaires?
Ghana News.content:
Few places on the planet have as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state known for glamour, coastal mega-mansions, and being home to the rich and famous.

Now voters are about to decide whether the mega-rich among them - including media mogul Oprah Winfrey, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Skims cofounder and reality television star Kim Kardashian, and filmmaker George Lucas - should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare.

Proposition 40 aims to levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California's billionaires.

There are a little more than 200 such individuals in the state - but that hasn't stopped the measure from dividing leaders and causing some of its ultra-wealthy residents to flee. One billionaire businessman says he's brought jobs to California, but the proposition made him feel "a little bit like I wasn't wanted".

But the vote is also offering regular residents a voice on an issue that has roiled politics for decades.

"I believe this is the first billionaire tax - meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution," says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure's historic nature and how it could help even out California's wealth gap.

The state has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth-largest global economy, bigger than India and the UK. It is also home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.

Supporters of the measure argue it helps ensure the ultra-wealthy contribute their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.

Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" to massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of US President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.

"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she tells the BBC.

While the ballot measure has many supporters, including billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, it has faced fierce opposition from a range of figures, from billionaires to the state's liberal governor.

Google co-founder Sergey Brin has donated more than $100m to a political organisation that funds ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports.

California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could drive the wealthy out of the state and cut off crucial income tax revenue.

A September poll from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided.

The statewide ballot measure would need a majority of residents to approve it.

California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in the US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a "millionaires tax" - a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year.

While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now exist in only three European countries, Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs.

Niemietz believes wealth taxes are "more trouble than they are worth" because they create administrative burdens, suppress investment, drive capital flight and, in the end, raise little revenue.

In Norway, a local news organisation found that a wealth tax increase led more super-wealthy people to leave the country in 2022 than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Lula holds off far right with victory in Brazil presidential election
World.content:
Share Lula holds off far right with victory in Brazil presidential election on social media

Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s contentious presidential race, pulling off a remarkable comeback after a first-round loss that galvanised the country’s political right.

Around 9:13pm Brasilia time (00:13 GMT), Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court called the race for Lula, who had earned 51 percent of the vote. More than 51.49 million ballots were cast for the incumbent.

Bolsonaro, meanwhile, netted 48.68 percent of the vote, or 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates.

With his victory, Lula has made history. No other politician in modern Brazilian history has lost the first round of a presidential election, only to win the second round.

Still, the vote process was marred by allegations of voter suppression, after reports emerged that public transportation in some areas had been suspended.

Lula’s allies accused Bolsonaro’s supporters of reducing the transportation in a bid to dampen the president’s working-class base.

Heavy rains, meanwhile, affected southern areas considered to be Bolsonaro strongholds.

The campaigns of both Lula and Bolsonaro ultimately petitioned the Supreme Court for a voting extension. Polls across the country were kept open two hours later than expected, until 7pm Brasilia time (22:00 GMT).

Sunday’s victory means that Lula will retain the presidency of the largest country in Latin America, denying a crucial victory to the region’s right wing.

In recent years, right-wing leaders have swept presidential races in nearby countries like Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Bolivia and Ecuador. Many have ridden a wave of anti-incumbent energy and have enjoyed support from United States President Donald Trump, who returned to office in January 2025.



A former union leader for metalworkers, Lula — at age 80 — will be sworn in on January 5, 2027, when he will beat his own record as the oldest Brazilian president to take the oath of office since the country’s return to democracy.

His victory has earned him an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term in office.

Lula came into Sunday’s runoff as an underdog, however. While he narrowly led in pre-election, the first round of voting on October 4 showed him trailing Bolsonaro.

He earned 45 percent of the first round vote, compared to the right-wing senator’s 47 percent — both tallies short of the 50 percent needed to avoid a runoff.

But in the weeks since, Lula has rallied supporters around cost-of-living issues. He championed a constitutional amendment passed this month that shortened the Brazilian workweek, and he floated the possibility of providing free public transportation on weekends.

Having entered politics in the 1980s, during the twilight of the country’s military dictatorship, Lula has run for president seven times.

He won two consecutive terms from 2002 through 2010, as well as a third term in 2022, in what was the tightest race in modern Brazilian history up to that point.

His rival in that election, former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, is father to Senator Bolsonaro, his adversary in this race.

Jair Bolsonaro has since been sentenced to 27 years in prison for his role in plotting a coup plot following his loss to Lula.

Despite overseeing a decline in poverty and low unemployment during his third term in office, Lula has faced questions about his age, his ability to combat crime, and the country’s polarised political landscape.

An explosion of household indebtedness has also left many Brazilians feeling that their economic circumstances had worsened.

In September, Lula banned online gambling and sports betting apps, in a bid to address the issue.

While the victory over Bolsonaro cements Lula’s status as one of the most significant and influential figures in Brazil’s modern history, efforts to advance legislative priorities during his fourth term could be stymied by the most right-wing Congress in recent memory.

World.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Can Barcelona phenom Lamine Yamal become youngest winner?
World.content:
While still a teenager, Yamal could surpass Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazario, who won the Ballon d’Or at the age of 21 in 1997.

Share After World Cup triumph, can Lamine Yamal add Ballon d’Or to his trophies? on social media

A once-in-a-generation talent. A superstar in the making. Equal parts audacious and ambitious.

Those are just a few words that best encapsulate Lamine Yamal’s appeal.

Since making his first-team debut three years ago, Yamal has taken world football by storm, compelling fans and players alike to take note of his talent.

His flair on the football field and flamboyant personality off it have made Yamal one of the sport’s best showmen in recent years.

Now, the 19-year-old has set his sights on another big prize to add to his glittering cabinet – the Ballon d’Or, football’s most prestigious individual honour.

No teenager has won the Ballon d’Or in the award’s 70-year history – Yamal is campaigning to become the youngest winner.

So, how does his bid compare with the other leading contenders? Al Jazeera breaks it down:

Yamal’s double – World Cup with Spain and La Liga with Barcelona

Very few players can boast such an impressive season as Yamal’s.

In 2025-26, the winger won the FIFA 2026 World Cup with Spain, only days after his 19th birthday. His success in North America came on the back of his La Liga title triumph with Barcelona.

While an injury-marred campaign meant Yamal did not dazzle viewers on his World Cup debut, grabbing just one goal and an assist, the youngster enjoyed far more success on club duty.

Yamal racked up 22 goals and 15 assists in 38 league appearances, playing a major role in Barcelona’s successful title defence. He was also part of the Catalan club’s Spanish Super Cup-winning squad.

Yamal matches Mbappe’s boast: ‘I deserve to win’

The major double of a world title and a domestic title has strengthened Yamal’s claim for the Ballon d’Or.



According to bookmakers, he is among the top three contenders, alongside Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane and Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe.

The 2026 Ballon d’Or race is the closest in decades. But Yamal is quite confident of winning the award, singling out Mbappe as his only threat.

“For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” the winger said in an interview on Movistar Plus.

“I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won,” he added.

This self-promotion by footballers is a relatively recent development in a team sport where, until a few years ago, the top individual prize went largely unnoticed until it was time to present it.

But now, the Ballon d’Or dominates football conversations during the following season, and the award, despite carrying no cash prize, brings greater status and worth.

Barca manager Hansi Flick said although he would have preferred Yamal not to have spoken about it, he accepts it as part of the winger’s self-belief.

“He’s exceptional, and it’s a part of this … I would not prefer this, but he’s doing this. He has self-confidence; he wants to win the Ballon d’Or.”

Nominated for the third time, Yamal finished runner-up to Ousmane Dembele of PSG in the 2025 Ballon d’Or race.

Yamal vs Mbappe vs Kane

Monday’s ceremony in London is likely to revolve around a three-way battle between Yamal, Mbappe and Kane. It is an interesting contest between three players in three different stages of their careers: one in his teens, one in his 20s and one in his 30s.

While Yamal has publicly pitted himself against Mbappe in the battle, he is confident that the trophies in his portfolio will help him beat the Frenchman, who has had no luck with silverware.

However, purely on an individual basis, Mbappe’s statistics are far better than Yamal’s.

Yamal had 25 goals and 20 assists for club and country. Mbappe, on the other hand, had a staggering 58 goals and 13 assists. The 27-year-old also finished the season as La Liga and Champions League top scorer, lifted the World Cup’s Golden Boot and broke the all-time goals record with 22.

Then there is the unstoppable force of Kane, who was in a league of his own. His 73 goals last season were the best haul by a footballer since Lionel Messi’s 82 in 2011-12.



So while Yamal has the shiny trophies to vouch for his Ballon d’Or bid, his solo displays pale in comparison with his seniors, Mbappe and Kane.

Kane’s incredible goal-scoring prowess – even at the age of 33 – is hard to ignore, but Yamal believes simply registering the maximum goals cannot be the criterion for the prize.

“The Ballon d’Or should go to the best player in the world, full stop,” he said. “Not to a player who has scored 80 goals, because if you score 80 goals, you get the top scorer award for that,” Yamal added, seemingly taking a dig at Kane.

“Those are two completely different things that people do not understand.”

Yamal’s fate now lies in the hands of a jury of journalists from 100 countries whose votes will decide whether he can become the youngest Ballon d’Or winner, surpassing Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazario, who was 21 at the time of his triumph in 1997.

After lifting the Kopa Trophy for the best Young Talent of the year twice, Yamal will hope the third time is the charm, this time stepping up to the biggest stage to bring home the ultimate individual trophy.

World.title: Thousands protest in Prague against public media funding reforms
World.content:
Several thousand people have taken to the streets in Prague to protest against plans to change the funding system for the Czech Republic’s public media, accusing the government of stifling press freedom.

On Sunday, protesters demanded the withdrawal of legislation seeking to abolish household licence fees and replace them with state budget allocations for public radio and television.

The Czech lower house of parliament approved fast-tracking the bill in a rare overnight vote on Saturday after governing coalition lawmakers rushed to open the issue, limiting the opposition’s ability to engage in debate before the vote was held.

The bill, proposed by the governing coalition led by billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis, which includes two far-right parties, must still be passed by the upper house before becoming law.

The opposition has pledged to challenge the legislation in the constitutional court. The plan would cut funding for public media by about 15 percent, possibly as early as next year.

At the protest in Prague’s Old Town Square, demonstrators chanted, “We’ve had enough”, “This must not be allowed to pass”, and “4:36”, referencing the early morning hour when the draft was approved by parliament.

Babis has said the plan is not an attack on media independence but a matter of funding transparency.

Critics warn the proposed change would allow the governing coalition to take control of the media. They compare it with the actions of populist governments, such as Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban and Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico.



Babis and his coalition, whose agenda includes reducing support for Ukraine as it fights off a Russian invasion, have a record of attacks against the media.

Public media staffers announced they would go on strike on November 3. They are backed by labour unions, university rectors, churches, international media organisations and many others.

A rally is also planned at Prague’s Letna park on November 15, two days before the anniversary of the 1989 anti-communist Velvet Revolution that ended more than 40 years of totalitarian government.

World.title: Bulgaria election heads to a run-off amid low voter turnout
World.content:
Bulgarians will now choose between President Iliana Yotova and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov next week.

Bulgaria’s presidential election is heading to a run-off after polls closed with low voter turnout and no candidate passing the required threshold.

Incumbent President Iliana Iotova received between 35 and 36.5 percent of votes on Sunday, according to exit polls. She will now face former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, who scored between 31 and 33.5 percent, in a second round on November 1.

Minister of Interior Ivan Demerdzhiev said the elections “took place peacefully, without the usual practices of vote buying and vote manipulation”, Bulgarian National Television reported.

The NATO and European Union member state saw 27 presidential candidates run in the election.

A run-off was expected, as turnout must reach more than 50 percent of registered voters, and the candidate must secure more than 50 percent of the votes to win in the first round.

Voter turnout was 22.2 percent as of 8pm local time (18:00 GMT), according to the Measure polling agency.

Black Sea attacks

Rising energy costs, inflation, attacks in the Black Sea and Russia’s war in Ukraine were the major issues in the lead-up to the vote.

A series of drone strikes on ships off Bulgaria’s coast, condemned by both candidates, dominated headlines during the campaign period.

Leftist Iotova is backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev, whose Progressive Bulgaria party enjoyed success in April’s parliamentary elections. Iotova became president in January after serving as vice president.

A former member of the European Parliament and a journalist, she ran as an independent with the backing of both Progressive Bulgaria and the Socialist Party.



Should she win, she is expected to keep Bulgaria in line with Europe, while calling for improved relations with Russia.

After casting her vote, Yotova said she wanted to address “the dire issue of poverty” in Bulgaria, as well as “inequalities and regional disputes”, the AFP news agency reported.

“I believe that there must be peace, stability, and security,” she added.
