Ufochukwu conveyed the fraternal greetings of President Bola Tinubu to Christodoulides and expressed her commitment to advancing relations between Nigeria and Cyprus throughout her tour of duty.



In welcoming the Nigerian envoy, Christodoulides reaffirmed the longstanding friendship between the two countries, which he said was rooted in shared historical experiences, common principles and enduring people-to-people connections.



He also acknowledged Nigeria’s strategic importance in West Africa and across the African continent, particularly its contributions to regional dialogue, cooperation, integration and stability.



The Cypriot president said his government was prepared to work closely with Nigeria to expand bilateral engagement, identifying the economy, trade, investment, education and political dialogue as priority areas.



He added that both countries could strengthen cooperation in addressing common challenges through bilateral and multilateral engagements.



The pledge comes amid efforts to translate diplomatic goodwill into practical partnerships capable of delivering economic and educational opportunities for citizens of both countries.



For Nigeria, stronger engagement with Cyprus could provide additional avenues for commercial cooperation, educational exchanges and improved engagement with Nigerians living on the island.

It could also create opportunities for Cypriot businesses to explore investment prospects in Africa’s largest economy.



However, translating the renewed diplomatic commitment into tangible benefits will depend on sustained engagement between officials, businesses, educational institutions and other stakeholders in both countries.



The presentation of credentials is a formal diplomatic requirement that authorises an ambassador to represent his or her country in the receiving state and officially undertake diplomatic functions.



Senior Cypriot government officials and members of the Nigerian diplomatic mission attended the ceremony.



Ufochukwu is expected to engage Cypriot government officials, business leaders and members of the Nigerian community as she begins efforts to strengthen bilateral relations.



Her accreditation signals a renewed opportunity for Abuja and Nicosia to build on their longstanding friendship and pursue practical cooperation in trade, investment, education and other areas of mutual interest.

World.title: Okonjo-Iweala’s Mother Dies at 96
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

The Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom in Aniocha South Local Government Area of Delta State has been thrown into mourning following the death of Professor Kamene Okonjo, mother of the kingdom’s traditional ruler, Obi (Dr) Ifechukwude Anishi Okonjo II, and Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.

The renowned sociologist and matriarch of the Umu Obi Obahai Royal Family died on Friday at the age of 96.

She was the wife of the late Obi (Professor) Chukwuka Okonjo, the immediate past traditional ruler of Ogwashi-Uku, with whom she shared 66 years of marriage.

The Palace Secretary, Prince Ifeakanachukwu Emordi, in a statement yesterday, said the royal family was mourning an exceptional woman whose life was marked by intellectual brilliance, humility, compassion and commitment to humanity.

He described the late Professor Okonjo as an internationally recognised sociologist who distinguished herself through her academic achievements, intellectual contributions and lifelong advocacy for women’s rights and empowerment.

“She was a woman of exceptional intellect, yet possessed a rare gentleness of spirit, humility and grace that endeared her to everyone privileged to know her,” he said.

The Palace Secretary noted that her achievements transcended Ogwashi-Uku and Nigeria, earning her international recognition and respect within academic and intellectual circles.

He described her as an embodiment of scholarship, womanhood, motherhood and service to society.

Beyond her professional accomplishments, Prof. Okonjo was a devoted mother, grandmother and great-grandmother, as well as a pillar of the royal family.

The Palace Secretary added that her wisdom, kindness, quiet strength, and exemplary character would remain an enduring source of inspiration for future generations.

“While we mourn her passing, we celebrate a life exceptionally well lived,” he added.

He maintained that the deceased left a lasting legacy of scholarship, service, family values, and advocacy for the dignity and advancement of women.

The royal family expressed confidence in its Christian faith, saying it drew comfort from the belief that she was resting peacefully with the Lord after completing her earthly journey with grace and distinction.

The family also extended its condolences to the reigning Obi of Ogwashi-Uku and to the deceased’s children, including Dr. Okonjo-Iweala, Dr. Njideka Okonjo-Udochi, Prince Onyema Okonjo and Prince Chichi Okonjo, as well as their spouses, grandchildren, great-grandchildren and the wider Okonjo family.

He urged the people of Ogwashi-Uku to join the royal family in celebrating the late professor’s life and legacy.

World.title: 2027 Re-election Campaign: Tinubu Appoints Keyamo to Head APC’s Directorate of Air Mobilisation
World.content:
– NAMA, FAAN MD’s named deputy directors

Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has appointed the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, to head the Directorate of Air Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 re-election campaign, placing him at the helm of one of the campaign’s strategic operational structures.

Under the new arrangement, Keyamo will serve as Director of the Directorate of Air Mobilisation, with the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku, appointed Deputy Director 1, while Engr. Farouk Ahmed Umar will serve as Deputy Director II.

Keyamo, in a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood, noted the appointments underscore the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to the organisation of a nationwide presidential campaign in a country as geographically extensive as Nigeria.

According to it, The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is expected to play a crucial role in coordinating the campaign’s air-movement requirements, facilitating travel arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and ensuring effective planning for air transportation in support of campaign activities across the six geopolitical zones of the country.

The statement added that given the scale of the 2027 presidential campaign, the directorate is expected to work closely with other relevant campaign structures to promote seamless coordination, operational efficiency and effective deployment of available logistical resources, subject to applicable aviation regulations and electoral laws.

Keyamo’s appointment, it further read, brings to the campaign structure the experience of a serving aviation minister who has been at the forefront of policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major aviation hub in Africa.

His familiarity with the operational demands of the aviation industry is expected to provide useful leadership in coordinating the directorate’s activities and establishing an effective framework for air-mobilisation planning.

The appointment of Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku and Engr. Farouk Ahmed Umar as Deputy Directors also brings aviation-sector leadership and technical experience into the directorate, strengthening its capacity to address the planning and coordination demands associated with nationwide campaign movements.

Air transportation is an important component of national campaign logistics, particularly where campaign leaders and officials are required to cover multiple locations within compressed schedules.

The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is therefore expected to support the broader campaign organisation through structured planning, coordination with relevant stakeholders, efficient scheduling and appropriate logistical arrangements.

Its effectiveness will depend on collaboration with other campaign directorates, clear operational procedures and strict compliance with aviation safety requirements and all applicable laws governing political campaigns.

The directorate’s activities will also be expected to maintain a clear distinction between campaign operations and official government functions, ensuring that campaign-related arrangements are undertaken through properly authorised channels.

President Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign is being organised through the APC Presidential Campaign Council, which brings together political leaders and designated directorates to coordinate the party’s preparations for the forthcoming general election.

World.title: Cats to burps: The Kiffness trolls President Trump [video]
World.content:
The Kiffness has spoofed President Donald Trump's burp. Images via YouTube screenshot

The Kiffness has done it again with another catchy jingle after by putting his unique spin on viral sound – this time poking fun at President Donald Trump burping mid-sentence.

The quirky artist has amassed millions of views with his samples of everything from animal sounds to singing children.

THE KIFFNESS TROLLS TRUMP’S BURP

The Kiffness’s latest music offering has poked fun at viral video of President Donald Trump burping mid-sentence.



The US leader was speaking at a campaign rally in South Carolina, in which he supported a local senator.

During his address, the 80-year-old appeared to loudl belch. Without excusing himself, he continued talking.

The video quickly went viral with many expressing disgust and concern.



Adding his spin was Cape Tow muso, The Kiffness who managed to turn the president’s ill-mannered actions into a catchy tune.

The “remix” was posted on Facebook, receiving hundreds and thousands of views, and almost 10 000 comments.

EATING THE CATS

It’s not the first time, The Kiffness has spoofed comments made by Trump.



Last year, the outspoken muso raised nearly R2 million for an SPCA shelter in the US from the proceeds of his catchy song Eating The Cats, featuring the then President-elect.

The song sampled the incoming statesman’s viral comments about immigrants, particularly Haitian people, whom he claimed eat domesticated animals.

An official music video has over 14 million YouTube views and many more millions on other streaming sites.

World.title: Hot mama! Mapimpi’s wife shows off post-pregnancy glow
World.content:

Makazole Mampimpi’s wife, Sasha de Sousa has shown off her post-pregnancy glow after recently giving birth to their second child.

MAPIMPI BECOMES A DAD AGAIN!

The pretty brunette showed off her glam hair and makeup as she pouted for the camera.

The woman linked to the Bok confirmed news of her pregnancy; however, both she and the player have shied away from making their relationship public.

Sasha is a well-known content creator from Eswatini who uses the Instagram handle @swazisoil. She enjoys posting content about fashion, cooking and her corporate career.

World.title: Springbok WAG shares her top marriage tips
World.content:
Springbok WAG Marise Pollard, the wife of Handre Pollard, has shared her top marriage tips with the public.

The teen sweethearts wed in 2017 and have two young children together

SPRINGBOK WAG MARISE POLLARD SHARES MARRIAGE ADVICE

On her TikTok account, Marise Pollard opened up about how she made her marriage to rugby star Handre Pollard work.



The mommy-influencer revealed that their relationship had been challenged by spending long periods apart and raising young children together.

However, through commitment and effort, Marise shared how they could overcome any obstacle.

“My marriage is something I take a lot of pride in”, she shared.

The brunette went on to share her best marriage advice, particularly for new moms, which included spending one-on-one time together, communicating clearly, and showing each other appreciation.

Take a look…

#motherhood #mom #foruyou ♬ original sound – Marise Pollard @marise.pollar02 Marriage after kids looks different, but I truly believe that doesn’t mean it has to change for the worse. 🤍 I’m no marriage expert, but one thing I’ve learnt is that a happy marriage doesn’t just happen.
