World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: As Ebola Spreads to 8th DR Congo Province, Families Battle to Feed Themselves
World.content:
A health worker carries a stretcher into an Ebola treatment centre in the DR Congo.

Geneva — Hunger in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) is undermining efforts to combat Ebola as the deadly disease has expanded across borders and also to an eighth province of the huge central African country, the UN said on Friday.

Families facing Ebola in the DR Congo, which has a population of more than 105 million, can find that protecting themselves from the virus can also mean losing the means to feed their children, according to the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP).

“Today, the outbreak has spread to an eighth province, reaching communities already under immense pressure,” David Stevenson, the WFP's DRC country director, said during a UN press conference.

“As it spreads, hunger continues to undermine the measures needed to contain it.”

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

And earlier in the week, the World Health Organisation (WHO), on Oct. 20, said that Nigeria has confirmed one imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

It became the fifth country to detect the virus since the DRC declared an outbreak on May 15.

The spread of the disease comes as agencies fighting the escalating Ebola virus in the DRC constantly battle to win the trust of local communities, according to international groups in the field calling for the protection of health workers.

Stevenson said that the WFP has two critical roles: helping families seek care without sacrificing food and providing the logistics backbone that keeps the wider response moving.

“Without sustained support, we risk leaving families unable to follow health guidance when it matters most.”

The WFP official explained that in Ituri’s Mungbwalu, the epicentre of the outbreak, Francine Birungi Amoti has lost a child to Ebola.

“She is raising her six surviving children and another baby entrusted to her care. Violence has cut her off from her fields.

“She told me, ‘If you go, you may not even return alive, and I do not have money to buy food at the local market. So we stay at home, and WFP helps us enormously.’”

For Francine, food assistance means feeding the children in her care when reaching her fields could cost her life.

'INSECURITY AND HUNGER'

“This is what a crisis on top of a crisis looks like: disease and bereavement, compounded by insecurity and hunger,” said Stevenson.

He also cited the case in North-Kivu’s Butembo, where Isabelle Kyakimwa arrived at an Ebola treatment centre without strength.

“As she recovered, she told us: ‘Food is important for us as patients because it helps us regain the strength to keep going.’

Close 

Her words show what food assistance brings to a treatment centre: regular, safe, nutritious meals that support recovery, dignity, and continuity of care.

“Food does not treat Ebola. Medical teams do,” said Stevenson.

“But their work takes place amid severe food insecurity and continued violence that repeatedly displaces families, destroys livelihoods and complicates access to care.”

He said food assistance is vital to supporting patients through that care and that WFP needs $115 million over the next six months, including $79 million for hot meals and dry rations.

World.title: Kenya: Calls for Penalties Follow 12-Story Building Collapse
World.content:
A building under construction collapsed in the Eastleigh neighborhood of Nairobi.

Nairobi — Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has called for tougher penalties against rogue developers and the restoration of prosecutorial powers to county governments following the collapse of an incomplete 12-storey building in Eastleigh.

Sakaja said weak penalties for violating construction regulations undermine enforcement efforts and allow developers to compromise building safety, putting lives at risk.

Speaking as he led multi-agency rescue operations at the site along 1st Avenue, 9th Street, the Governor urged professional bodies representing architects, engineers and quantity surveyors to take action against developers who dismiss qualified experts after obtaining construction approvals.



He said some developers engage licensed professionals to secure approvals but subsequently remove them from projects and proceed with construction using unqualified personnel, undermining safeguards intended to ensure buildings meet approved designs and safety standards.

"We have formally written to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, and we hope our request will be considered. Counties must be empowered to take firm action against rogue developers who disregard building regulations and put lives at risk," Sakaja said.

The Governor questioned the deterrent effect of existing penalties, noting that some developers found guilty of violating construction regulations could face fines as low as Sh5,000.

"Even when such offenders are arrested and taken to court, the penalties can be as low as Sh5,000, which is not a sufficient deterrent," he said.

Sakaja argued that restoring prosecutorial powers to county governments would strengthen enforcement and enable authorities to take firmer action against developers who disregard approved construction plans and safety requirements.

He called on professional associations representing architects, engineers, quantity surveyors and builders to collaborate with county governments in identifying and investigating cases where qualified professionals are withdrawn from construction sites under questionable circumstances.

The Governor said the bodies should take appropriate disciplinary action against professionals found culpable, adding that experts responsible for building design, supervision and safety must be allowed to discharge their duties without interference.

Sakaja also reiterated the need for developers to obtain occupation certificates before putting buildings into use. He said structures must undergo the necessary inspections to establish that they are safe and fit for occupation.

According to the Governor, developers are required to secure county approvals, engage qualified professionals and sign indemnity forms committing them to comply with approved plans and construction standards.

However, he said some developers disregard these commitments after obtaining approvals, compromising the integrity of construction projects.

The calls for stronger enforcement came after an incomplete 12-storey building collapsed in Eastleigh, triggering a multi-agency search and rescue operation amid fears that people were trapped beneath the rubble.

The building was still under construction, with the ground floor occupied at the time of the collapse.

Nairobi City County emergency response teams were coordinating operations alongside the National Disaster Operations Centre, the Kenya Red Cross, the Kenya Defence Forces and other agencies.

Heavy machinery had been deployed to clear debris and create access to sections where victims could be trapped, as additional resources were mobilised to support the rescue effort.

Sakaja urged families and members of the public with information about missing persons to report to designated centres established by rescue teams at the scene.

Close 

Residents were also advised to share information through the county's emergency hotlines, 1508 and 1199.

"Our health teams are on standby to provide immediate medical attention and support rescue efforts as soon as victims are reached. We are doing everything possible to ensure the operation proceeds as quickly and safely as possible," he said.

The collapse has renewed scrutiny of building safety enforcement in Nairobi, particularly compliance with approved construction plans, the engagement of qualified professionals and inspections at different stages of development.

Sakaja said stronger legal powers, tougher penalties and closer collaboration between county governments and professional bodies were necessary to hold developers accountable and prevent similar incidents.

He maintained that restoring county prosecutorial powers would complement existing inspection and enforcement mechanisms by strengthening the ability of local authorities to pursue violations of construction regulations.

World.title: Rwanda: Kagame Defends Strict Dress Codes Amid Rwanda's Dressing Controversy
World.content:
Rwandan President Paul Kagame has defended cultural expectations on dressing, arguing that societies have their own standards of acceptable behaviour which should not be abandoned simply because other countries embrace different ways of life.

Speaking on Thursday while addressing more than 10,000 young Rwandans at BK Arena in Kigali during the "Meet The President" session, Kagame said dress codes should be understood within the context of the places people visit and the values of the society in which they live.

"If you are going to the beach, by the water, where people go to relax, there is a certain way you can dress and behave that may be different from other places. That is perfectly acceptable. But imagine someone coming here dressed as though they were at the beach. Would that work? Wouldn't you all turn around and wonder, what happened to this person?" Kagame asked.



His remarks come amid a growing debate in Rwanda over restrictions on women's dressing, following incidents in which women have faced scrutiny over their clothing in public spaces.

The debate intensified after a video circulated showing police officers forcefully handcuffing a young woman wearing a miniskirt at a bus park in Rubavu.

The Rwanda National Police subsequently cleared the woman of wrongdoing and detained the officers involved pending disciplinary review.

The incident also drew criticism from human rights advocates and public commentators, who argued that cultural values should not be used to justify police intimidation, harassment or arbitrary enforcement of dress standards against women.

Addressing the wider debate, Kagame said the expectations should apply to men as well, arguing that discussions about dressing are often unfairly directed at women.

"By the way, this is not just about women. Most of the time, these things are made to be about women, but the same applies to men. Even now, imagine we are sitting here, and a man suddenly walks in, as though he has just come from the gym, wearing shorts, with nothing on his upper body, and comes to sit among us. People would ask, what happened to this person? Did he forget where he was going?" he said.

Kagame argued that societies should be allowed to maintain their own social standards rather than adopt practices from other countries without considering whether they fit local values.

He said people's willingness to participate in a particular social setting could also depend on the expectations established by those organising it.

"Now, if we had all agreed to come dressed that way, then perhaps that is how it would be. But some people would not come. Isn't that so? Some would simply decide not to attend, saying, we are not going to be part of that," he said.

The Rwandan leader said communities have ways of regulating behaviour through shared expectations and self-regulation, adding that practices accepted elsewhere should not automatically be embraced by Rwandans.

"There is a way society regulates itself, including through self-regulation. But when you simply say, we have seen this elsewhere, so let us do the same here, and you bring it into our society, society may tell you, we have not reached that point yet. Perhaps we were moving in that direction, but we are not there yet," Kagame said.

He called for disagreements over cultural values to be handled through dialogue rather than hostility, saying people should be able to reach an understanding when differences emerge.

"That should not create any hostility. There should be a way of regulating these things so that people can come to an understanding," he said.

Kagame compared society's response to unfamiliar practices to the body's reaction to a foreign object, which it gradually attempts to remove.

"It is like a foreign body. I think those of you in the medical profession know this. When a foreign object, a fragment of something, enters the body, the body tends to reject it. It keeps pushing it out. Even when a thorn gets stuck in your skin, if you leave it there for some time, it begins to work its way out. Eventually, you find it near the surface and remove it. Society works in much the same way," he said.

He added that tensions can arise when individuals seek to introduce practices that conflict with the established values of a community, while other members of that society resist the changes.

"A healthy society, with its own way of functioning, when something unfamiliar is introduced into it, gradually, little by little, that society begins to push it away. There is then a struggle between someone trying to change society to fit something they have brought from elsewhere, and society itself saying, do not bring these things here, and pushing that person away. But there should be no conflict. That is how these things should work," Kagame said.

Close 

He urged young people to reflect on the values they want for themselves and the direction in which they want their society to develop.

"Young people like you should keep these things in mind. Think about them. Understand what it is that you want for yourselves," he said.

Kagame also called for open discussions about changing social norms, urging young Rwandans to question practices that are becoming more common but which they consider inconsistent with their culture or harmful to society.

"Even here, in our discussions, people should be able to raise these questions and say, there are things we have seen becoming increasingly accepted in our society, yet they are not part of our culture. They do not even bring us any benefit. Why should we accept them, especially when they are things that harm people? Why?" he asked.

World.title: Nigeria: Ebola - FG Orders Strict Screening At Nigeria's Entry Points
World.content:
The Ministry of Health says the directive follows concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser over reported breaches of approved Ebola entry protocols.

The federal government has directed relevant agencies and health institutions to strictly enforce Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) screening and other entry protocols at Nigeria's designated points of entry following reports of non-compliance with approved measures.

The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) over reported breaches of the government-approved protocols.

The directive was contained in a circular dated 22 October and signed by the ministry's Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.



The ministry said consistent and non-discriminatory enforcement of the protocols was necessary to reduce the risk of cross-border transmission and protect public health and national security.

Screening, surveillance

Under the directive, relevant ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), health institutions and other stakeholders are required to comply with prescribed Ebola screening, health declaration, surveillance and other applicable entry requirements.

The ministry also called for stronger coordination, communication, and information sharing among the institutions responsible for implementing the measures.

It said these efforts would support effective disease surveillance, early detection and prompt responses to potential public health threats.

The directive comes as Nigerian health authorities respond to a confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), involving a woman who recently arrived in the country from Uganda.

The authorities have also begun contact tracing to identify people who may have been exposed to the virus.

Reporting breaches

The ministry directed relevant institutions to document and report any actual or attempted breaches of the approved protocols promptly through established channels.

It also urged them to support officials responsible for enforcing the measures and to establish monitoring and accountability mechanisms to sustain compliance.

Close 

The ministry stressed that personnel responsible for enforcement should be allowed to perform their duties professionally and without undue interference.

It further directed the immediate, widespread circulation of the advisory to relevant departments, units, field offices, and personnel to ensure they understood their responsibilities.

All concerned MDAs were instructed to treat the directive as a priority, promptly address identified lapses, and maintain compliance with the approved entry protocols.

The ministry said the measures were intended to safeguard public health and national safety.

World.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's Abiy Inaugurates Major Megech Irrigation Dam
World.content:
Gondar — Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project in Gondar, a major infrastructure development aimed at expanding agricultural production, improving water supplies and creating economic opportunities for surrounding communities.

The dam, with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, is expected to irrigate more than 17,000 hectares of farmland, directly benefiting tens of thousands of farmers, Abiy said in a statement posted on X.

"Today, we officially inaugurated the Megech Irrigation Dam Project, a major milestone for historic Gondar and its surrounding community," Abiy said.

The prime minister said the project had faced years of delays and implementation challenges before the government resolved obstacles to its completion through its Medemer development philosophy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Beyond agricultural irrigation, the dam is expected to provide reliable drinking water to Gondar and nearby towns, supporting efforts to improve access to essential services.

Abiy said the artificial lake created by the dam would also support fisheries, urban agriculture and tourism development, potentially generating employment opportunities for young people and stimulating economic activity in the region.

"The artificial lake will foster urban agriculture, large-scale fisheries, and tourism resorts, creating massive job opportunities for local youth," he said.

The inauguration forms part of Ethiopia's broader efforts to expand irrigation infrastructure, improve agricultural productivity and strengthen water resource management.

Abiy said sustained government monitoring had helped bring the long-delayed project to completion but acknowledged that Gondar required further development investment.

"Gondar still deserves much more development. I urge the public to actively participate in its development," he said.

The prime minister reaffirmed his government's commitment to ensuring that infrastructure investment and economic development benefit communities across Ethiopia.

"We remain dedicated to ensuring Ethiopia's progress is inclusive, benefiting all regions and citizens," he added.

Reporting by HornDiplomat News Desk)

World.title: Kenya: Eastleigh Collapse - Kalonzo Urges Probe Into Building Safety Failures
World.content:
Nairobi — Wiper Patriotic Front leader Stephen Kalonzo Musyoka has called for accountability over the collapse of an incomplete multi-storey building in Eastleigh, Nairobi, saying those responsible must be identified and held liable regardless of their positions or connections.

Kalonzo said the incident had raised serious questions about construction approvals, inspections and enforcement of building regulations, urging authorities to establish how a building of that size was allowed to stand and subsequently collapse in a densely populated neighbourhood.

In a statement issued on Friday, the former Vice President expressed dismay over the incident, noting that rescue teams were still searching for people reported trapped beneath the rubble.

"My prayers are with the families of those trapped and with the injured, as well as with everyone waiting for news of their loved ones," he said.



Kalonzo commended the Kenya Red Cross, the Kenya Defence Forces Disaster Response Battalion, the National Disaster Management Unit, Nairobi County emergency teams and members of the public who joined the rescue efforts.

He urged all agencies involved in the operation to coordinate their response without delay, emphasising the urgency of reaching those still trapped.

"Every minute counts, and I urge all agencies to work together without delay. I also urge members of the public to follow the instructions of the first responders," he said.

The Wiper leader also sent a message of support to those affected, praying for the recovery of the injured and the safe rescue of those still trapped in the collapsed structure.

"To the injured, we pray for a quick recovery. To those still trapped, we pray that help reaches you in time. To the families waiting, be strong. The nation is with you," he said.

Beyond the immediate rescue operation, Kalonzo called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the collapse, saying the public deserved clear answers on how the building was approved, inspected and constructed.

He said anyone found responsible for failures in the construction process should be held accountable, including those involved in approving or inspecting the building and those who may have ignored safety concerns.

"When the dust settles, Kenyans will ask how a building of this size came to stand, and fall, in a crowded neighbourhood. That question must be answered honestly," he said.

Close 

"Whoever approved, inspected, built or looked away must be identified and held to account, whatever their position or connections."

Kalonzo warned against allowing corruption and weak enforcement of construction laws to undermine public safety, insisting that Kenyans should not continue to lose their lives in preventable building disasters.

The statement adds to calls for greater scrutiny of construction standards and the enforcement of building regulations in Nairobi following the Eastleigh incident.

Authorities and emergency response teams were continuing search and rescue operations at the scene as concerns remained over people reported missing after the collapse.

Kalonzo concluded his statement by calling for comfort for affected families and strength for emergency personnel working to save lives.

"May God comfort the families and grant strength to all who are working to save lives," he said.

The Eastleigh building collapse has renewed questions about compliance with approved construction plans, the effectiveness of inspection systems and accountability for developers and officials responsible for ensuring buildings meet required safety standards.

World.title: Kenya: Nairobi Braces for Heavy Rains and Flash Floods
World.content:
Nairobi — The Kenya Meteorological Department has warned of heavy rainfall, flash floods and strong winds in dozens of counties, with the heaviest downpours expected between October 26 and 28.

In an advisory issued on October 23, the department said rainfall exceeding 20mm within 24 hours is expected in parts of the Coast, Northeastern region, the Highlands West and East of the Rift Valley, Central Highlands and Southeastern Lowlands from October 24 to 28.

Parts of Nairobi are among the areas expected to receive rain, alongside Mombasa, Kilifi, Kwale, Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Kisumu, Nakuru, Kiambu, Machakos, Kajiado, Meru and Nyeri, among other counties.

The department warned residents to remain alert for flash floods and poor visibility, noting that floodwaters can also occur downstream in areas that have not received heavy rainfall.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Residents in all the mentioned areas should remain vigilant for potential flash floods and poor visibility," the advisory stated.

The rains are also expected to be accompanied by gusty winds, with strong southerly to southeasterly winds exceeding 25 knots forecast in coastal, eastern and northern regions.

Ocean waves exceeding two metres are expected on Sunday, October 25, prompting a warning to people involved in maritime activities to exercise caution.

Residents have also been advised to avoid sheltering under trees or staying near grilled windows during storms because of the risk of lightning strikes.

The rainfall intensity is expected to reduce by October 30, according to the department, which said further updates would be issued if conditions change.

World.title: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Stresses for Stronger Indigenous Capacity to Drive National Development
World.content:
Addis Ababa — Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has emphasized for stronger domestic institutional and human capacity, improved coordination among government institutions, and the removal of systemic bottlenecks to accelerate Ethiopia's development.

Speaking at the inauguration of the Megech Irrigation and Water Supply Project in Gondar, the Prime Minister emphasized that sustainable national progress depends on strengthening local expertise and reducing reliance on external entities.

Located on the Megech River, a major tributary of Lake Tana in the North Gondar Zone of the Amhara Region, the project is designed to expand agricultural production, improve access to clean drinking water and stimulate economic activity.

With a storage capacity of 185 million cubic meters, the dam is expected to irrigate more than 17,000 hectares of farmland, benefiting tens of thousands of farmers.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

It will also provide a reliable supply of drinking water to Gondar and neighboring towns.

Beyond irrigation and water supply, the project is expected to create additional economic opportunities through urban agriculture, fisheries and tourism development, generating employment for local youth and supporting the regional economy.

Addressing the inauguration ceremony, PM Abiy stressed that building indigenous institutional and human capacity is essential to ensuring the effective implementation of development projects.

He cited the 19-year delay in completing the Megech project as an example of structural weaknesses that have hindered the timely delivery of public infrastructure.

He said the government had to replace the contractor and restructure the implementation process to bring the project to completion.

The Prime Minister identified delays and the accumulation of unfinished projects as major obstacles to national development, emphasizing the need to address the underlying institutional and administrative challenges.

He also underscored the importance of effective coordination between federal and regional governments, saying stronger collaboration and aligned implementation efforts are necessary to achieve shared development objectives.

PM Abiy further emphasized that development infrastructure belongs to the public and requires collective responsibility for its protection and proper use.

Close 

He urged residents of Gondar to take an active role in safeguarding the project and ensuring that its benefits are sustained.

Concluding his remarks, the Prime Minister highlighted the close relationship between peace and development, noting that Ethiopia's historical and civilizational potential can be fully realized only when stability and economic progress advance together.

World.title: Conservative wave hits roadblock in Brazil as Lula holds off Bolsonaro challenge
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Incumbent leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva narrowly defeated conservative Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro in Sunday's presidential runoff, according to The Associated Press. The deeply polarized nation returned to the polls for a second round runoff on Sunday.

Bolsonaro narrowly won the first round on Oct. 4, with 47% of the vote, to Lula's 45%, but fell short of the 50% majority required to win the election outright.

BRAZIL BECOMES NEXT TEST FOR LATIN AMERICA’S SURGING CONSERVATIVE MOVEMENT

The victory marks an unprecedented fourth presidential term for Lula, and a remarkable comeback victory. The result is even more surprising given that Bolsonaro had led, albeit by tight margins, in recent polling, and Brazil had recently elected a conservative congress aligned with the Bolsonaro agenda.

Earlier in the day, Lula voted in Sao Bernardo do Campo, Sao Paulo, while Bolsonaro voted in the north of Rio de Janeiro, the state he represents in the Senate.

The first vote tallies came in from Brazilians living overseas, where Lula won a decisive victory in Germany, and Bolsonaro won an overwhelming victory in Japan.

BRAZIL’S RAPID ELECTION COUNT PUTS SPOTLIGHT ON VOTING SECURITY AHEAD OF US MIDTERMS

While Bolsonaro performed well in his southern electoral strongholds, winning by comfortable margins in Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Paraná, and Rio Grande do Sul, he won those states by smaller margins than in the first round.

His turnout in the south was not enough to overcome Lula's famed Northeastern firewall; a reflection of the Workers Party dominance in the country's populous "Nordeste" region.

Bolsonaro also turned in a disappointing performance in Minas Gerais, which geographically and politically straddles the Brazilian north/south divide. Often referred to as the nation's quintessential bellwether state, it is fair to say that as goes Minas Gerais, so goes the nation.

While Bolsonaro won Minas Gerais by 5% in the first round, in the second round it was essentially tied.

Bolsonaro had received endorsements from other first round candidates: best-selling author Augusto Cury, former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema, and former Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado.

LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION

However, they were not enough to overcome the much-respected electoral machinery of the Workers Party. Lula has now appeared on the presidential ballot 7 times, winning 4 of those elections.

Heading into the first round, Flavio Bolsonaro was effectively able to make the case to working-class and middle-class voters that the Lula's economic approach was driving up their cost of living.

He painted the Lula administration as bloated, tax-heavy, and given to racking up debt and tied this to inflation and kitchen table economics.

Additionally, his message of hardline law and order appealed to a Brazilian public where voters routinely suggest that violence is the most pressing issue.

Nonetheless, these economic and security concerns were not enough to overcome a generation of loyalty to the Workers Party and its social programs, particularly in the North and Northeast of the country, where Lula won by wide margins.

While Lula will be riding high heading into a historic fourth term in office, he will face a Congress with a center-right and right-wing majority that has been described as one of the most conservative in history.

While Flavio Bolsonaro lost the 2026 election by a narrow margin, the Bolsonaro movement is certainly not going away, and arguably remains an influential force in modern Brazilian politics.

The Lula victory also brings to an end a long string of victories for Trump-backed right-wing candidates across the region. While Trump had not officially endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro, he made no secret of his preference, and enjoyed a close relationship with the Bolsonaro family.

Looking forward to 2030, all eyes will turn to Bolsonaro clan ally Tarcisio de Freitas, who stepped aside this election cycle, in order to clear the way for Flavio Bolsonaro's run. Will the Brazilian right back another Bolsonaro in four years time, or will the popular São Paulo governor also mount a bid?

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In addition to the presidential election, voters in five states, as well as the federal district of Brasília, were also selecting governors in runoff elections. Bolsonaro-aligned candidates appeared poised to win most of those races.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Todd Blanche challenges Dana Bash for only citing part of Constitution during heated election clash
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Attorney General Todd Blanche confronted CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday after the network highlighted only the first portion of the Constitution's Elections Clause during a heated exchange on "State of the Union" over the Justice Department's lawsuit concerning two candidates with similar names in Alaska's closely watched Senate race.

Blanche pushed back as Bash referenced the Alaska Supreme Court's earlier ruling allowing Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who shares a name with incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, to remain on the ballot. The attorney general demanded that CNN display the remainder of the constitutional provision, which grants Congress authority to make or alter regulations governing congressional elections.

"Conveniently, you put up the Constitution on your screen, but you highlighted only the first clause. Why don't you show the next clause to your viewers, which says that Congress is allowed to pass laws to make sure that that happens? Put that back up there," Blanche said.

BLANCHE WON'T RULE OUT DOJ BLOCKING ELECTION CERTIFICATION IN 'DOOMSDAY' SCENARIO

The exchange centered on Article I, Section 4 of the Constitution, which gives state legislatures authority to establish procedures for congressional elections while permitting Congress to enact or modify those regulations.

Blanche argued that the second half of the provision supports the federal government's intervention under existing federal statutes.

"The second clause says that the Congress may at any time by law, and we have a law, and that's the law that we're relying on when we filed suit earlier this week," Blanche said.

The Justice Department’s lawsuit relies on the National Voter Registration Act, arguing that allowing a candidate who, according to the DOJ, intends to confuse voters to remain on the ballot undermines election integrity. The complaint asks the court to delay election certification if votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. could alter the final outcome.

The DOJ's complaint accused the challenger of deliberately attempting to mislead voters by using a name similar to the incumbent's.

DOJ OFFICIAL DEFENDS TRUMP'S NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ON '60 MINUTES,' ACCUSES SHOW OF EDITING OUT HER ANSWERS

Media Research Center President David Bozell criticized Bash's presentation of the constitutional language in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing CNN of failing to provide viewers with the complete provision.

"An anchor who hands viewers half a provision on election integrity is running a magic act, and the trick fell apart on live television. Bash's job is to give the audience the full text up front. CNN owes its dozens of viewers the whole clause, and a better editor," Bozell said.

The DOJ lawsuit follows a June ruling by the Alaska Supreme Court allowing the challenger to appear on the ballot despite objections from state election officials. The court left the question of how his name should appear to the state's Division of Elections.

"Daniel J. Sullivan decided to run for Senator in 2026 as a Republican with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him," the complaint states.

BLANCHE ANNOUNCES CHARGES AGAINST 10 PERMANENT RESIDENTS ACCUSED OF MINNESOTA VOTER FRAUD

Republicans have accused the challenger, a retired teacher from Petersburg, of attempting to siphon votes from the incumbent. Daniel J. Sullivan has denied those accusations and maintained that his candidacy is legitimate.

President Donald Trump also addressed the controversy Friday while speaking to reporters in Florida, acknowledging that he personally encouraged the Justice Department to pursue legal action.

"I'm the one that said, do it," Trump said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The federal challenge faces opposition from voting rights groups and the campaign of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola, both of which filed motions to intervene in the case. The American Civil Liberties Union argued that the National Voter Registration Act establishes voter-registration procedures and does not authorize blocking election certification over candidate placement.

"Knots Landing" star Donna Mills is revealing the one unexpected request she refuses to fulfill for her OnlyFans subscribers.

"I do the Peloton," Mills said. "Just, you know, they’re the things of everyday life: having a cup of coffee, you know. They say they like it when you brush your teeth…I’m not going to brush my teeth."

DONNA MILLS DOES 100 SIT-UPS A DAY, PLAYS TENNIS FIVE TIMES A WEEK AT 85 BUT WON'T QUIT DORITOS

PLAYBOY'S CELEBRITY-DRIVEN RELAUNCH FACES CREDIBILITY TEST IN ONLYFANS ERA, EXPERT SAYS

CRYSTAL HEFNER FELT 'ABSOLUTELY BRAINWASHED' DURING HUGH HEFNER MARRIAGE, REVEALS STRICT PLAYBOY MANSION RULES

'HARRY POTTER' ACTOR SAYS ONLYFANS VIDEOS EARNED HER MORE THAN HER ENTIRE ACTING CAREER

DREA DE MATTEO SAYS ONLYFANS BECAME ‘POLITICAL STATEMENT’ AFTER FINANCIAL STRUGGLES THREATENED HER HOME

WHY WWE LEGEND DAWN MARIE IS HEADING TO ONLYFANS AT 55

Mills said fans were hungry for a behind-the-scenes look at her life, which she noted wasn't possible during her TV heyday.

'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS ISSUES URGENT WARNING ABOUT AGING

"They want to know me," she told Variety at the time. "They want to know what I do during the day when I’m home. They want to see my home. They want to know much more about my personal life than we ever experienced back in the ’80s and the ’90s that, you know, the fans were cut off from."

In an interview with Fox News Digital last month, Mills teased what fans can expect from her future content.

World.title: NFL's French national anthem performer Nina Tonji alters words to La Marseillaise, sparking outrage in France
World.content:
Words often matter as much as actions and amid the civil unrest that France has felt in recent days, some French people are apparently angry and offended over the altering of their national anthem before the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints.

And, yes, this has to do with immigrants in France.

Before the game, singer Nina Tonji performed La Marseillaise at the Stade de France. Although she received a warm round of applause afterward, there has been significant online backlash because she modified the lyrics of the song.

NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS

Tonji changed "Qu'un sang impur abreuve nos sillons!" to "Qu'un sang uni abreuve nos sillons!," and that was clearly done on purpose because it has political and societal ramifications.

"Qu’un sang impur abreuve nos sillons" means "May impure blood water our furrows/fields." In the revolutionary context of La Marseillaise, "impure blood" referred to enemies and traitors – particularly French immigrants fighting alongside foreign armies.

Replacing impur ("impure") with uni ("united") changes the meaning of the passage from from a call for enemy blood to nourish France’s soil into an appeal for national unity and solidarity that includes immigrants to nourish France's soil.

Tonji thus changed the song's tone from violent exclusion of a foreign enemy to a message of unity with foreigners.

She gave immigrants cover that La Marseillaise did not in 1792 when it was written during the French Revolution.

And, yes, this rendition represented a lyrical alteration by the Tonji that departed from the traditional wording of the French national anthem. But it comes at a time when people in France are on edge about immigration and foreigners.

That’s because at least some of the protesters who took to the streets during the past two weeks of civil unrest were immigrants. Some rallied for anti-Israel causes, while others called for the overthrow of the current political system.

So, predictably, there has been an online backlash.

This is where we also inform you that Tonji was born in Montreal, Canada.

Much of the attention she is now getting has come from media accounts with massive followings.

Cerfia posted the song to its 1.3 million followers and highlighted the changes made.

RMC Sport posted it to its 2.7 million followers, saying the change caused "confusion."

Francetvsport also posted the song to its 297,500 followers.

The replies to the viral posts did include some people willing to overlook the change. But a vast majority insulted everything from Tonji's voice, to looks, to the action itself, calling it a "scandal," and "disrespectful" and a "controversy."

Seems some French people have pride in their national anthem.

So here is a common sense approach the NFL should adapt to avoid these public relations black eyes – because the league gets a lot of coverage over national anthem performances that go awry.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The league, which supposedly has a right of refusal over these pregame and even halftime acts, can easily force the artists to sign binding contracts that demand they perform the songs as written.

Sure, interpret all you want, the league can tell the artists. That's what makes you an artist.

But don't alter lyrics to suit a personal agenda or feeling. Because that makes you an activist.

World.title: DAVID MARCUS: The future of the GOP in New England rides on Maine’s Senate vote
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The New England region of the United States comprises six states, more than 15 million people, 21 seats in the House of Representatives, and 12 senators. Yet, of this congressional delegation, only one is a Republican — Sen. Susan Collins of Maine — at least for now.

In the Pine Tree State, Democrat Troy Jackson has a slight lead in the polls. Over her 30 years in the Senate, Collins has pulled a lot of electoral footballs from Democrat Charlie Browns, who thought victory and a Senate seat were a chip shot away.

In Maine, I chatted with Republican State House Representative Laurel Libby — a rising star in the local GOP and possible heir to the kind of centrist Republicanism that Collins has managed to cling to in this mostly blue region.

Libby told Fox News Digital that "[Collins] is great on constituent services and goes out of her way to be in the community," adding, "it's kind of hysterical for Troy Jackson to say she doesn’t hold town halls. Susan Collins is out in the community constantly."

DAVID MARCUS: IN BLUE MAINE, NOBODY BELIEVES SUSAN COLLINS WILL LOSE UNTIL THEY SEE IT

I pressed Libby a bit on what role, especially if Collins holds on to win, the Maine and broader New England Republican Party can play in the post Trump era — which lies just over two years over the horizon. She replied, "I think we need to be providing the long-term solutions for Maine.

"We’ve seen what a Democrat trifecta [in state government] has done for Maine. During Jackson’s time in the Senate, he is responsible for our electricity costs going up 70%," she said. "He supported a budget that went up 50%."

VOTERS PREPARE TO WEIGH-IN ON TRUMP'S ECONOMY AS COSTS CONTINUE TO SURGE

These were concerns that I also heard from Don, a Vietnam veteran in his late 70s who recently moved into Bangor from a nearby farm after his wife passed away.

"All those Democrats south of [the state capital] Augusta, they just think everyone is made of money, and it's really hurting normal folks," Don said.

Among Republican voters in Bangor, and even some Independents, the word "Augusta," is generally uttered with approximately the level of disdain Jerry Seinfeld had when saying "Newman!"

Dan and Tess, a couple in their 30s, were in town from Massachusetts, of which Maine was once a part. They both see Collins as a strong centrist voice for the region.

"It's a problem when every politician in New England is a Democrat," Dan said. "Especially when the Democrats are out of power."

Chris, also from Massachusetts, was in Maine upgrading carrier lines. When asked what Republicans could do to get a foothold in the region, he said, "I don't really know, when the state's been Democratic [for so long]. ... Coming together to the people with things that don't pull sides apart, because they have two sides, but they're supposed to meet in the middle."

This is a point that Libby refined in our conversation when asked about the fact that Collins was campaigning this week with former moderate Democratic Senator Joe Manchin of West Virginia, while Jackson barnstormed with far-left New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

KYRSTEN SINEMA QUESTIONS WHETHER MODERATES STILL HAVE A PLACE IN THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"It’s absolutely representative of what they both [would] bring to the Senate," Libby told Fox News Digital. "Susan Collins has proven that she is willing and able to work in a bipartisan manner, to get things done, and during his time in the [state] Senate, did the opposite," including Libby claims a few end runs around the Maine Constitution.

Manchin is now out of power, mostly owing to his refusal to bow to the far left zeitgeist of the current Democratic Party. This is thus far a fate Susan Collins has avoided over the past decade when she distances herself from Trump and MAGA populism.

If Troy Jackson does manage to topple Collins, the message to Republicans in Maine and New England will be that centrism doesn’t work, that they need bare knuckle brawlers more like Rep. Brandon Gill of Texas, than bipartisan peacemakers like Collins.

Nationally, there are some hardcore Republicans who would welcome a Collins loss in this respect. They see moderate Republicans as more of an obstacle than an asset. But most in the GOP concede that holding the Senate for Trump’s final two years in office outweighs the broader ideological intraparty fights.

Win, lose, or draw for Collins, in the future it will be younger Republican politicians like Libby, who will have to define what a Republican is in Maine, New England, and to some degree in America as a whole.

Democrats exiled Joe Manchin for his lack of political purity; they are on the way to doing the same to Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., even though, somewhat hilariously, he really could wind up as the 51st vote in a one-seat Democratic majority next year.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

If Maine Republicans can save Susan Collins once again, it will show that the GOP really can, at least in part, and unlike Democrats, embrace moderate and centrist positions — a point that could play heavily in their favor as both parties try to define themselves for the post-Trump age.

World.title: Steve Hilton hits Dem governor's 2028 pitch by calling out Newsom's rail record
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Republican California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton challenged Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear's argument that a Democratic governor should lead the party's 2028 presidential ticket Friday on HBO's "Real Time with Bill Maher," pointing to California Gov. Gavin Newsom's unfinished high-speed rail project as Beshear touted Democratic governors' accomplishments.

Beshear, discussing potential Democratic presidential contenders, argued that governors could point to tangible accomplishments that would distinguish them from President Donald Trump.

"What Democratic governors have are receipts," he said. "You can look at, have you built the housing?"

"Have you built the high-speed rail?" Hilton asked.

BILL MAHER CLASHES WITH NEWSOM OVER CALIFORNIA LEADERS, SAYS OTHER SIDE WILL ASK, ‘HAVE YOU SEEN THE STATS?'

The exchange came after Maher raised Newsom as a potential 2028 contender, although the California governor has not formally announced a presidential campaign.

Maher acknowledged Hilton's point, suggesting the Republican candidate could use the project's troubled history against Newsom.

"You're going to have a field day with that. No, you're right," Maher said.

Matt Ciepielowski, Hilton's campaign manager, criticized California's continued investment in the project in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"If Andy Beshear thinks California’s high-speed rail is something to brag about, he should try buying a ticket. Billions spent, years behind schedule, and Californians still can’t ride it. Gavin Newsom’s answer is to keep pouring money into it."

Ciepielowski also said Hilton would end state funding for the project if elected governor.

"Steve Hilton will end state funding on day one," he said. "Californians are struggling to pay their own bills. They shouldn’t have to keep paying for Sacramento’s failures, too."

TRUMP BACKS HILTON AHEAD OF CALIFORNIA GOP VOTE, TESTING BIANCO’S GRIP ON PARTY ENDORSEMENT

California state Sen. Tony Strickland, R-Huntington Beach, vice chair of the Senate Transportation Committee, also criticized Newsom's handling of the project, pointing to findings about taxpayer-funded travel expenses submitted by project consultants.

"The high-speed fail should have been defunded when Newsom took office in 2019," he said. "Instead, he doubled down on a project that will never be built as originally proposed to Californians. The latest scandal involving project consultants' misuse of public funds to pay for luxury travel under Newsom’s watch is yet another slap in the face to California families struggling to pay for essentials like gas, food, and rent."

"These are taxpayer dollars, yet project consultants treat them like their personal ATM. This project will go down as one of the most wasteful government projects in California history," he continued.

LIZ PEEK: CALIFORNIA VOTERS FED UP WITH DEMOCRATS MAY TURN TO STEVE HILTON FOR CHANGE

California's high-speed rail system has faced years of delays and escalating costs since voters approved nearly $10 billion in bonds in 2008. An April estimate placed the cost of the full project at approximately $126 billion, compared with an original estimate of $33 billion. No high-speed track had been laid as of that report.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority said in its 2026 business plan that completing the initial Merced-to-Bakersfield segment would cost an estimated $35.7 billion, with passenger service targeted for 2033. According to the authority's financial records, approximately $15.7 billion had been spent through February.

The project's financial oversight also came under renewed scrutiny following a September investigation by California's independent high-speed rail inspector general. Investigators identified approximately $81,000 in consultant travel expenses that appeared to violate state regulations and another $543,000 that appeared impermissible under contract terms, with some overlap between the findings. Questionable charges included premium transportation and trips to gyms, a nightclub and an escape room.

The California High-Speed Rail Authority outlined corrective actions, including additional oversight, employee training and efforts to recover payments determined to be improper.

Despite the criticism, the California High-Speed Rail Authority has maintained that construction is advancing. In an October update, officials reported completing 66 major structures and nearly 90 miles of guideway in the Central Valley, while emphasizing the project's expected transportation, economic and employment benefits.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Fox News Digital reached out to Newsom and the California High-Speed Rail Authority for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

World.title: Stolen car slams into South Carolina home as teens bolt, authorities say
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A stolen car barreled through neighborhood yards and smashed into a South Carolina home before two teenagers ran, triggering a search involving deputies, K9 teams and a drone, authorities said.

Video released by the Greenville County Sheriff’s Office shows the car slamming into the house before deputies rush toward the wreck and chase a fleeing suspect.

"Is everybody alright?" a deputy can be heard asking as authorities check the home for anyone who might be hurt.

FOUR TEENS KILL COUPLE IN HEAD-ON CRASH AFTER STEALING G-WAGON, LEADING COPS ON HOURS-LONG CHASE: POLICE

The sheriff’s office said deputies attempted to stop the reported stolen vehicle around 2:30 p.m. Oct. 15. The driver fled, but deputies said they did not pursue the car before it crashed into the home on Renwood Road in Simpsonville.

Two teenagers, ages 15 and 16, were eventually arrested and charged with possession of a stolen vehicle, authorities said. No injuries were reported.

WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA

The video shows one deputy running after a fleeing suspect while another heads toward the damaged home. The passenger was quickly taken into custody, while the search for the driver brought help from above and on the ground.

K9 teams used multiple dogs to track the driver’s path, and drone operators provided an aerial view of the neighborhood, according to the sheriff’s office. The video also shows a dog picking up a scent collected from the vehicle before tracking the driver.

BLOODHOUND K-9 UNIT HELPS BRING GEORGIA MANHUNT TO END WITH ARREST OF SUSPECT ACCUSED OF SHOOTING WOMAN

"When someone decides to run from law enforcement in Greenville County, they quickly learn that our deputies have more than one way to find them," the sheriff’s office wrote in a post accompanying the video.

"You can run, but our deputies have a pretty impressive toolbox. And they know how to use it," the agency added.

For neighbors, the crash brought a frightening interruption to an otherwise routine afternoon.

"I was just putting my baby down for a nap, and I heard a big crash outside," next-door neighbor Rachel Bush told WYFF.

Just minutes earlier, Bush said, she had been walking outside with her baby and dog.

"We were grateful we were back inside before everything happened," she told the outlet.

DRIVER RELEASED WITHOUT CHARGES AFTER PICKUP KILLS BOY, 6, AND MAN ON KANSAS SOCCER FIELD

One of the home’s residents told WYFF that no one was home when the car crashed through the front door. He and his fiancé returned from an errand minutes later to find the damage.

World.title: Zelenskyy can leverage Moscow ties from comedy days to make peace deal, says former key aide
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's former spokesperson urged him Sunday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face in Moscow, arguing that his past business and political connections in the Russian capital from years back could help him negotiate a peace deal there.

Iuliia Mendel, who served as Zelenskyy's spokesperson from 2019 to 2021, told Fox News Digital that the former comedian had also made his first millions in Russia and should perhaps leverage those ties to pursue lasting peace.

"When Zelenskyy was an entertainer, he often performed in Moscow," Mendel said, adding that the Ukrainian president "knows a lot of people from Putin's elite."

"He actually professionally grew in Moscow and earned his first millions in Moscow, and today he pretends that he has nothing in common with them," Mendel said.

RECOVERING FROM LUNG SURGERY, POPE LEO URGES PUTIN TO AGREE TO CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIAN-HELD UKRAINE CITY

"He needs to go to Moscow and needs to agree on compromises that are acceptable," she said, before adding that Zelenskyy "doesn't need to play his maximalist games and to play this noble actor."

Mendel's criticism came as Ukraine, Russia and the United States prepared for another round of technical-level peace talks, potentially in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland, in November.

U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have helped lay the groundwork for renewed negotiations that officials hope could finally lead to direct talks between the two leaders.

Before entering politics, Zelenskyy had built a successful entertainment career. Beginning in the late 1990s, he performed with the comedy troupe Kvartal 95, competed on the Russian-language comedy program KVN and later worked as an actor, writer and producer in television and movies.

From the late 1990s, he performed on Russian stages and at private parties and appeared in movies shown across former Soviet republics, Mendel claimed.

She said that after Russia annexed Crimea and launched its war in Donbas in early 2014, Zelenskyy traveled to Russia to work on the comedy film "Eight New Dates" which was released in Russian theaters in 2015.

ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE

According to a report by Business Insider, many of Zelenskyy's movies were also in Russian and were marketed to a Russian audience, David Dodson, an American movie editor who worked with Zelenskyy told the outlet.

"He was a well-loved comic, actor and performer in Russia, but after [the 2013-14] Maidan [Revolution], everything changed," Dodson said.

"People need to realize that Volodya’s movies were very big in Russia. Most of his market was in Russia. He’s always been a popular comedy star in Russia," Dobson also clarified to GQ when asked if he directed the former actor in "Eight First Dates" in Russia, released in 2012.

In 2013, the movie received the Russian National Movie Awards as the Best Russian Comedy of the Year.

In 2019, Zelenskyy also promised to relinquish ownership of a Cyprus-registered company operating a film studio in Russia after investigative journalists revealed that he and his business partners still owned three Russian companies, according to the Kyiv Post.

Zelenskyy's entertainment career made him a household name in Ukraine and other former Soviet republics before he entered politics and won Ukraine's 2019 presidential election with roughly 73% of the runoff vote on promises to fight corruption and pursue peace in eastern Ukraine.

Mendel argued that Zelenskyy's promise to bring peace at the time stands in stark contrast to the devastating war that has crippled the country and defined much of his presidency.

TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE

"Zelenskyy became the president with 73% record support," Mendel said. "Because he promised to bring peace to Ukraine."

"And now he has been presiding for almost five years (over) the largest war in Europe since World War II. This shows a lot."

"When his country is bleeding, he needs to make a peace deal for his people," she said before adding that the leader "needs to put the interests of his people first, just for Ukraine to exist as an independent state."

Whether Zelenskyy should travel to Moscow has, in fact, become a flashpoint in efforts to arrange direct peace talks.

In 2025, Putin offered to host Zelenskyy for talks in Moscow, but the Ukrainian president rejected the invitation as Russian forces continued attacking Ukraine.

"He can come to Kyiv," Zelenskyy told ABC News at the time, saying he could not visit Moscow while Ukraine remained under Russian missile attacks.

In September, on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, Russian journalists pressed Zelenskyy on when he would visit Moscow. He replied, "On a missile."

ZELENSKYY CONGRATULATES TRUMP ON TURNING 80 IN BIRTHDAY CALL, VOWS MORE UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AT G7 ON TUESDAY

Mendel, however, argued that personal animosity between the two leaders has become the main obstacle to diplomacy.

"Today there are diplomatic efforts to try to stop this brutal and bloody war that Russia started," she said.

"But what we see now is a personal opposition between Zelenskyy and Putin that continues to grow into constant escalation in which people suffer tremendously, Ukraine's infrastructure, energy grid, and businesses are in ruins, and refugees are fleeing."

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. More than four years later, peace negotiations are deadlocked over territory, security guarantees and the terms of a lasting ceasefire.

Moscow has demanded territorial concessions from Ukraine, including areas Russian forces do not fully control.

Kyiv has rejected ceding sovereign territory and insists that any agreement include enforceable security guarantees against another Russian attack.

RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN

Mendel went on to praise President Donald Trump's efforts to break the diplomatic deadlock, calling him the first Western leader to "challenge the status quo" and consistently push for an end to the war.

"For this reason, many Ukrainians place great hope in his ability to bring peace," she said.

"A sustainable peace deal cannot be reached solely between Zelensky and Putin; it requires the involvement and initiative of a strong third party to halt the ongoing devastation."

On Friday, the White House announced that first lady Melania Trump had helped broker a temporary ceasefire in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine's Kherson region, to allow humanitarian aid deliveries, demining operations and civilian evacuations.

An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in the devastated front-line town, many of them facing severe shortages of food, medicine and other essentials.

The White House said the ceasefire would begin Oct. 29, although Ukrainian and Russian officials have indicated that operations could begin Oct. 27.

Pope Leo also reportedly spoke with Zelenskyy and Putin about the humanitarian crisis, according to Vatican News.

ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE

"Melania Trump has become synonymous with the words of a saver and a hero, since she has brokered the deal for Oleshky," Mendel said. "This is something that is going to save around 2,000 people and that neither Ukraine nor Russia could have solved for months and months."

"That is why, you know, what Melania Trump has done is actually a case to show that where two men are fighting, a woman can actually save lives," she added.

"And this is the new approach that would show that peace really should focus on human lives, not on maps and territories."

Mendel also criticized the influence of Zelenskyy's longtime ally Andriy Yermak on his diplomatic approach, arguing that the Ukrainian president has favored confrontation over compromise.

"Mr. Yermak was teaching Zelenskiy to be a strong man in diplomacy. And what today we see is actually diplomacy that doesn't exist," she said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It's a diplomacy of humiliation, diplomacy of constant threats, diplomacy of demands," Mendel added.

World.title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign events after car crash
World.content:
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.

Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.

The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”

Police added that the incident is under investigation.

Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points.

Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.

Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.

Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.

Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.

Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “voter confusion.”

On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.

World.title: Trump leans into Islamophobic rhetoric at Michigan rally
World.content:
President Donald Trump embraced Islamophobic rhetoric Sunday as he rallied in Port Huron, Michigan, in support of the state’s Republican candidates, including the GOP Senate nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers.

Trump alleged that Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat with Rogers, is a “jihadist,” calling him a “Muslim Brotherhood member” while saying Rogers is “apple pie.”

“Anyone with that record of support for jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate,” Trump said about El-Sayed. “He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector.”

Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. Brendan Smialowski / AFP via Getty

Trump went on to draw a comparison between the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks and El-Sayed as he introduced speaker David Beamer, whose son, Todd Beamer, was a passenger who died on the hijacked United Flight 93.

“Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight just like Todd did to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” Trump said.

Beamer went on to extend Trump’s comparison between the Senate race and 9/11.

“What has changed? Well, one thing is 9/11 was a surprise attack. What’s going on right now in our country and here in Michigan? It’s not a surprise. We can see the attack coming that culminates in this battleground state on Tuesday, November the 3rd,” Beamer said as Trump stood behind him onstage.

“What’s different this time is the enemy has not come from abroad. The enemy is right here among us, local terrorists, local citizens that want to demolish our country,” he added.

Beamer, who has been featured in Rogers’ campaign ads, compared the two men and claimed Rogers is “an American” while saying El-Sayed is not, going on to call him “anti-American.”

“Abdul has a birth certificate. The birth certificate says he’s a citizen of America. You know what? A birth certificate doesn’t make you an American,” Beamer said.

“He has blood that’s red. However, he has chosen to remove any strain of the white and blue part in his life. We cannot, cannot allow this man to invade and occupy our country,” he added.

Both Rogers and El-Sayed were born in Michigan.

Michigan Democrat senatorial candidate Abdul El-Sayed and former President Barack Obama appeared onstage together at a rally in Detroit on Saturday. Bill Pugliano / AFP via Getty

El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump’s and Beamer’s remarks.

Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. The Trump administration has designated certain chapters of the group in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt as terrorist organizations. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied any ties to the group, which he has denounced.

El-Sayed went viral for a heated interaction last week with a town hall attendee who asked him to condemn the organization.

“You assume ... that because I am Muslim, that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed told the attendee last week.

Rogers was asked Sunday about Trump’s calling El-Sayed a “Muslim Brotherhood jihadist” and a “violent terrorist” in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press.” Pressed about whether he agreed with Trump’s characterizations, Rogers said the election is about “me versus Abdul,” adding, “I’ve never called him a terrorist.”

Rogers has previously questioned El-Sayed about his mother, Fatten Elkomy, over her work decades ago at a charity the U.S. government later labeled a supporter of terrorist groups, leading to its closure. Elkomy was not accused of wrongdoing at the time.

Trump helped popularize a false conspiracy theory about former President Barack Obama, claiming he was not a U.S. citizen and demanding to see his birth certificate. He has since repurposed “birther” attacks against other political rivals, including former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley, who was born in South Carolina.

Trump displayed content featuring El-Sayed at his rally in Port Huron, Mich., on Sunday. Brendan Sialowski / AFP via Getty

Trump on Sunday referred to Obama, who rallied in Detroit on Saturday on behalf of El-Sayed and other Michigan Democratic candidates.

“My competitor was here yesterday,” Trump, who is not running for office, said about Obama, who is also not running for office. “He didn’t have a crowd like this, I can tell you.”

World.title: How Democrats could win the House, how the GOP could hang on, and where to look for a wave
World.content:
Districts to watch: NC-14, KY-6

Another way to estimate the possible size of November’s swing is to look at the partisan shifts in elections held in 2025 and 2026, ever since Trump returned to office. These races include the 2025 governor’s elections in New Jersey and Virginia, other high-profile statewide elections and several special elections for the U.S. House.

Although Trump lost Virginia and New Jersey, the other recent elections have tended to occur in places that supported Trump in 2024. Averaging across all of these states and districts, Trump won them by an average of about 3.5 percentage points in 2024. In the 2025 and 2026 elections, however, those states and districts supported the Democratic candidate by an average of about 11 points. This amounts to a shift of 14.5 points in the Democrats’ favor.

If the Democrats are able to shift the vote in every district by such a historically massive margin in 2026, they could win as many as 263 seats to the Republicans’ 172. That would be the largest majority that either party has held in the U.S. House since the 1990 midterm elections.

Such a shift could put into play districts like Florida’s 27th District, represented by GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar. Republicans in Florida left this district nearly unchanged when they redrew the state’s congressional map, believing that a district that Trump won by 14.6 points would be out of reach for the Democrats.

But it appears the race in this heavily Hispanic district is tightening, as polls show Latino voters nationwide turning against Trump and Republicans, with economic concerns weighing heavily on their minds. These voters were critical to Trump’s winning coalition in 2024, and indications that they are moving back toward Democrats are helping drive the party’s competitiveness in Republican-leaning, heavily Hispanic districts in states like Texas, too. Salazar outran Trump’s win margin by nearly 6 percentage points in 2024, and her survival in the 2026 election may require a similarly strong overperformance.

A 14.5-point national swing toward Democrats could also make North Carolina’s 14th District competitive. Republican Rep. Tim Moore’s district is one that North Carolina Republicans did not bother changing when they redrew their maps last year. Trump won the district by 15.1 points, and Moore himself won it in 2024 by 16.1 points.

Another district to watch is Kentucky’s 6th District. Republican Andy Barr has held this open Lexington-based seat since 2013, and Trump carried it in 2024 by 15 points. Barr is running for the U.S. Senate this year. Republican- and Democratic-aligned groups are spending heavily here, reflecting the importance of the race, as Republican Ralph Alvarado faces off against Democrat Zach Dembo.

The NBC News Decision Desk rates this race as lean Republican. In 2024, this district reported almost 90% of its votes by 8:40 p.m. ET. If Democrats are on track for a massive national shift, this district may provide one of the best pieces of early evidence.

National trends don’t mean every district shifts the same amount

To be sure, all of these scenarios assume that the partisan shift in 2026 will be the same in every district. This may be true on average, but some districts will have a larger shift than the national average and others will have a smaller one.

Demographics of a specific district may play a role in the size of the shift. For example, if Hispanic voters shift more dramatically toward the Democratic Party than non-Hispanic voters, then districts with higher concentrations of Hispanic voters will vote more favorably for the Democrats than the underlying partisanship of the district would predict.

Incumbency can also play a large role in causing a district to shift more or less than the national average. In 2024, the incumbent members of Congress outperformed their party’s presidential candidate by an average of 2.5 percentage points.

This year, there are slightly more Democrats seeking re-election than Republican ones. This means that the Democratic Party as a whole stands to gain more from the benefits of incumbency compared with the Republican Party.

On the other hand, there are more Republicans who represent districts with evenly divided underlying partisanship. For example, an “incumbency bump” matters a lot more to a Republican in a district Trump won by 5 points than to a Democrat in a district Harris won by 25 points.

Finally, redistricting has also played a key role in this year’s midterms. By redrawing districts in several states, Republicans stand to win as many as 10 more seats than if the map remained unchanged after 2024.

Redistricting impacts the role of incumbency, too. When the lines for a district are redrawn, incumbents are fighting for the votes of people whom they’ve never represented and who may be less familiar with their records. This tends to diminish the size of the incumbency advantage. Republican incumbents in Texas and other red states and Democratic incumbents in California must lean heavily on the “D” or “R” next to their names when they try to win the support of their new potential constituents.

World.content:
Former President Barack Obama, appearing in Ohio on Saturday at his first campaign rally of this fall’s midterm elections, called President Donald Trump an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises.

Obama’s visit was aimed at boosting two Democrats: Amy Acton, the party’s nominee for governor; and former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who has mounted a comeback bid for his old job.

Obama was particularly scornful of Vivek Ramaswamy’s attack ad aimed at Acton, saying there is “no line” Ramaswamy won’t cross.

Later in the night, Obama rallied for Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit. The city, where 75% of the population is Black, is crucial to statewide victories.

Notable quote

He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. former president barak obama during a rally in ohio

Obama made pointed criticisms of his Republican successor, lambasting Trump for his focus on White House ballroom construction.

Iranian plots to kill U.S. officials have reached ‘advanced stages,’ intel memo warns

Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Oct. 19. Kylie Cooper / Pool/AFP via Getty

Iran has stepped up efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and elsewhere, according to a memo Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday.

The memo warned that “the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.”

A U.S. official confirmed the memo’s authenticity to NBC News after it was first reported by Axios.

The intelligence comes days after sources told NBC News that the U.S. military has been quietly scaling back its troop presence at bases across the Middle East. The State Department has also ordered further staff reductions at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to a State Department official.

Clayton told Rubio that the risk was “relevant to more individuals than are currently cleared to receive this information,” adding: “We will make every effort to downgrade as much intelligence as possible so you can share it with State Department personnel at your discretion.”

‘Meet the Press’

Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., told NBC’s “Meet the Press” that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should testify before the Senate on the Starlink satellite limitations that disrupted Ukrainian military operations.

If Democrats retake the Senate, Schiff told moderator Kristen Welker, “Defense Secretary Hegseth should be brought in. Anyone who has knowledge of what happened.”

Michigan’s Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers responded to Trump calling Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a “jihadist” and a “violent terrorist.”

“I’ve never called [El-Sayed] a terrorist,” Rogers said on “Meet the Press” after being asked about Trump’s comments.

Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer pushed back on comments made by former first lady Michelle Obama last year that U.S. voters aren’t ready to elect a woman as president.

“Listen, I have got a lot of colleagues who I think are probably interested in running for president, and I’ve heard everyone say, ‘You can’t have this person or that person,’” the governor told “Meet the Press.”
