World.title: Family pays $220,000 above reserve for Stanmore ‘renovators delight’
World.content:
PropertyNewsAuctions Family pays $220,000 above reserve for Stanmore ‘renovators delight’ Carmen Forward October 26, 2026 — 11:57am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 Gift this free article Share full article with anyone — no subscription needed to read it. It won't deduct your gift credits. Learn more Share article as gift Share A A A

Key points A five-bedroom house in Epping sold just below the top of its guide for $3,419,168.

Experts say buyers and sellers in Sydney are holding back, which is reflected in the clearance rate.

In Allambie Heights, a three-bedroom mid-century home sold just below its reserve for $2 million.

A family from Newtown paid $220,000 above the reserve for a four-bedroom renovator’s delight in Stanmore, which sold under the hammer for $2.52 million on Saturday. The two-storey terrace home at 106 Cavendish Street, which was considered unlivable had remained unrenovated for decades, was guided at $2.2 million. The home had five registered bidders and three active during the auction, all looking to upsize into western Sydney. The Stanmore property was one of 885 auctions scheduled in Sydney last week. By evening, Domain recorded a preliminary auction clearance rate of 45 per cent from 490 reported results, while 184 auctions were withdrawn.



Withdrawn auctions are counted as unsold properties when calculating the clearance rate. Bidding in Stanmore opened at $2.1 million with offers of $50,000, $20,000 and $10,000 increments following. The property needed a lot of work done. Gerber Properties The price reached its reserve of $2.3 million and continued to climb until it was called three times at $2.52 million where it sold under the hammer. Gerber Properties’ Nicole Gerber said the property would cost at least $1 million to make it livable.



“I think it’s very interesting that such a property that is actually not livable… in this market and these conditions actually sold,” Gerber said. “I think people sort of fell in love with the dream of what it can be.” The vendor, who was thrilled with the result, grew up in the home which had been in the family since the 1950s. In Epping, a five-bedroom house at 17 George Street with a $3.2 million to $3.5 million guide, sold for the unusually precise number of $3,419,168 to an upsizer from Castle Hill. Five bidders registered and three competed for the grand family home.



Bidding opened at $2.8 million and rose in $100,000, $50,000, and $1000 increments. When the price reached $3.4 million the $3.5 million reserve was adjusted down by $100,000, and it was put on the market. After forty or so minutes from start to finish the home sold for $3,419,168. Related Article Auctions Maroubra ‘blank canvas opportunity’ goes for $7 million Uniland Real Estate’s Andy Lin said the interested buyers had upsized to Epping. “The market is still tough,” Lin said. “Agents are finding it much harder to sell a property at auction, and only property with a good location and good land can still sell, but they also drop in price compared to last year [by] around seven to 10 per cent.” The vendor is downsizing to the Hills area, with the house last trading for $480,000 in 2002, records show.



In Allambie Heights a three-bedroom house at 22 Kirra Road sold at its guide price of $2 million, but below the $2.05 million reserve. It last sold in 2020 for $1,235,000 records show. Four bidders registered for the renovated mid-century property with butterfly roofline, but only two competed, with the buyer from Camperdown becoming the new owner. Bidding opened at $1.8 million and quickly jumped in $50,000, $20,000 and $10,000 increments until it sold under the hammer. “People loved that the quality was high, of the rebuild in 2021,” McGrath Manly’s Tim Cullen said. “There was nothing to do. It was move-in ready, ready to go.”



Related Article Sydney house prices ‘The downturn’s broadened’: Sydney’s median house price falls to $1.66m It also offered a good opportunity for the vendor to upsize, he said. “It’s the best climate I’ve ever seen to trade up,” Cullen said. “So when people say, ‘Is it a good market or a bad market?’,” It depends on your current situation.” LJ Hooker’s head of research and business intelligence Mathew Tiller said Sydney’s clearance rate of 45 per cent meant buyers and sellers were sitting on the fence. “There is still a lot of price pressures in the economy at the moment, which I think will probably lean the RBA more to [interest rate] hiking than holding,” Tiller said. “So that will obviously affect confidence again. “Given we’re in the spring selling season, and it’s meant to be the height of confidence for the property market, we’re just not seeing that come through this spring.”

World.title: Lidia Thorpe rebukes defiant Hanson over bus attack cartoon
World.content:
PoliticsFederalPolitical leadership Lidia Thorpe rebukes defiant Hanson over bus attack cartoon Emily Kaine October 26, 2026 — 11:52am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has defended a cartoon showing independent Senator Lidia Thorpe being run over by a bus, just days after independent MP Helen Haines was rammed by a car. Hanson’s unapologetic stance in a Monday morning interview with radio station 2GB prompted Thorpe to accuse One Nation of leaving death threats against her unmoderated on its platforms for months. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson in the Senate. Alex Ellinghausen On Sunday, AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett urged politicians to speak carefully as she drew a direct link between inflamed rhetoric and the rise in violent threats. She indicated, when asked about a One Nation clip of cartoon character Bluey driving down Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and former Victorian Premier Daniel Andrews, that there was a reaction when “examples like that” were produced. But Hanson is determined not to take down two cartoons showing politicians being run over, posting on X Sunday night that “they will not be going anywhere” and telling 2GB on Monday she would not apologise to Thorpe for the 2023 episode, Under the Bus.



“Look, this woman’s on the floor of parliament … You should see the hatred coming out of her mouth,” Hanson said. “So don’t tell me about my cartoons because they’re satirical … And besides, that last episode happened years ago in the cartoon,” Hanson said. Victorian senator Lidia Thorpe. Dominic Lorrimer The One Nation leader accused Barrett of deflecting responsibility for protecting Australians. “You’ve got kids out there on streets with ‘kill Pauline Hanson’. ‘I hate Pauline Hanson’, ‘shoot Pauline Hanson’. What does the commissioner do about that? Absolutely nothing,” Hanson said.



“So don’t tell me about the cartoons because this is passing the buck where you haven’t been able to do your job, [to] make it safe for the same people.” Related Article Haines attack Hanson hits back at AFP chief’s cartoon claims as MPs urged to sign civility pledge Thorpe said on Monday that Hanson should “think carefully about the example she is setting”. “Making light of violence, particularly against women in this country, is a problem. It’s not something anyone should be joking about,” the senator told this masthead. Thorpe added that she had reported a number of death threats posted by users on Hanson’s social media pages that had been left unmoderated by her team for months.



“If her supporters are making death threats against other politicians, that should be a red flag, and she should reflect on what sort of leadership qualities she is showing, and what sorts of things she is making light of. We can disagree fiercely about politics, we can have a laugh at each other, but making jokes about violence is not on.” Hanson last week apologised for a separate cartoon mocking Tasmanian senator Jacquie Lambie for her battle with vaginal prolapse, and One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce did offer an apology last month to Coalition frontbencher Andrew Hastie, who was labelled a traitor in another clip for testifying in the defamation case Ben Roberts-Smith has brought against Nine. Monday’s clash comes on the same day parliament pays tribute to independent MP Helen Haines, who remains in hospital recovering from an attack last Monday afternoon in the Victorian town of Wangaratta. Speaker of the House Milton Dick. Dominic Lorrimer Speaker of the House Milton Dick told parliament on Monday that politicians had a responsibility to lead by example.

World.title: An inscribed bullet on the windscreen: The mafia-style ‘death threat’ against a Victorian minister
World.content:
NationalVictoriaEmergency services An inscribed bullet on the windscreen: The mafia-style ‘death threat’ against a Victorian minister Alexander Darling Updated October 26, 2026 — 11:50am ,first published October 26, 2026 — 10:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

By the time Paul Edbrooke found the inscribed bullet on the windshield of his car in Frankston late last week, he was no stranger to threats and abuse. The emergency services minister had been the target of scorn for months, as the government remained locked in a series of disputes with the United Firefighters Union. Only a day earlier, union secretary Peter Marshall had said Edbrooke and Premier Ben Carroll were “in the gun” ahead of the November election. A bullet left on the windscreen of Paul Edbrooke’s car over the weekend. But when Edbrooke peered closer at the menacing object, his blood ran cold: The word “RAT” was etched into the gold metal casing. Even more chilling was an inscription on the other side: His five-digit ID number from when he was a firefighter, a personal detail known to only a small number of people. As his mind began to race, he suspected immediately where this “death threat” had come from.



“My kids drive this car, and you know, you start thinking: ‘Am I being followed? Who knows I’m here? Am I being surveilled?’,” he recalled to ABC radio on Monday. “It’s not subtle… that’s a death threat.” Coming mere days after federal MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberately mowed down by a vehicle outside her Wangaratta office on Monday, Edbrooke told Premier Carroll over the phone that he was making a report to police. He also had to explain what had happened to his family, including three young adult children, showing them the bullet. Emergency Services Minister Paul Edbrooke has taken aim at the UFU after finding the engraved bullet. The Age “I could see the terror, and I didn’t want to traumatise them. I think they took it in their stride, but at the same time, this is an escalation they’ve never seen. Just seeing the look in their eyes made me really sad.”



The matter, now with police, is the latest example of violence and intimidation towards elected officials that has dominated the national conversation since the alleged attack on Haines. Haines remains serious but stable in the Alfred hospital, having had both legs amputated to save her life. The driver, Brendan Nugent, is now behind bars, charged with several offences. Edbrooke worked as a firefighter in Frankston for 14 years, during which he served as the station’s workplace representative for the UFU and fought the Black Saturday bushfires in Marysville and Kinglake. He was also a long-time teacher before turning to politics. Edbrooke had been out in the community meeting his constituents face-to-face the day he walked back to his car to find the bullet. “I’m not sure how long it had been there. It could have just been put there, possibly. I’m waiting for the police to investigate that.”



He points the finger at the same union he once worked for because very few people knew his five-digit ID number. “The only people I’m really getting aggressive threats from at the moment are members of that union,” he said. “This is a new low in a pattern of threatening behaviour against politicians.” Related Article Exclusive

Industrial relations Firefighters shocked after union sends them debt recovery letters “There is a small minority in the UFU who think threats and intimidation are acceptable - this does not represent our firefighters.” “It’s one thing to be an armchair critic and say what you want from behind a computer. It’s another thing to follow somebody and put something on their car like a bullet.” He added that the small group of UFU members he was referring to “believe everything they are told by the leadership and think that by someone intimidating or bullying me, I will support them and give them a taxpayer-funded slush fund for the union. It ain’t gonna happen”.



Edbrooke clarified that there was an issue with an income protection scheme going to the UFU, when he believed it should go to firefighters directly. “That’s what this is about. It’s not about firefighter safety or staffing. There is no threat to that from the state government.” He urged candidates from other parties to stop campaigning with the UFU. “The message I’d like to get out there to all [election] candidates is: if you enjoy our democracy, the standard you walk past in the standard you accept,” he said.



Opposition leader Jess Wilson said her thoughts were with Edbrooke. “I can’t imagine how upsetting it is for him and for his family,” she said. “There’s just no place for these sort of threats and intimidation in Victoria or this country.” Edbrooke has also recently been the target of a fresh campaign by the UFU: Since Wednesday, it has been running televised ads urging people to put Labor last in next month’s state election, angry that the government wants to end enforceable minimum staffing for firefighters. “Firefighters beat these arguments in court when a Liberal government ran them. Now a Labor government is running the Liberals’ case against its own firefighters,” said UFU Secretary Peter Marshall in a statement announcing the ad blitz. “Minister Edbrooke can end this with the stroke of a pen. Until he does, firefighters will tell voters the truth.”



Marshall also addressed union members on Friday, saying Edbrooke and Premier Ben Carroll would be “in the gun” if they affected his members. On Monday, Marshall clarified this comment. “I meant at the ballot box and anyone there, or seeing the video, would know that,” he said. “Threatening anyone, including a minister we strongly disagree with, is the opposite of everything this union stands for. I condemn it without qualification.” Marshall said whoever had planted the bullet did not act for his union or for firefighters more generally, and that he hoped police found the culprit. The union has also been locked in a years-long pay dispute with the government, which remains before the Fair Work Commission. In August, Fire Rescue Victoria firefighters urged the government to intervene, alleging Marshall was stalling the negotiations.



“We stand ready to give firefighters the pay rise they want, but we won’t be including any kind of slush fund in that agreement,” Edbrooke said. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: Lost in the arena: Lily Allen’s intimate theatrical drama falls flat plus other big shows this week
World.content:
TikTok Entertainment Centre, October 25, also October 26

In her brutal narrative album of marital discord and disaster, West End Girl, Lily Allen has the perfect vehicle to merge several elements of her career and appeal into something new.

There’s the frank feminist who bridged aspiring-cynic teens with seasoned-cynic adults and the hook-tastic pop singer who made that sound like a hoot; the hedonist-who-tried-it-all and the romantic-despite-it-all; the latter-day stage actor of other people’s words and the life-long diarist who will share her truth.

Lily Allen did not speak between songs, performing the show as more of a theatrical piece. Emma Louise Smith

So turning last year’s record firstly into a small theatre creation and then into this year’s arena pop show – to which you can add a solid bit of sisterhood bonding over male treachery, with women near me regularly yelling out affirmations (“you’re too good for him … get him Lils”) and condemnations (“he’s a c---” and, to the marital interloper Madeline, “f--- you bitch”) – didn’t just make sense, it was excitingly different for an artist who has not always found live performance a particularly interesting exercise.

World.title: Wet and windy end to Labour day weekend for parts of the country
World.content:
Parts of the South Island are being lashed by heavy rain and severe gales as an active front moves up the country.

MetService meteorologist Samkelo Magwala said a wind gust of about 200km/h was recorded at Mount Hutt, Canterbury, around 8am on Monday.

He advised people in affected areas to keep an eye on the weather and road conditions.

"Those people who are planning to travel after the long weekend ... should be vigilant when driving, especially in those areas where the weather won't be so pleasant," he said.

Meanwhile, police are closing a central road in Wellington due to high wind gusts.

A spokesperson said a stretch of Oriental Parade and Evans Bay Parade was being shut following reports of multiple people falling off bicycles and wing mirrors being blown off cars.

The road around the point is closed from Carlton Gore Road in Oriental Bay to Maida Vale Road at the intersection with Evans Bay Parade.

Fire and Emergency said crews have so far dealt with five wind-related callouts, including material falling from buildings and downed power lines.

Shift manager Becca said a piece of panelling had fallen off the ceiling of Jetts Fitness in Miramar, and glass had fallen onto the footpath and street from a balcony in Mount Victoria.

Crews in both areas were trying to keep the area safe, Becca said.

Weather warnings in place

Westland and Fiordland are under orange rain warnings, with up to 250 millimetres of rain expected about the ranges of Westland.

Metservice issued rain and wind warnings and watches for some of the South Island on Sunday, but more warnings are now in place for parts of the lower North Island.

New Zealand Transport Agency Waka Kotahi said heavy rain would make roads slippery, meaning drivers should think about adjusting their speed and travelling distances, avoiding sudden braking and staying visible.

"People are also urged to avoid driving through any floodwaters, especially where the depth is unclear and there may be hidden obstructions," the agency said.

"NZTA contractors will be monitoring the state highway network and will respond to any slips or obstructions that need clearing."

An orange strong wind warning is in place for Wellington, Wairarapa, the Canterbury High Country and Plains, Otago, Fiordland, Marlborough, Southland and Stewart Island, with gusts up to 120km/h possible in exposed places.

These warnings expire from 7pm Monday in the south and 9am Tuesday in Wellington.

A strong wind watch has also been issued for Christchurch from 6pm Monday, the Tararua District from 11pm Monday and in Horowhenua and Kāpiti from 3am Tuesday.

An orange heavy rain warning is in place for Grey and Buller districts, Westland, the headwaters of the Canterbury lakes and rivers about and south of Arthur's Pass, the headwaters of the Otago lakes and rivers, and Fiordland.

An orange heavy rain warning will go in place for the Tararua Range from 2am Tuesday.

There is a heavy rain watch for the Queenstown Lakes district away from the headwaters and Southland and Stewart Island, expiring from 11pm Monday in the south to 11am Tuesday in the north.

Westland can expect the heaviest falls, with 200 to 250mm forecast about the ranges and 300mm possible about isolated peaks.

Most of the warnings expire from Tuesday morning, with those in the lower South Island expiring on Monday.

MetService said there was a low to minimal chance of its orange wind and rain warnings being upgraded to red.

World.title: Southland scrub fire still burning as wind hampers firefighting efforts
World.content:
High winds have been preventing firefighters working on a scrub fire that is still actively burning in nearly 80 hectares of land in Southland.

Six helicopters worked with monsoon buckets to protect two communications towers in the Centre Hill area after emergency services were alerted to the blaze at about 4pm on Sunday.

Fire and Emergency said high winds on Monday morning were preventing aircraft from operating.

Ground crews had not been sent out due to the terrain of the high country grazing and conservation land burning.

FENZ said firefighting would resume when conditions allowed, and investigators would be looking into the cause of the blaze.

MetService had an orange strong wind warning in place for Southland on Monday with severe gales expected to reach up to 130 km/h in exposed places.

World.title: 'I said no': Samoan PM told Luxon treaty refresh must wait until new NZ government elected
World.content:
Samoa's Prime Minister La'aulialemalietoa (La'auli) Leuatea Schmidt paused talks on a refreshed treaty with New Zealand until after the New Zealand general election.

La'auli claimed Prime Minister Christopher Luxon had asked for them to "proceed with it" anyway, but he decided not to.

La'auli made the revelation at a cocktail function supporting the 'visa on arrival' campaign led by prominent Aotearoa community leader Anae Arthur Anae in Apia last week, according to a report by the Samoa Observer.

According to the Samoa Observer, Anae was in Samoa seeking signatures for changes to New Zealand's immigration arrangements for Samoans. He has become a leading campaigner for immigration reform for Pacific Islanders.

"Regarding the Treaty of Friendship that was being prepared, Luxon wanted me to go ahead and proceed with it, but I said no," La'auli was quoted as saying by the newspaper.

"I told him to wait until the (NZ) election is fully concluded and to see who the new Prime Minister is; only then will I have a 'fair' go at whoever will be newly elected."

The Treaty of Friendship between Samoa and New Zealand is the principal bilateral agreement between the two nations. It is a unique partnership, signed in August 1962 after Samoa gained independence from New Zealand.

The newspaper reported that the Samoan prime minister said he was preparing proposals to "refresh and refine" Samoa's relationship with New Zealand under the treaty.

"I am currently putting together Samoa's perspective on how we might refresh and refine our relationship with New Zealand," he said.

Luxon visited Samoa in March this year. Facebook / Government of Samoa

Luxon visited Samoa in March this year, where he met with La'auli and was also bestowed with the matai (chiefly) title of Tuisinavemaulumoto'otua from the village of Apia. During the visit, he signed memorandums of understanding for police and customs cooperation to combat transnational crime.

World.title: ACT publishes manifesto with $22b in cuts, ditches migration promise
World.content:
ACT has published its campaign manifesto on the first day of voting, pitching itself as the only party seeking to save taxpayers' money this election.

The document also shows ACT has ditched an earlier promise to scrap the existing Permanent Resident Visa category in response to "anxieties" among migrant communities.

Instead, the manifesto states those visa-holders will have to maintain "a genuine connection to New Zealand".

The plan brings together all of ACT's announced policies, including a KiwiSaver tax break, a higher pension age and a three-year freeze on the minimum wage.

Together, it promises to cut $22 billion of "wasteful" spending over four years, with government debt $12.4b lower by 2031 than currently forecast.

Launching the manifesto in Auckland on Monday, leader David Seymour called on voters to re-elect the coalition, but he also made a point in the document to distinguish ACT from its governing partners.

"Every other political party, even National, wants to spend more of your money," he wrote.

"ACT alone is proposing to save your money."

Speaking outside the St Heliers Arts and Crafts market, Seymour said the manifesto represented the pitch ACT would take into coalition negotiations.

He said ACT would be "professional and collegial" in pulling together a government "as fast as possible" but he scoffed at Labour leader Chris Hipkins' guarantee of a government before Christmas.

"The only Christmas we're campaigning for is [Tamaki candidate] James Christmas!" Seymour said.

Migration policy tweak

Seymour told RNZ the party had heard the concerns of migrant communities about its September pledge to "put 'reside' back in 'resident'."

ACT previously promised to axe the Permanent Resident Visa and impose ongoing physical-presence requirements on Resident Visa holders who wanted to retain their travel rights.

Seymour said ACT had dropped the policy after listening to feedback from the community.

"People felt that it was disrespectful and exclusionary. That's never been the ACT party's intention. And when we get feedback, we can listen and we can change."

Seymour said ACT would instead campaign to bring New Zealand's rules into line with those in Australia and Canada.

"Permanent residence will continue, and the rules will not change for people that currently have PR.

"But if you get permanent residence in the future, you will have to stay in New Zealand for at least two out of any five years to retain it."

The manifesto included a commitment to "ensure new Permanent Resident Visa holders maintain a genuine connection to New Zealand, retaining sensible work, family, service, humanitarian and investor exemptions".

Among the policies already announced is a plan to remove tax on KiwiSaver investment earnings. In exchange, ACT would scrap the government's KiwiSaver contribution.

It would also gradually increase the age of superannuation.

By 2035, New Zealanders would have to wait until 67 to receive the pension, with early access for people in physically demanding jobs.

People could still withdraw their KiwiSaver savings at 65.

People receiving Jobseeker Support who were considered ready to work would face restrictions on their spending after four months on the benefit.

Their payments would be managed electronically, covering essentials such as food and housing while blocking spending on alcohol, tobacco and gambling.

ACT would also require independent medical assessments and gradually reassess people receiving health-related Jobseeker Support and the Supported Living Payment.

The party would also freeze the adult minimum wage for three years and allow employers to pay workers under 20 a training wage worth 60 percent of the adult rate during their first year of employment.

On health, ACT promised an extra $400m for general practice over four years and funding for pharmacists to treat more common illnesses.

The party also backed a national cancer centre with campuses in Auckland and Christchurch.

World.title: Candidates push back on ACT's plan to abolish 'done nothing' Pacific ministry
World.content:
ACT Party candidate Henrietta Devoe is standing by her call to abolish the Ministry for Pacific Peoples (MPP), questioning whether it has delivered for Pasifika communities.

Devoe made the comments during last week's Pacific Media Network (PMN) debate, which brought together Pasifika representatives from across the political parties.

Debate moderator PMN's William Terite asked the candidates whether the MPP "should remain".

Devoe was the only candidate to say it should not, arguing the ministry had failed to deliver for Pacific people.

"I'd just like to say I raised my kids in Ōtara, and honestly, what has it done for the people? Like, what has it done? Really? Nothing," Devoe said.

"The Ministry for Pacific Peoples has done nothing for Pacific Islanders."

Devoe's comments are not a new position for ACT, which has long-called for MPP to be abolished.

Back in 2023, ACT leader David Seymour controversially said he fantasised about sending a "guy called Guy Fawkes in there and it'd all be over, but we'll probably have to have a more formal approach than that".

But Devoe's comments were rejected by several other candidates, who described them as "insulting".

From left: National's Angee Nicholas, NZ First's Alfred Ngaro, Pacific Morning's Host William Terite, Labour's Jenny Salesa, Opportunity's Romeo Tavaga, Terite, ACT's Henrietta Devoe and Green Party MP Teanau Tuiono. PMN News

"I think that's a really insulting thing to say," Opportunities Party candidate Romeo Tevaga said. "In terms of the public servants who work at the Ministry for Pacific Peoples, how do you think they achieve Language Weeks, which are really important to our identity, language and culture?"

"We're not just any other population," Green Party candidate Teanau Tuiono added.

Labour's Jenny Salesa also pushed back.

"I absolutely disagree with [Devoe's comments]," Salesa said.

"I think that's a really insulting thing to say. Very insulting. Why should we get rid of the ministry now when we have this many people?"

'Focus on need, not race' - Devoe

Devoe has since told RNZ Pacific that she stands by her comments, pointing to the experiences of her own whānau.

"My husband and I raised our children in Ōtara - our daughter was the first in our family to attend university gaining two degrees and is now a lawyer, while our son has completed his commerce degree and works fulltime," she said.

She said that reflected the "legacy that our Pacific families came to New Zealand for".

"Risking everything to build a better life for generations to come. That's the legacy that unlocks Pacific potential everywhere.

"I support ACT's plan to abolish the Ministry for Pacific Peoples and build a smaller, accountable government. Health, education and housing agencies should meet people's needs and deliver results.

"I'm tired of Pacific people being used as a political football or portrayed as needing more help than others. Do you know how insulting that is? That our kids supposedly need special treatment. Every community has needs."

She added that governments needed to offer support based on need rather than race.

"Every community has needs - the government should focus on need, not race. I don't need a ministry in Wellington to tell me to be proud of my culture, and I certainly don't need one telling me what my people are capable of achieving."

Guided by priority communities

The MPP said it would not respond to the views of individual political candidates, but said its work was directly guided by priorities identified by Pacific communities.

MPP secretary Gerardine Clifford-Lidstone said these included education, health, housing, economic development and Pacific languages.

World.title: Fire in Auckland Kainga Ora property deemed suspicious: FENZ
World.content:
A fire in a Kainga Ora property in Mount Albert, Auckland, on Monday morning has been deemed suspicious, Fire and Emergency says.

Emergency services were called to the duplex unit on Tasman Avenue just after 2am.

Three fire trucks fought the blaze, which was well involved by the time crews arrived, a FENZ spokesperson said.

There were initial concerns that the building was occupied but no-one was found inside once the fire was extinguished, the spokesperson said.

Meanwhile, FENZ said a residential property that caught fire in the Auckland suburb of Glen Eden on Sunday night appeared to have been abandoned.

Emergency services were called to the blaze on Shah Place just after 9.30pm.

The two-storey residential building was well ablaze by the time crews arrived and five fire trucks fought the fire at its peak, a FENZ spokesperson said.

Crews worked to protect surrounding houses and remained at the scene until about 3am to watch for any flare-ups.

World.title: Cordons come down at Auckland playground where child critically injured
World.content:
The cordons around a playground in a central-city park in Auckland have been taken down after a child suffered critical injuries.

Police say a person was assaulted by a man at the park about 4.45pm on Sunday.

Inspector Jim Wilson said the man was not known to the victim.

A 20-year-old man was taken into custody and both the victim and the man required medical treatment.

St John says one person was taken to Auckland City Hospital in a serious condition and the other to Starship Children's Hospital critically injured.

World.title: England 'gutted' after second extraordinary ODI defeat in as many games
World.content:
Shadab Khan hit an epic ODI century, and England suffered a second extraordinary defeat in as many games as Pakistan snatched a one-wicket victory on Sunday to secure its place in the cricket tri-series final.

Pakistan's chase looked doomed at 9-154 before a defiant 89-run, last-wicket stand between Shadab and number 11 Haris Rauf secured Pakistan a dazzling win. Shadab smashed his first one-day ton to take Pakistan to 9-243 in 47.1 overs.

Even within that 10th wicket stand, Pakistan seemed to have been beaten when Gus Atkinson won an LBW decision against Shadab with 21 runs still required.

Shadab threw his bat down and started congratulating England's players before asking for a speculative review, which showed the faintest inside edge, leaving Shadab screaming with joy at the reprieve.

"The boys are absolutely gutted," England coach Brendon McCullum told the BBC.

"Today they fought incredibly hard … we were in a pretty good position, well, a very good position and then obviously we weren't able to get across the line.

"The last game was, the boys were gutted after that, and you look in the dressing room now, they're also extremely gutted now."

England, which scored 429 and still lost in its last game against Sri Lanka, was earlier all out for 241 in 46.4 overs.

Playing his first game in the tournament, Shadab scored 113 not out off 96 balls and farmed most of the strike. Rauf (7 not out in 19 balls) hit the winning boundary as Pakistan enjoyed its third successive win.

It was the biggest last-wicket partnership in a successful chase in ODIs.

The 10th wicket partnership was the largest ever to win a game in ODI cricket. (Getty Images: Sameer Ali)

Left-handed opener Ben Duckett scored 105 for England — his fifth ODI century and first against Pakistan — after Shaheen Shah Afridi won his first toss in the tournament and elected to field after successfully defending 300-plus scores in the first two games.

It was England's third successive defeat in the tournament after losing to Pakistan by 87 runs and seeing Sri Lanka pull off the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history despite captain Harry Brook scoring a blistering 114-ball double century.

Pakistan will take on Sri Lanka in their last league game on Tuesday after beating the Sri Lankans by 37 runs in the opening game.

Rauf joined Shadab at 154-9 in the 34th over and launched a partnership neither side will quickly forget. While Shadab outsmarted England pace with his brilliant batting, Rauf gave him ample support by sensibly not going for expansive shots.

Shadab protected Rauf well by keeping the strike to himself and counterpunching the bowlers by hitting boundaries early in the over, completing his century by playing a late cut off Atkinson for his 12th boundary before hitting the fast bowler over long off for a six to reduce the target to three runs off the final three overs.

Rauf drilled debutant fast bowler Henry Crocombe for a straight boundary to cap a remarkable recovery for Pakistan.

Earlier, Jamie Overton (3-43) took two smart slip catches to remove both struggling opening batters Fakhar Zaman (10) and Saim Ayub (6) and Babar Azam will continue his search for a big innings after Atkinson pegged back his off stump as Pakistan slumped to 31-3 inside the first seven overs.

Brook then turned to Overton soon after the batting power play, and the fast bowler responded immediately in his first over when 19-year-old Saad Baig (32) cut straight to Will Jacks at point.

Left-arm spinner Liam Dawson (2-30) and Jacks (1-18) then bowled tidily and raised England's hopes of their first win.

Duckett revived England from a precarious 52-4 with a 93-run stand with Sam Curran, who made 42 off 52 balls.

Afridi picked up 4-46 and England lost four of the five top batters for single digits. That included the run-out of Brook, who went for a second run but fell short of his crease to an electrifying throw from debutant Razaullah.

England lost quick wickets and slipped to 201-9 after Afridi removed Curran in his return spell when he holed out to fine leg off a mistimed pull. Razaullah took 2-38, grabbing the wickets of Jacks and Dawson.

Duckett, who hit 10 fours and two sixes in his 111-ball knock, fell in the 37th over when he top-edged a sweep to fine leg against left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas before Atkinson (36 not out) shared a 40-run last-wicket stand with Crocombe.

AP/ABC

World.title: Manchester United booed off pitch after calamitous defeat
World.content:
Michael Carrick patted his chest and gave an apologetic salute to the Manchester United fans who were applauding him, before trudging down the tunnel at the end of another bruising afternoon at Old Trafford.

Then came a chorus of boos for the United players walking behind him.

United had just lost 3-0 to Bournemouth again in the Premier League, and the disgruntled home support made it clear who they were behind in this latest sorry episode for a team that, not too long ago, was the pinnacle of English football.

Indeed, the only person to escape censure was the manager overseeing an eight-match winless run that is bringing more embarrassment to the country's biggest club.

"It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time," said an emotional-looking Carrick, who spoke of his "mixed emotions" during a match that further exposed the weakness in his fragile United team.

"It wasn't a farewell from me," Carrick added of post-match actions that saw him lead his players on a walk around the field.

"What it looks like, what is next — I really don't know. But I'll always do what's best for this football club."

Carrick is trying everything to get United out its perilous position, which sees the club languishing in 16th place in the 20-team Premier League.

That includes even dropping captain Bruno Fernandes.

Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United players traipse off (Getty Images: Marc Atkins)

The humbling by Bournemouth came four days after a humiliating 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League that was followed by critical comments to the media by Fernandes about Carrick's tactics.

Carrick responded by leaving the Portugal star — the player of the year in England last season — out of the team in what the manager described as a "pure football" decision.

Fernandes briefly went out to warm up at one point but never made it onto the field, where United defended woefully as Bournemouth scored through Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson.

Carrick's job is under huge threat, barely five months after he signed a permanent deal as manager after leading the team back into the Champions League while on a short-term contract in the second half of last season.

But getting rid of Carrick would not solve the huge problems at United, whose fans also chanted against Jason Wilcox, the club's director of football who was the target of recent criticism from defender Lisandro Martinez, and the Glazer family, the majority owners, before letting rip on the players.

United has won one of its eight league games this season — and that was at home to promoted Ipswich on August 30.

"It's nowhere near good enough," United defender Harry Maguire said.

"Something needs to change."

Manchester United fans have rarely felt such dejection at their club's form. (Getty Images: CameraSport/Dave Howarth)

As for Bournemouth, it has now beaten United 3-0 at Old Trafford in three of the last four seasons. On its other visit in that stretch, there was a 4-4 draw.

Brighton run ends at Anfield, Newcastle win

Brighton, the league's surprise package this season, was beaten 2-0 at Liverpool for its first defeat since August, after which the south-coast team embarked on a stunning run since that included two 5-0 wins and a 3-0 victory over defending champion Arsenal.

That streak ended in a tight game at Anfield, with Liverpool's goals coming in a four-minute span midway through the first half. Pascal Gross deflected Florian Wirtz's shot into his own net before Alexander Isak turned home Bradley Barcola's cross.

It was Liverpool's first league win at home under Andoni Iraola, hired as manager over the summer, and it lifted the team into fourth spot — a point and a place behind Brighton

Brighton had 64 per cent possession and 17 shots — though just one on target — and manager Fabian Hurzeler called it a "missed opportunity" for his team to further underline its status as a growing force.

"I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game," Hurzeler said, "and therefore I have to praise my players."

Newcastle beat Crystal Palace 2-0 thanks to second-half goals from William Osula and Harvey Barnes.

Hull and Brentford drew 1-1, while Sunderland and Leeds finished 0-0.

AP

World.title: Smith will be 'fine' as Australia returns to Cape Town
World.content:
Australia returns to the scene of one of the darkest days in the country's cricket history when the series-deciding third Test against South Africa starts at Newlands on Tuesday.

ABC Sport will have live blog coverage and radio commentary of the third Test.

The battle may be mental as much as one of skill for several of the Australian players, not least former captain Steve Smith, who was at the centre of the Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018.

Current skipper Pat Cummins was part of that side, as were fellow seamer Josh Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon, though they say they had no knowledge of the attempt to alter the condition of the ball with a piece of sandpaper.

Smith bore the brunt of the considerable fallout in Australia eight years ago and, having not reached the heights he might have expected on this tour, averaging a little over 20 with the bat, he would see this as the perfect time to put that right.

How Sandpapergate rocked Australian cricket In 2018, Sandpapergate rocked Australian cricket to its very core. Here's how a febrile atmosphere colluded with a team persistently testing the limits of acceptability to change the game.

There has so far been little chatter in South Africa about Sandpapergate but that could change at Newlands, where the first three days' ticket sales have been strong after sparse crowds at the first two Tests in Durban and Gqeberha.

"He'll be fine," Australian opener Travis Head said of Smith.

"I think he showed that in 2019 in England. We support him.

"He's been through a lot in that space and handles it well. Sometimes it brings the best out of him, as we've seen in the past."

The series is level at 1-1 after big wins for both sides in the opening two games, and Australian wicketkeeper Alex Carey told reporters on Sunday that it looked to be another good Test-match pitch.

"We are still a couple of days out but it looks another great surface," he said.

"If you look back at Durban it was a five-day Test match and a great contest between bat and ball. The same in Port Elizabeth [Gqeberha] and this should be no different."

There has never been a Test match played at Newlands in October, and just three in November, all against Australia.

The tourists won the first two in 1902 and 1921, but the most recent November fixture was an eight-wicket victory for South Africa in 2011 when Australia was famously bowled out for 47 in the second innings.

South Africa will be without fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who injured his groin in the second Test.

Captain Temba Bavuma said the hosts would pick horses for courses in terms of his replacement.

"You've got guys like Gerald [Coetzee], Pato [Dane Paterson], as well as [Corbin] Bosch, and we have Sen [Senuran Muthusamy] as well, so the options are there," he said.

"Whoever we decide, we'll be confident they form part of our best XI for the conditions."

Reuters

World.title: England legend Anderson disappointed over Lancashire exit
World.content:
England legend Jimmy Anderson says he was disappointed when Lancashire decided not to renew his contract.

The 44-year-old fast bowler, England's all-time leading Test wicket taker, has played for his home county for 25 years.

Anderson, who claimed 704 Test wickets for England, will leave Lancashire as the county looks to rebuild its squad for a promotion push from Division Two of the County Championship.

The veteran bowler made 112 first-class appearances for Lancashire, claiming 443 wickets, and was involved in its County Championship title triumph in 2011.

"I've supported Lancashire since I was a kid, and so to get to play for them for 25 years was a dream come true," Anderson said in a statement.

"I have always found it special walking out to play at Old Trafford and have some incredible memories of doing so including the honour of being captain.

"If it was up to me it wouldn't have ended like this but I wish the players and fans all the best for the future."

Anderson, who was appointed Lancashire's red-ball captain for the first time in his career in the 2026 season, took 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 this summer, but the county finished seventh out of eight teams in the second division.

That was the seventh-best return of any bowler in Division Two, while his average was fourth-best of any bowler to bowl over 100 overs in the season, and considerably better than any other Lancashire player.

"I spoke to Jimmy about our ambitions to rebuild our men's squad that is capable of securing promotion from Division Two of the County Championship and then challenging to win Division One over the next three to four years," said Paul Farbrace, Lancashire's incoming director of cricket.

"We are keen to begin that rebuild now, both in terms of the playing squad and the wider professional cricket set-up, and to make important progress over the coming months.

"As part of those plans, I informed Jimmy that we had taken the incredibly difficult decision not to extend his playing contract for the 2027 season."

Lancashire Cricket had honoured Anderson's contribution to the club by renaming the Pavilion End at Old Trafford the James Anderson End. He was also knighted in 2025 in recognition of his services to cricket.

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Essendon sack coach after one-win AFLW season
World.content:
Hawthorn will remain anxious after their win over Essendon, though they are not faring worse than the Bombers, who sacked their coach after her one-win season.

The Bombers told Natalie Wood this week they would not renew her contract, but both parties chose to wait until after Sunday's 3.7 (25) to 3.2 (20) loss to the Hawks to inform players, coaches and staff.

The scores were level at half-time and Essendon's defensive structure was impressive, keeping the Hawks scoreless in the final quarter.

However, the Dons gave up nine intercept marks in Hawthorn's attacking half and it proved costly.

It was a needed win for Hawthorn, which found itself in eighth spot on the ladder, one win clear from Fremantle and Adelaide.

But its finals spot is not cemented with one round remaining.

If the Dockers and Crows win next weekend, and Hawthorn lose to West Coast in Perth, the all-important ladder position will be determined by percentage points.

The Hawks ran away from the Bombers in the second half. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Daniel Pockett)

Wood will see out the season, aiming to claim one more win against fellow cellar dwellers Collingwood at Windy Hill next Sunday.

"This was a difficult decision and we thank her for the role she has played in our history," Essendon chief executive Tim Roberts said.

"When we entered the competition in 2022, Natalie set the standards and culture of our team, and our back-to-back finals in 2023 and 2024 reflected that work."

Roberts added this season had been "challenging".

"We have fallen short of what we wanted on field. We believe a change is the right step," he said.

"Natalie has handled this with real integrity, and her commitment to coaching out the season says a lot about her and how much she cares about the players.

"We thank Natalie for everything she has given the club over five seasons, and we wish her all the best for the next step in her football journey."

GWS coach Cameron Bernasconi has escaped a similar fate.

His side has finished in the bottom three on the ladder for the past three seasons, but he penned a two-year contract extension at the start of the year.

His Giants team performed similarly to the Dons against Carlton.

Carlton kept their top four hopes alive with a win over struggling GWS. (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Michael Willson)

The scores were level at three-quarter time, but the Blues found two more goals in the final term to secure the 5.8 (38) to 3.5 (23) win and keep their top-four hopes alive.

Essendon said the club would commence its search for a new AFLW coach, while also assessing "every part of the program to make sure it continues to grow with the competition and is positioned to improve".

Wood joined the Bombers in March 2022, ahead of their inaugural AFLW season.

During her tenure, Wood became the first woman to coach 50 AFLW games and she led Essendon to finals appearances in 2023 and 2024.

"Building an AFLW program from the ground up takes an enormous collective effort. I'm proud to have led that work and supported our players to grow as footballers and people," Wood said.

"It has been a privilege to be Essendon's inaugural AFLW senior coach."

AAP

World.title: Weather ruins MotoGP but Phillip Island goes out on high
World.content:
The phrase "die hard" doesn't sufficiently describe the passion of the MotoGP fan.

Not only did enthusiasts travel for hours in traffic to get onto Victoria's Phillip Island, but they sat all day Sunday in the rain, waiting under the looming prospect the final race on the island's iconic circuit would be cancelled.

Finally, the crowd was put out of its misery.

After delay upon delay, the final MotoGP to be held on the island was no more, unceremoniously cancelled due to poor visibility and rain that had been falling steadily overnight and into the day.

The breadth of the weekend's weather suited the mood of the final weekend of MotoGP racing.

Fans stood on Friday under a blazing spring sun to watch their heroes do practice laps at the island track, the azure waters of the Bass Strait blazing on the horizon, before conditions shifted to a wintry deluge on the last two days of racing.

Stephen Greenwood rode his bike from Campbelltown in New South Wales, and was part of the heaving crowds swarming the island in a haze of adrenaline, nostalgia, and bittersweet sense of loss.

Stephen Greenwood was one of the 500 riders who made the pilgrimage onto Phillip Island to farewell the MotoGP. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

He has hopes the race could some day return to the island.

"It's such a shame to lose it from here. It's one of the best tracks in the world and I just love coming here," Mr Greenwood said.

He said the community and atmosphere of the event was intoxicating, and draw him back each year.

"You walk the streets, you see the riders in cafes. I've seen a couple of the riders at the Italian restaurant. The track is phenomenal," he said.

"I have friends who rode down from Arlie Beach … everyone just wants to support it."

More than 500 riders took part in the final TAC Homecoming Ride last Thursday. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

One final roar

When the MotoGP makes its annual pilgrimage to the Gippsland region, the island becomes a melting pot of cliche and chaos, with the roar and hum of motorcycles in their thousands set against the backdrop of a blue ocean that could be the envy of any Greek Island.

Aria Bie from Knox near Melbourne has had her licence for three years, and travelled to the island on her Triumph Daytona 660 for the Homecoming Ride.

"Coming to Phillip Island is really exciting, because I'm still getting used to the long ride for the whole day," she said.

"But it makes it special. This is the national event, and we have lots of bikers here with passion. It just feels really nice to be part of the group and the biker community as well."

Arie Bie took park in the Homecoming Ride. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

The MotoGP has drawn thousands of motoring fans to the island to watch the annual race since 1989.

And the island pulled out all stops in its farewell to the sport.

Chequered flags hung from street lights and snapped in the coastal wind. Shop fronts were decorated welcoming the motorbikes to town. And business owners braced themselves for one of their busiest weekends of the year, coming back to life after a seasonal winter hibernation.

Pino's Trattoria owner Rosa Scarlato, almost a MotoGP celebrity in her own right, is the race's number one ticketholder.

She was part of the local push to save the race earlier this year.

And as she rode onto the iconic circuit last Thursday for the Homecoming Ride, she shed a tear.

"It's a shame we've lost it," she said.

"Driving into the track this morning, I cried just a little bit, because we've got such a beautiful venue."

She said the loss would be felt by all islanders because people worked together and made it a "very successful weekend".

Marking the occasion

Newer residents to the island have readily embraced the electric atmosphere of island life during the MotoGP weekend.

Connor Cardus, who has lived in Cowes for five years, isn't a huge motoring fan.

But as a business owner in town, he admits to getting swept up in the atmosphere every time the bikes roll in.

He even marked the occasion this year with a MotoGP-inspired tattoo.

Connor Cardus and tattoo artist Jack Montgomery commemorating the final MotoGP on Phillip Island with some fresh ink. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

"It's amazing. There are so many people, and it's such an injection for local industries, and the money that comes through," he said.

"As a punter, going down to the local pubs and seeing all the businesses so busy after a quiet winter, it's amazing. It's really what we need, and it's going to be missed.

"Over the next few years, it's going to be very clear that we had a good thing, and we lost it."

Connor Cardus's tattoo marking the last MotoGP on Phillip Island. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

One last dance

Standing beside hundreds of idling motorcycles and feeling the road rumble beneath your feet as they pass you by, it's easy to understand why riders tolerate all conditions to see their heroes tear down Gardner Straight one final time.

But despite the delays, the cancellation of the race's grand finale, and an entire day spent sitting in the cold and the rain, motoring fans were treated to one last roar, as rider and fan alike bid farewell to one of the sport's most beloved tracks.

Wet weather plagued the final day of motor racing at the Phillip Island circuit. (ABC News: Madeleine Stuchbery)

World.title: Antonelli wins in US but must wait one more week for F1 world championship
World.content:
Kimi Antonelli will have to wait one more week to claim his maiden F1 drivers' championship, but the 20-year-old all but sealed the title with a near-flawless win from pole position at the United States Grand Prix.

The Mercedes ace, who needed to win on Monday morning (AEDT) to have a chance of sealing the title in Texas, was magnificent as his Mercedes team made sure he was on the correct tyre strategy to win his ninth grand prix of the season.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished fourth, and Mercedes' George Russell placed eighth, meaning they can mathematically still win a championship that is all but decided.

Kimi Antonelli beat Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen for the win. (Getty Images: Rudy Carezzevoli)

Antonelli leads Russell by 123 points, and Hamilton by 124 points, with a maximum of 125 points left to win from the final five rounds.

Antonelli had the perfect start from pole position to hold a comfortable lead over Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Red Bull and Ferrari elected for a two-stop strategy in Texas, bringing their drivers in early. But Mercedes did not react, believing the one-stop would be the fastest option.

It was the right call from the Mercedes team and allowed Antonelli to win the race by more than 13 seconds.

"It was a result we needed; the whole team deserve it so much," Antonelli said.

"It was perfect execution from strategy to make the one-stop [work]."

Verstappen and Leclerc pitted early, showing their hand that they were going for the two-stop strategy.

Mercedes held their nerve and kept Antonelli out, believing he would have enough pace at the end of the grand prix to hold off the fast-finishing duo who would be flying on track after their second stops.

But any hope of Verstappen and Leclerc making the final laps of the US Grand Prix exciting were thwarted by McLaren's Lando Norris, who surprisingly elected to stop just once but was fast enough to hold up Antonelli's challengers. Verstappen and Leclerc would pass Norris, who ultimately finished fifth, on lap 47 of 56, but did not have enough time to chase Antonelli.

Kimi Antonelli wins the United States Grand Prix, all but sealing the F1 drivers' championship. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Simon Galloway)

Antonelli will win the drivers' championship next week in Mexico City if he finishes ninth or higher, or Russell and Hamilton fail to win the race.

"We are very close, but we try to finish on a high and we try to clinch [the title] very soon," he said.

Leclerc, with fresher tyres, passed Verstappen for second place with five laps remaining.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, who started third, placed sixth.

Australian Oscar Piastri finished seventh, where he started, after being ordered by McLaren early to let a faster Norris overtake him.

Russell finished a disappointing eighth, copping a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage on the first lap.

New Zealand's Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) and Frenchman Pierre Gasly (Alpine) rounded out the points positions, finishing ninth and 10th respectively.

World.title: Kangaroos escape with World Cup win after Fiji threatens upset
World.content:
The Kangaroos have locked in their semifinal spot at the Rugby League World Cup, beating Fiji 36-22 after receiving an almighty scare in Brisbane.

Tom Trbojevic's second-half hat-trick helped Australia over the line after the Bati twice took the lead either side of half-time at Lang Park.

Fijian five-eighth Kurt Donoghoe was rightly named player of the match after laying on three tries and dictating terms for much of the game.

"I think we need more from everyone," Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters said after the game.

"We know we can play better but let's give Fiji a lot of credit. At times it seemed like we were getting on top and they pulled themselves back into the game."

Taane Milne's try gave Fiji an early lead. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

Despite coming into the game as 50-1 outsiders, making three early errors and conceding the first try of the night, Fiji hit back through Semi Valemei and Taane Milne to lead 10-6 after half an hour.

For the second straight game, Kevin Walters's side looked vulnerable in defence and struggled with their last-tackle options, but still led at half-time after some James Tedesco brilliance led to a try for Sam Walker on debut.

But again the Fijians hit back, with Valemei's second retaking the lead for the underdogs just after the break and Solomone Saukuru appearing to extend soon after, only for the bunker to rule a line-ball obstruction.

The Kangaroos immediately went up the other end and Tom Trbojevic dove in for his first of three straight tries to snuff out the Fijian challenge.

Valemei completed his hat-trick late on before Jacob Preston added Australia's sixth shortly before full-time to lock in their semifinal berth, playing a double-header with the similarly undefeated Jillaroos at the Sydney Football Stadium next Sunday.

Fiji will have a chance to push for a surprise final-four spot if it can pull off an upset win over New Zealand next week, which suddenly does not seem so far-fetched.

Tech.title: iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.

The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.

The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

Tech.title: Scott Walker’s The Drift will get under your skin
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like “The Monster Mash” and John Carpenter’s “Halloween Theme.” Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle, The Body, or Scott Walker’s The Drift.

This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci. He sings about 9/11, his stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide. Lyrically, it’s about as dark as an album gets.

But it’s the experimental backdrop that drives it all home.

At times, the record sounds more like the score to an Ari Aster film than anything that could be called pop music under even the most generous definitions. Seasick guitars in the verses of “Jesse” give way to dissonant strings that drone oppressively over the chorus. You can feel the low-bitrate MP3 noise that opens “Clara” in your jaw, which also allegedly features the sound of his percussionist punching a pig carcass as part of the rhythm track.

Songs stop on a dime, linger in uncomfortable silence, then erupt in bursts of mechanical noise. Animal bleating, foley work, and atonal orchestra sections grind against Walker’s warble. Nothing is ever quite in tune, and it can be challenging to get through the record in a single sitting if you’re not in a very particular mood. But sticking with it can be quite rewarding.

Some songs and performances are so beautiful they send shivers down your spine or give you goosebumps. Scott Walker’s The Drift is the opposite of that. You will still have an involuntary physical reaction, but it’s more shudders than shivers. It will make your skin crawl.

Scott Walker’s The Drift is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including YouTube Music, Apple Music, Qobuz, Deezer, and Spotify.

Tech.title: A YouTuber dissected an iPhone Duo and thinks he found the cause of crackgate
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Social media and the iPhone Duo subreddit are filled with reports of Apple’s foldable failing quickly and in spectacular fashion. Some users report having the phone for only a few hours before the hinge seems to catch on something, then audibly crack and break the screen. Tellingly, the cracks all seem to happen in the same place.

YouTuber CuriousHagi was able to reproduce the cracked screen during some durability testing of the iPhone Duo. Then he pulled it apart to try and find the culprit. What he found is that the Duo’s hinge is quite complex, consisting of a gear-like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges.

The piece that broke is one of the links in the middle of the phone that happens to be thinner than the links below or above it, and it snapped at a small notch where it would be weakest. He also found marks where the hinge met the support plate, indicating where it may have gotten caught.

Tech.title: Zen Browser is the Arc replacement I was looking for
Tech.content:
is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

I know many of you are mourning the loss of the Arc browser, and I get it. It felt like the first app in a long time to really offer a new approach to browser design. Atlassian bought the company last year and shifted its focus to developing Dia, its even more AI-focused browser. And soon enough, Arc will officially be no more, leaving dedicated users in a lurch. But I abandoned Arc quite some time ago for the Zen Browser and haven’t really missed it. If you’re willing to deal with some minor inconveniences, I think you’ll find Zen is the Arc replacement you’re looking for.

Zen unabashedly rips off all the best bits of Arc. Visually, they’re almost indistinguishable. It has the launcher-like pinned sites, tab bar on the left, siloed spaces, and mods that let you customize the browser’s UI to your liking. It takes the bits that made Arc’s interface feel fresh, then strips out everything that made it bloated and drove me into the arms of another.

Most notably, Zen is AI-free.

There’s no agent in a sidebar hounding me to let it handle tasks. I’m not worried about Zen training an LLM on my browsing activity. It’s just a web browser.

Zen prides itself on its privacy features: “Beautifully designed, privacy-focused, and packed with features. We care about your experience, not your data,” it proudly proclaims. Now, I’m no fool. I know that nothing I do on the internet is really private, but with Arc, it always felt like my data was an integral part of the business plan. That’s not the case with Zen. It’s a free and open-source project that relies on volunteers and donations.

In addition to Zen Mods that can do anything from tweak the look of an active tab to overhaul how PiP videos are handled, you can also install Firefox extensions. Yes, you can install Chrome extensions in Arc, but anecdotally, I’ve found that Zen handles extensions better. Both Zen and Arc are different enough from a UI perspective that not all extensions display properly, but Zen offers more workarounds.

Zen also just kind of lets me focus on the task at hand. Links open in “glance” view, which is a temporary pop-over tab, which is really great when you’re doing some window shopping or light research. If I want to open it in a proper tab, it’s just a click away. Zen also has a floating bar that pops up whenever you press Command+T or CTRL+T. From here you can launch a new tab, switch to an existing tab, perform a search from the search engine of your choice, and even trigger an extension.

Zen isn’t perfect. I love its clean UI and organizational features, but it can’t play DRM-protected video content right now. That means Netflix, Spotify, HBO, Disney+, and more do not work in Zen. The Zen Team is working to obtain a Widevine license from Google. In the meantime, I use Chrome when I want to watch a movie, which is fine. Zen is built on Firefox, and Firefox’s Web MIDI support is lacking. So I have to fire up Chrome semi-regularly anyway.

I also miss Arc’s Boosts in some cases, but I’ve learned to accept the web as it is. Zen implemented a similar Boost feature in May, but it’s not super obvious and, if there is an official, easily browsable repository of installable Boosts, I’ve yet to find it. Instead, you have to tweak individual sites’ appearance yourself.

If you tried Zen a long time ago and were turned off by its buggy early builds, rest assured it’s come a long way. Look, if you are all in on Arc’s AI features, Dia is probably more your speed. Personally, I always loved Arc’s interface, but never really dug the vibes. Zen just feels right.

Update October 25th: Added information about Zen’s implementation of Boosts.

Tech.title: This Switch 2 sequel accessory was a few millimeters away from being good
Tech.content:
is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

The Crkd Nitro Deck was a saving grace for the original Nintendo Switch. The slide-on $59.99 accessory brought Hall effect sticks to drift-plagued consoles — no need to open up your Joy-Con for a complicated repair. The Nitro Deck 2, made for both the original Switch and the larger Switch 2, continues the tradition of having better sticks than what Nintendo puts in even the newest Joy-Con (though these aren’t Hall effect or TMR). But it doesn’t feel as essential, and there’s one thing I really can’t stand about it.

It’s too difficult to use the Nitro Deck 2’s ABXY face buttons without the right stick getting in the way. The stick-to-button arrangement is a big step down from the original Nitro Deck (and especially bad compared with the symmetrical Steam Deck-like stick layout in the video output-ready Nitro Deck Plus). I’m surprised Crkd’s team thought this was an improvement. My patience with the run-based gameplay in Echo Weaver is already tested enough, and trying to quickly hammer inputs on the Deck 2 only adds to the frustration.

Your preference may differ, but I like having a little breathing room between the right stick and the face buttons. Some companies choose to space them out or, in the case of the Switch 2’s Joy-Con, make the stick small enough to allow my thumb to hover over it so I can press the buttons. The Deck 2 makes me adjust my thumb’s angle of approach outside of what’s comfortable. It’s just a few millimeters off.

The original’s superior slide-in design was traded for a vice-grip design to ensure compatibility with both the newer and older Switch consoles. The Deck 2 has a twisting mechanism on the back that you can loosen, tighten, or lock. It’s clever, though the tradeoff for broader compatibility is a design that feels inherently less secure. Crkd is asking Switch 2 owners to put a ton of faith in this mechanism staying tight around their $500 consoles. My Switch 2 didn’t feel wobbly during testing, but I’d rather not have to think about its safety at all when I’m gaming. I would have preferred a slide-in design for the Deck 2 made expressly for the Switch 2.

It’s disappointing that Crkd’s Joy-Con-replacing solution isn’t as good because I like some things about it more than the original. For instance, the accessory has adjustable tension on both sticks, so they can snap back to their original position faster or slower than the default speed. Also, the accessory’s bulkier design makes the console more comfortable in my medium-size hands to use in handheld mode. It also has a bunch of customizable buttons: four on its back and an extra near the triggers.

Not many similar accessories are out there yet, and the other one I tried (the abxylute N6) wasn’t all that good, either. I plan to test Mobapad’s latest take on Joy-Con soon, and it seems promising. Alternatively, you can add a bunch of comfort to your Switch 2 in handheld mode with either the Dbrand Killswitch 2 or the Mechanism Basecase. And with the money left over, you could buy a good wireless Switch 2 controller with long-lasting sticks and better rumble.
